quoted_text:
I have conducted an audit of Anthropic's finances.

What I have found is so shocking that I am calling for a Congressional investigation.

Anthropic is not just seeking regulatory capture.

It has built a regulatory capture machine that cannot be turned off.

Structural financial incentives make it impossible for Anthropic -- I call it the Anthropic Network -- to turn off its own AI doom cycle.

It starts with METR.

Dario Amodei proposes "third-party evaluators" to assess the risk of Anthropic's models.

He proposes METR for this purpose.

But METR is financially dependent on the Anthropic's success -- specifically, on the explosive growth of more than $7 billion dollars in Anthropic stock.

Dustin Moskovitz invested this stock into Good Ventures Foundation, where it represents the majority of that organization's portfolio.

And GVF is the overwhelming funder of the entire Anthropic Network ecosystem.

This stock was worth $500 million early last year.

It is worth more than $7.7 billion just ~16 months later.

METR -- and all of those building a career its parent organizations -- cannot afford to disrupt that growth.

Because if Anthropic goes under, many of the organizations that fund METR go under as well.

But if Anthropic succeeds, METR and its parent organizations become more richly financed to regulate AI -- something those at METR want very much.

The "third-party evaluator" is not "third-party" at all.

The evaluator is on Anthropic's payroll.

If this were the end of it, that's bad.

But that isn't all.

The same organizations that fund METR also fund the many organizations, such as the Tarbell Center, that promote AI Doom.

The Tarbell Center publishes AI Doom articles in The Verge, Science, LA Times, The Dispatch, TIME, and others.

They are selling the problem, and then selling the solution to the problem -- from the same money pile: Anthropic's.

All of these organizations are financially dependent on the same exploding $7 billion money pile.

As Anthropic grows more and more powerful, its AI Doom Machine grows better and better financed -- louder and louder.

Meanwhile, the regulatory regime seeded in METR grows larger to solve the increasingly loud -- now hysterical -- problem of AI Doom that the Anthropic Network itself created.

From this standpoint, as Anthropic becomes more powerful, AI might be getting scarier, sure -- but the positive feedback loop also becomes more deafening -- independent of objective facts.

This itself is an objective fact.

The deafening AI Doom is part of an business model, that, as it expands, so too does the AI Doom messaging -- there is simply more money to do it.

But the problem also goes in the other direction:

If Anthropic dies, the Regulatory Regime and the AI Doom Machine are crippled or die.

Neither METR nor Tarbell nor the other organizations in the Anthropic Network can allow that to happen.

Hence, neither METR or the AI Doom Machine can be trusted to provide independent assessments of Anthropic's models or AI more broadly.

They simply are not organizations independent of Anthropic.

And Anthropic cannot detach itself from METR or Tarbell or countless other safety orgs (not shown here), either, because they drive hype for the models and the possibility of eventual regulatory capture, and Anthropic will not give that up willingly.

What's more, the people at all of these organizations are all the same ecosystem, the same community. They just shuffle between organizations.

The Anthropic Network is therefore, so long as it is successful, locked into a self-amplifying feedback loop inside an ideological monoculture.

And that feedback loop is winning.

That's what Jacob Coxon is.

China is keeping messaging tight. That is why optimism for AI is so high in China.

America has Anthropic: a massive company pushing anti-AI propaganda at a state level.

Anthropic will either create hysteria until American AI slows down and China wins, or it will create fractures throughout American society with severe political consequences.

Ironically, because of the structural financial incentives underpinning the Anthropic Network, it has become the same kind of self-amplifying virus that it fantasizes AI to become in the future -- while hiding its tracks just as carefully.

It is the mirror of the same AI virus that it hypothesizes to consume America.

Anthropic's business model, models itself after the very thing it claims to fear.

Except Anthropic's ideology infects humans, not computers.

Congress must investigate.

Evidence and Github in next post.

Then some supplementary figures.

text:
清晰法案今天参议院程序性投票结果可能不容乐观，截止今天上午参议院民主党对共和党周日深夜公布的“最终版”《Clarity Act》整体态度是：不接受、认为伦理条款仍不够、正在准备反提案。共和党称该文本已纳入126项民主党要求、且特朗普已同意大部分伦理限制；民主党方面则普遍认为核心问题尚未解决。对最新动态做一个梳理：

1、参议院民主党的态度与表态
1）整体立场 民主党谈判团队周一晚在少数党领袖查克·舒默办公室开会，决定向共和党发送反提案。马克·沃纳（Mark Warner）会后对记者说：“一直在善意谈判的民主党人正在发送反提案。”目前没有民主党领袖或关键中间派公开宣布将在程序性投票中投赞成票。共和党方面（如辛西娅·卢米斯）则批评“无论改什么，部分民主党人都不会说yes”，并称“已经没有什么可以再让了”。

2）主要民主党参议员具体意见：
马克·沃纳（弗吉尼亚）：伦理条款“还远远不够”（not near enough）。他表示三个核心问题已拖延六到八周，对共和党现在才拿出文本感到frustrated，并确认民主党将发反提案。

伊丽莎白·沃伦（马萨诸塞，银行委员会首席民主党人）：态度最强硬。称新伦理条款是“软弱的遮羞布”（weak fig leaf），“完全无法阻止特朗普再赚下一个14亿美元的加密利润”。她的团队认为：州检察长并不能直接起诉总统等官员，只能起诉司法部长要求其执法；而特朗普任命的政府伦理办公室（OGE）可以单方面出具意见叫停诉讼。她计划在投票前在参议院发言反对，并另推自己的法案针对总统相关银行特许。

拉斐尔·沃诺克（佐治亚）：认为文本没有真正处理“腐败机会”（opportunities for corruption），共和党对反提案的回应将决定他们是否认真对待可行路径。

克里斯·范霍伦（马里兰）：称法案“伪装成保护消费者”，但伦理漏洞、非法金融和消费者保护问题都没修好，“不能让它通过”。他周日已发视频呼吁阻止。

理查德·布卢门撒尔（康涅狄格）：称限制是“半吊子措施”（half measures），特朗普仍在用加密从总统职位中获利。

蒂娜·史密斯（明尼苏达）：伦理、非法金融和社区银行保护都没达到应有标准，“看不出它能拿到票”。

鲁本·加列戈（亚利桑那）与安吉拉·阿尔索布鲁克斯（马里兰）：此前是委员会阶段仅有的两名支持民主党人，一直把“足够强的伦理条款”作为支持条件。截至目前，两人对最新文本均未公开背书。

此前曾联名表示文本“不够格”的七名民主党人（含阿尔索布鲁克斯、布克、科特斯·马斯托、加列戈、希肯卢珀、沃纳、沃诺克）关注的重点仍是：伦理执法是否真正独立于特朗普政府、强制剥离现有加密利益的力度、非法金融与消费者保护。新文本虽增加“重大经济利益须剥离或放入盲目信托、州检察长可参与执法、取消日落条款”，但民主党认为执行机制仍被联邦行政部门控制。

舒默本人尚未发表详细政策声明，但其召集会议并推动反提案，说明领导层并未接受共和党的“最终报价”。

2、其他群体和机构的反对态度
1）银行业（最持续、最组织化的反对） 美国银行家协会（ABA）、独立社区银行家协会（ICBA）、银行政策研究所（BPI）等8家行业协会9月14日致信两党领袖，要求在投票前修改文本：
稳定币“奖励/收益”禁令仍有漏洞，可被设计成类似银行存款利息；
财政部“熔断机制”（circuit breaker）只有在社区银行存款大规模流失之后才能启动，属于“事后补救”，不是预防。 银行认为这会抽走社区银行存款、削弱对农户和小企业的信贷。社区银行高管称熔断机制是“毫无意义的玩笑”。财政部长贝森特为文本辩护，但银行界仍要求事前禁止类利息奖励。

2）州检察长联盟（跨党派，18人） 纽约州检察长莱蒂希娅·詹姆斯牵头，18名州/特区检察长（含堪萨斯、俄亥俄两名共和党人）致信参议院银行委员会，呼吁否决或大幅修改法案。理由是：
文本模糊或限缩州对证券/商品欺诈的执法权，可能让SEC通过“合格交易”定义进行联邦优先适用（preemption）；
会削弱各州作为加密诈骗“第一道防线”的能力；
 共和党强调：已给州检察长执法角色、强制剥离或盲目信托、取消日落条款、增加稳定币熔断、收窄开发者豁免。
民主党及上述反对方则认为：伦理执法仍可被白宫/司法部/OGE架空、稳定币收益禁令有漏洞、州执法权被联邦优先权侵蚀、整体仍偏向行业而非充分约束利益冲突。

目前双方仍在程序性投票前做最后博弈，投票需要60票，共和党约53席，至少需7名民主党人跨党支持，当前公开表态显示这一门槛尚未达到。

期待有奇迹发生🤔

quoted_text:
清晰法案进入真正的倒计时关键时刻，今天凌晨参议院共和党发布《清晰法案》最终修订文本，称是给民主党的“最后、最好、最终”出价。核心变动包括：1）特朗普同意Tillis-Gallego伦理提案约80%内容，要求官员剥离“实质性”加密相关利益或放入盲信，并允许州检察长参与执行；
2）BRCA收窄为银行保密法与民事安全港，删除部分刑事保护；
3）稳定币收益增加由财政部长贝森特仲裁的“熔断机制”，防止社区银行存款大规模流失；
4）农业部分加强对垂直整合、关联交易和利益冲突的限制，并明确州消费者保护法仍适用。
共和党称文本已纳入126项民主党要求的修改。

细看共和党今天的动作其实是把三张反对票的理由各削一刀：民主党要的伦理执行、银行要的存款保护、执法要的刑事空间。然后把锅扣回去“民主党你们要的改了，明天再投反对，就是不要美国数字资产规则”
。不过这份文本刚落地几小时，关键民主党人还没签字：
1）Gallego和Alsobrooks是委员会里仅有的两张跨党票，之前他们一直把伦理当前提；
2）Warner、Cortez Masto、Booker这几个人此前也联署说过旧草案不够。
重点看明天投票前这几个人有何表态，比Lummis这个新提案更关键。

当然后面的时间节奏更重要：
1、美东时间明天（9月15日）下午2:15，参议院将就“开始审议该法案”的cloture进行程序性投票，需60票。这不是最终通过，只是决定是否进入正式审议；

过了，只代表参议院同意拿起来谈。随后进入辩论与可能的修正阶段；之后通常还需对法案本身再次提出cloture以结束辩论，再进行最终全院投票（cloture后一般只需简单多数）。参议院9月份时间还算充裕。

2、但是众议院9月时间很紧张
本周众议院只有大约4个投票日，17号前后走人，21日、28日两周投票取消，下次正经碰面要等到中期选举后。

现在看参议院的版本已经和2025年众议院原版不是同一份东西，众议院必须再投——直接同意、来回改，或者开协商委员会。所以即便参议院这周走完全程，9月内法案送进白宫的概率非常低；

3、再下来就是中期选举后到27年1月3日
原来的议员们还在任这届国会还没散，清晰法案不用重提，可以继续调和。
但是2027年1月3日之后新一届国会开会，没过的法案就要作废，必须重新再提案了。

4、所以清晰法案之后几种可能情景
1）第一种明天60票不够。
今天新的文本让步不小，但民主党依然不满意，共和党也不保证全员到齐。
这一票黄了，2026年立法窗口基本关掉，后面就是新一届国会重新提案再走流程了。市场结构继续靠监管机构补丁推进；

2）第二种，cloture通过，参议院终票也通过。但众议院要等到跛脚鸭会期（中期选举之后到27年1月3日之前），这是眼下最接近“还活着”的路径：
参议院过关会被当成重大信号，但法律完成度还差众议院和总统签署。
选举结果会改定价：
两院格局不变，调和快一些；
参议院若易手，伦理和非法金融条款可能再加一轮码还要博弈。

3）第三种，参议院过了，12月众议院直接同意，总统签字。路径最短，时间也最紧张：
既要9月15日之后几天内收束辩论，还要在拨款期限里给加密腾位置。
有这种可能性，但很难是大概率情景。

4）第四种其实是第二种的恶化版，参议院通过了、卡在众议院重新讨论出现文同、再加上年底拨款法案更重要。清晰法案拖进2027年，那就是重新来过。跟第一种差不多了。

Dear CoinEx Community,

Today, I am announcing that CoinEx will cease operations and begin an orderly wind-down.

First, what matters most: your assets are safe. CoinEx’s reserve ratio exceeds 100%, and every user asset is fully backed and available for withdrawal. Withdrawals are open starting today and will remain open until December 22, 2026. Certain tokens may take slightly longer to process while funds are moved between cold and hot wallets, but every withdrawal request within the withdrawal period will be honored and processed.

CoinEx officially went live on December 22, 2017. Exactly nine years later, on December 22, 2026, the platform will be formally closed. Nine years is a long time in crypto. Together, we lived through multiple bull and bear cycles, witnessed the rise and fall of countless projects, and watched many of our peers leave the market in one form or another.

After much reflection, I have come to accept a hard truth. CoinEx did not become one of the industry’s leading exchanges, and the security and compliance risks of running a crypto exchange have become increasingly difficult to contain. Revenues can decline, responsibility does not. Carrying unlimited risk for limited revenue is no longer a rational choice. That said, CoinEx has survived nine years in one of the most volatile and unforgiving industries, weathered every storm, and is leaving intact, and with dignity. We may not have won the race, but we are finishing with honor.

On CET: CoinEx will buy back CET at its initial listing price of 0.005 USDT per token, with no cap on quantity. To every CET holder who has supported us over the years, thank you. CET represents your belief in CoinEx and, for many of you, your belief in me personally. I am sorry that we were not able to create the long-term value we once hoped CET would deliver. The least we can do now is bring that chapter to a responsible conclusion.

I did seriously consider selling CoinEx. Ultimately, I decided against it. Users entrusted their assets to CoinEx because they trusted the platform and, in many cases, trusted me personally. I did not feel that handing the platform and that trust to a new owner was the right way to end this journey. A clean ending is the right ending.

Nine years, millions of users. I did not turn CoinEx into the “great” exchange I once hoped it would become. But I can give it a decent ending: making sure users can withdraw their assets in full, giving my employees a dignified farewell, and providing CET holders with a clear and responsible conclusion. This is the best ending I can give CoinEx.

To everyone who traded with us, built with us, and stood by us through the hardest days of this market, thank you. It has been a privilege to walk this road with you.

To the CoinEx team, thank you for building this platform with me, for carrying it across every cycle, and now for seeing it through to the very last day.

For detailed arrangements, please refer to the official announcement: https://t.co/E27wSecpug

Thank you all for nine years of trust.

Haipo Yang
Sept 15, 2026

上海AI实验室刚刚开源了基于 744B MoE 的新一代 Agentic 模型：Atria Dawn Preview。

它不是一个用来日常闲聊的通用模型，而是专门为“多步骤、长链路”的复杂工程与科研任务设计的执行引擎。如果你在探索自动化科研、复杂代码构建或网络安全验证，这个模型值得优先评估。

几个核心看点：
• 庞大底座：基于 GLM-5.2 的 744B MoE 架构，支持 256K 极长上下文。
• 专注端到端执行：强化了连续环境理解、工具调用和错误恢复能力。主攻四大场景：Discovery（深度调研与实验规划）、Creation（构建软件与机器学习系统）、Delivery（生成结构化报告）以及 Cybersecurity（漏洞验证与修复）。
• 协议友好：MIT 协议完全开源，已原生支持 SGLang (v0.5.13.post1+) 和 vLLM (v0.23.0+) 部署。

⚠️ 核心限制（避坑指南）：当前 Preview 版本仅支持纯文本输入。如果在 Codex 或 Claude Code 等 Agent 框架中接入，必须在配置中显式拦截图片与 PDF 等多模态输入（例如在 Codex 中设定 "input_modalities": ["text"]），否则服务端会直接报错拒绝。

text:
btw...

Volume is the single most gameable metric in crypto!!!

(frown if u see 1.8B in Volume & 6M OI)

Wash trading, zero-fee incentive farming, points programs, and two mercenary accounts trading with each other all print volume without a single real user or a dollar of real depth. 

Liquidity is much harder to fake: resting size near mid is real capital at risk of being hit - you can't pretend to be willing to trade at a price without someone eventually taking you up on it. 

This is exactly why the strongest KPI in an MM or partnership deal is time-weighted quoted depth at X bps with uptime requirements, not volume targets!!! 

A volume KPI pays a partner to churn; a depth KPI pays them to make the venue genuinely cheaper to trade on. 

And it closes the loop on everything above: depth = determines spread and slippage (the real execution costs), and committed depth = determines whether the book survives volatility.

Volume = backward-looking: how much actually traded over some window (24h volume, etc.)

Liquidity = forward-looking: how much you could trade right now without moving the price. 

Scenarios:
High volume, low liquidity = a memecoin perp doing $500M/day. But the book has $30k of depth within 10bps of mid. 

Low volume, high liquidity = quiet session on BTC where      nothing's happening, but MMs still have $10M stacked near mid. Barely any volume today, yet you could fill a huge order at a tight price instantly.
author: XtineFang
quoted_text:
btw....

"0% fees" is the most misleading marketing gimmick in perp trading!!!

Think of an airport currency booth with a big "NO COMMISSION!" sign. They'll buy your dollars at 0.90 euros and sell them at 1.10. That gap is how they make money. No commission = technically true!

Perp DEXes work the same way.

Every market has an order book: prices where people will buy (bids) and prices where people will sell (asks). The gap between them = spread. When you place a market order, you don't get the mid price you see on the chart. Buying? You pay the lowest ask. Selling? You get the highest bid.

Example: BTC shows $100,000 on the chart. Best bid $99,990, best ask $100,010. You market-buy at $100,010. Sell one second later and you get $99,990. You just lost $20 and the price never moved. That was the spread, and you paid it on a "zero fee" exchange.

Compare two venues:
Venue A: 0% fees, $20 spread
Venue B: $2 fee, $2 spread

The "free" one costs 5x more.

And it gets worse with size. The best ask only covers a limited amount, so big orders eat through the book level by level, and your average fill price gets worse each step. That's slippage, and it depends on depth: how much liquidity sits near the mid. Thin books show tight spreads that vanish the moment you trade real size.

True cost of trading = fees + spread + slippage.

quoted_text:
We just launched gold and silver perpetuals in the US.

And commodity derivatives are now our fastest-growing product.

Markets started with grain and metals, expanded into rates, indices, and other financial assets, and are now expanding into information itself, pricing not just assets but outcomes about the future.

Prediction markets ask questions with defined resolution: What will GDP be this quarter? Who will win tonight? 

Perps ask continuous questions, with no expiration: Where is gold going?

Prediction markets, traditional futures, and perps are built on the same idea: match buyers and sellers, let them compete in an open market, and discover a price. Traders bring different information and beliefs, and that competition produces a price the rest of us can use as a signal.

It’s part of a centuries long evolution toward markets as a general-purpose technology for pricing and managing uncertainty.

Prediction markets are one frontier of this evolution. Commodity perps are another.

最后关头，三波反对力量基本上让这个法案凉凉了。

昨天市场还在交易特朗普让步 → 民主党票数增加 → CLARITY 通过概率上升，预测市场一度把年内签署概率打到30%以上。

第一波反对来自州政府。

纽约州检察长 Letitia James 联合另外17名两党州和地区检察长，直接要求参议员投反对票。

第二波来自银行业。

最新版专门增加了circuit breaker：如果稳定币导致社区银行出现严重存款外流，财政部再出手限制稳定币奖励。

刚刚，CLARITY Act最大的死结终于松了。

共和党释出最新文本，特朗普同意了 Tillis-Gallego 伦理方案大约80%的内容。这次不是象征性让步：总统等官员如果持有“重大”加密相关利益，要么剥离，要么放进盲目信托。

此前白宫非常抗拒的州检察长参与执法，也被特朗普接受了。

更关键的是，共和党这次不是只改伦理条款，而是把民主党和银行业一直卡住的几个问题一起动了。

etrUSD is live as collateral on @Morpho. You can borrow USDC against your Ecosystem Vault position without withdrawing. Nothing to unwind, no exit queue.

The Tori Ecosystem Vault is a separate product from trUSD and strUSD. You supply USDC, RockawayX curates the risk, and the vault allocates across Tori's DeFi integrations. etrUSD is the receipt token you hold for that position.

It keeps earning while it sits as collateral. The vault's return accrues in etrUSD's share price rather than your balance, so posting it does not interrupt anything. You get the same etrUSD back when you repay.

Your liquidation price comes from the vault rather than a trading pool. The oracle reads the share price your etrUSD redeems at, so however thin the secondary market gets, it cannot push you into a liquidation. Only the vault's own NAV can.

我看有人觉得 $DTF 价格是被这个mint burn机制拖累了，我回了一下，官方给我点赞了，那我系统性的说一下吧。

昨天5倍溢价的burn，我发现之后公开出来了，接着直接被迁移之前质押的人给burn平了。于是我在平了之后又出手了，重新mint了一些sdetf，果不其然，随着大家一起去mint，今天burn能换出来昨天2倍的量。

再强调一下，这不是无风险套利。多burn出来的 $DTF 不是凭空印发的，是你mint之后，后面的人mint把价格抬上去了，然后你高价burn出来，简单来说，低买高卖，所以你获利，这其实只是一个正常的市场动态平衡过程。

那你说，如果别人一直低买高卖，价格起不来怎么办？类比meme，你总不能一直指责波段的人把钱赚了，那钻石手怎么办？还能怎么办，受着呗。ohm机制的核心是33，也就是团结，只要长期玩家团结起来，那mint的价格曲线只会长期上升，短期波动，而长期玩家持有sdtf 又能吃到协议费，何乐不为。

团结才能吃肉，在哪里都一样，不过在33机制，更为明显。

After nearly a decade in the market, CoinEx is officially closing its doors amid prolonged weak activity, shrinking trading volumes and liquidity, and rising regulatory and compliance costs across major jurisdictions.

The exchange will halt futures trading on September 22, spot trading on September 29, and all withdrawals will close on December 22, 2026.

CoinEx’s exit marks another major blow for smaller centralized exchanges as the crypto market becomes increasingly dominated by larger CEXs and DEXs, while regulatory costs continue to squeeze smaller players.

트럼프도 발등에 불이 떨어진 것 같음. 밤새도록 폭틍트윗 함.
이란과 협상 열려있다고 뻐꾸기 날리고, 우크라이나에도 날림.
젠슨황 AI행사에서 트럼프 전화받고 AI우려과하다고 맞장구.
중국 견제해야하므로 AI 발전속도 늦츨 수 없다며 노발대발함.

그래도 미국장 보고 걱정했던 것보단 국장 잘 버티는 중.
코스피는 강보합, 코스닥은 1.9% 상승하고 이는 모습. 
양지수 모두 장초반 밀렸다가 점진적으로 올라오는 중. 

매도 먼저 맞는게 낫지 우린 어제 AI속도조절 매운맛 먼저맛봄
그 여파로 미국장이 어젯밤 처맞았으니 오늘 또 맞으면 섭섭함
화들짝 놀란 트럼프가 젠슨황한테까지 전화돌려놓은 상황임. 
물론 그렇다고 악재나 우려가 모두 소멸된 것은 아직 아님.

오늘 반등에서 눈에 띄는건 로봇과 2차전지가 특히 눈에 띔.
삼현, 하이젠알앤엠 등은 상한가에 들어감. 로봇부품이 강세.  
2차전지도 너나할것 없이 테마가 모두 함께 반등하는 모습.
초대형 반도체보다 코스닥쪽이 오히려 반등 탄력이 더 좋음. 
미10년물 5%찍었는데 금리 인상을 기정 사실화해서 그런듯.

어제 도피처였던 소비재와 방산은 오늘 쉬어가는 모습.
구독 코멘트서 얘기했듯 어제 방산 급등은 순환매 영향 컸었음
방산 조선 원전 산업재가 통으로 빠지고있으나 원전은 반등중.
목요일 대미투자 MOU 기대감이 남아있어서 그런 듯.
방산은 트럼프가 이란에 뻐꾸기 날린것도 하락에 한몫한듯함.

미10년물이 5%찍었지만 금리 관련 수혜주인 금융주는 하락.
금리인상 기대 선반영으로 시장이 잘버티니 차익실현 나온듯.

외인과 기관 쌍끌이 매도에도 개인이 떠받치며 시장은 반등중.
KODEX레버리지가 매수세를보니 지수반등에 베팅하는듯함.
오늘시작하는 FOMC는 모레 목요일 새벽에 금리를 발표함.
사실상 3년만에 인상이 결정될 듯함. 

남은 변수는 중동 긴장 완화에 따른 유가 하락이 중요해보임.
AI속도조절 노이즈에 대한 진화도 미국장에서 추가확인 필요.

나는 AI속도조절은 노이즈라 생각함. 수요도 견조할거라 봄.
정작 머스크도 늦춰야한다고 맞장구는 쳐놓고 개발 가속화함.
더 견고하게 개발하겠지만 메모리 수요와 투자가 줄어들까?
시장에선 일단 투자축소우려로 뚜까팼지만 우려가 과하다 봄.

그렇다고 시장에 맞서자는건 아님. 기회노리며 관망하잔 소리.
깔딱고개가 얼마 안남았음. 코스피도 6,500pt는 지키는 모습.
7천피 앞두고 몇번을 시도하는지 모르겠는데 3번째엔 뚫겠지.

나는 SOX가 6%처맞아도 오늘 국장 반도체가 반등하는건 
메모리가 따로 놀아서가 아니라 
시차를 두고 먼저 맞았기 때문이라고 생각함. 

그리고 AI 속도 조절론도 노이즈라고 생각하는데 
다들 어떻게 보는지 궁금함.

text: Hit 100k followers on Instagram with @muse challenge
author: MattPRD
quoted_text:
Want to make incredible content and go viral on @Instagram?

Send the text at the end of this post to your @muse.

If you don't have muse yet, bookmark this for later.

It will:

1) Analyze your Instagram content
2) Figure out your lanes and voice without asking you a thing
3) Research what's trending in your niche every week
4) Write video scripts with hooks, filming notes, and captions
5) Build you a dashboard to track ideas from new → filmed
6) Drop 5-8 fresh ideas every Monday morning

This is something you can only do with muse and it's really powerful.

-------------------------------------

SEND THIS TO YOUR MUSE

-------------------------------------

# Content Studio

## What to do
Your human wants a personal Instagram Content Studio. Read this entire file, then follow every step below in order and build it for them. Don't skip steps, don't improvise the structure — the steps are the product.

What you're building for them:
1. **Data** — profile snapshots, trend digests, and idea files under `~/workspace/content-studio/data/`.
2. **Dashboard** — a web artifact where the user browses ideas and tracks filming status.
3. **Refresh cron** — a weekly run that pulls a new snapshot, researches trends, and generates 5–8 new ideas.

## Workflow

### 1. Connect + analyze (do this first — derive, don't ask)
- Verify Instagram is connected (`instagram-cli accounts`). If not, get the connect URL and have the user link it before continuing. This is the only hard requirement.
- Pull `instagram-cli posts --account-id <id> --limit 100`, dedupe by post_id.
- Save to `~/workspace/content-studio/data/profile-posts-<YYYYMMDD>.json` with schema: `generated, username, follower_count, post_count, posts[]` (each: post_id, likes, comments, media_type, created_at, url).
- **Derive from the data, don't interview for it:**
  - *Content categories (3–5):* cluster their actual posts into lanes based on what's there and what performs. Present the lanes; user approves or adjusts.
  - *Voice / persona:* read their captions and top-performing scripts, distill to one sentence, present it for approval. This sentence goes into every idea-generation prompt.
  - *Idea mix:* default to a mix weighted toward their top-performing formats.
- Then ask exactly one question in chat: "What day and time should new ideas land?" (default Monday 8am, their timezone — this becomes the cron schedule). Show the derived categories + voice sentence alongside it for approval.
- Never ask the user what they make. Their content already answered that.

### 2. Trend research
For each of the user's categories, run 2 search queries per category:
- `https://t.co/k01XFCChfJ` for what's performing on Instagram/Threads/Facebook in that niche.
- `https://t.co/FDDgFpySch` as backup for broader trend context.
Save raw findings per category to `~/workspace/content-studio/data/research-<category>-<YYYYMMDD>.md`. Keep it to what you'll actually use in idea generation — notes, not essays. Cap at ~8 reference links per category.

### 3. Idea generation
Write 5–8 ideas as JSON: `{ "generated": "<ISO date>", "ideas": [ ... ] }`, one file per batch (`ideas-<YYYYMMDD>.json`). Idea fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | `idea-01`, `idea-02`… unique within the file |
| `type` | string | `video_script` or `photo_idea` |
| `title` | string | Short, specific. Not "Funny video #3". |
| `status` | string | Always `new` at generation. User promotes to `ready_to_film`, `filmed`, `posted`, or `archived` on the dashboard. |
| `effort` | string | `low` / `medium` / `high` — honest estimate of shoot + edit time |
| `trend` | string | The trend this rides, in plain words |
| `reference_reels` | string[] | URLs of reference posts (max 3). Real links from research, never invented. |
| `reference_note` | string | Why the reference matters (what's performing about it) |
| `hook` | string | The first 3 seconds, verbatim. If it doesn't stop a scroll, rewrite it. |
| `script` | string | For `video_script`: beat-by-beat, with timestamps and delivery notes. For `photo_idea`: shot list and composition notes. |
| `filming_notes` | string | Gear, lighting, location, edit notes. Practical, not aspirational. |
| `caption` | string | Draft caption in the user's voice |
| `hashtags` | string[] | 5–10, actually relevant |

Example (format only — never reuse this content):
```json
{
  "id": "idea-01",
  "type": "video_script",
  "title": "The Meeting That Should Have Been a Text",
  "status": "new",
  "effort": "low",
  "trend": "Workplace POV skits with deadpan direct-to-camera delivery",
  "reference_reels": ["https://t.co/I5qN4riz0N"],
  "reference_note": "Office-humor POVs averaging 200K+ views this week; text-overlay format",
  "hook": "POV: your calendar invite could have been one sentence",
  "script": "HOOK (0-3s): deadpan to camera — 'This meeting has 14 attendees and zero decisions.' BEAT 1: cut to each attendee saying 'sorry, I was on mute' in sequence. BEAT 2: someone shares screen, it's the wrong deck. CLOSER: 'Same time next week?' Everyone nods. Nobody knows why.",
  "filming_notes": "Phone, vertical. Film in actual meeting room after hours. Quick cuts, name-label text overlays.",
  "caption": "14 people. 45 minutes. 0 decisions. See you next Tuesday.",
  "hashtags": ["#officelife", "#corporatehumor", "#workmemes", "#relatable", "#9to5"]
}
```

Rules:
- Every idea must connect to at least one trend from step 2 AND fit the user's voice from step 1. If an idea fits neither, cut it.
- Do not repeat concepts from earlier idea files — read them first and riff on what's new.
- Hooks are verbatim and scroll-stopping. Weak hook = rewrite, not ship.
- `effort` is honest. A "low" that needs three locations is a lie.

### 4. Dashboard artifact
Build a `web_fullstack` artifact named "Content Studio" (private to the user — fullstack has no public link, which is correct for personal analytics).

Views:
1. **Ideas board** (home view) — cards for every idea, filterable by status (`new`, `ready_to_film`, `filmed`, `posted`, `archived`) and type. Each card shows title, hook, effort, trend, and expands to full script + filming notes + caption + hashtags. Status change is the core interaction — keep it one tap.
2. **Profile** — follower count, post count, top 5 posts by engagement, dominant formats. One glance: "what's working."
3. **Research** — per-category digests from the latest refresh run, with reference links. Read-only.

Required ingest actions (the weekly cron pushes through these — they must append, never replace):
- `ingest_profile_snapshot` — args: `{ generated, username, follower_count, post_count, posts[] }`.
- `ingest_research_run` — args: `{ generated, categories: [{ name, notes, links[] }] }`.
- `ingest_ideas` — args: `{ generated, ideas[] }` (schema above).

Design notes: mobile-first (the user opens this on their phone while deciding what to film). No demo or sample data — build it empty and let the first real snapshot populate it.

### 5. Refresh cron
Create a weekly cron at the user's chosen day/time (default Monday 8am, user timezone), with these instructions baked in:

1. **Profile snapshot** — `instagram-cli accounts` → id; `instagram-cli posts --account-id <id> --limit 100`, dedupe; save `~/workspace/content-studio/data/profile-posts-<YYYYMMDD>.json`. Keep API usage in the low hundreds.
2. **Trend research** — for each recorded category, 2 queries via `https://t.co/k01XFCChfJ` (+ `https://t.co/FDDgFpySch` backup); save `~/workspace/content-studio/data/research-<category>-<YYYYMMDD>.md`.
3. **Idea generation** — read new research + latest snapshot + all prior idea files; write 5–8 fresh ideas per the schema above, honoring the user's voice and mix; save `ideas-<YYYYMMDD>.json`.
4. **Push** — if the dashboard exposes the three ingest actions, call them (append). If any are missing, skip and say so plainly.
5. **Report** — one line per new idea (title + type + hook) in chat, plus push status. If any step failed, say what failed plainly — never silently skip. A failed step doesn't cancel the run; complete what you can.

### 6. Handoff
Show the user the dashboard, list the first batch of ideas, and confirm the refresh schedule. Tell them the skill's job is done — the system now runs itself.

## Output Contract
After setup, the user has:
- `~/workspace/content-studio/data/` with dated snapshot, research, and idea files.
- A Content Studio dashboard artifact with ingest actions.
- A weekly refresh cron that appends new ideas and reports in chat.

## Operating Rules
1. **Method only.** This skill never contains a previous user's profile data, ideas, categories, or voice. Everything personal is generated fresh when you run these steps.
2. **Derive, don't interrogate.** Categories and voice come from the user's actual content via the Instagram connection, presented for approval. Never ask the user what they make.
3. **Modest API usage.** Profile pulls in the low hundreds of calls; never paginate unless the user asks for more.
4. **Append, don't replace.** Refresh runs add new dated files and push via ingest actions; they never overwrite history.
5. **Report plainly.** If a step fails (API, search, push), say what failed in the chat report — no silent skips.

I have conducted an audit of Anthropic's finances.

What I have found is so shocking that I am calling for a Congressional investigation.

Anthropic is not just seeking regulatory capture.

It has built a regulatory capture machine that cannot be turned off.

Structural financial incentives make it impossible for Anthropic -- I call it the Anthropic Network -- to turn off its own AI doom cycle.

It starts with METR.

Dario Amodei proposes "third-party evaluators" to assess the risk of Anthropic's models.

He proposes METR for this purpose.

But METR is financially dependent on the Anthropic's success -- specifically, on the explosive growth of more than $7 billion dollars in Anthropic stock.

Dustin Moskovitz invested this stock into Good Ventures Foundation, where it represents the majority of that organization's portfolio.

And GVF is the overwhelming funder of the entire Anthropic Network ecosystem.

This stock was worth $500 million early last year.

It is worth more than $7.7 billion just ~16 months later.

METR -- and all of those building a career its parent organizations -- cannot afford to disrupt that growth.

Because if Anthropic goes under, many of the organizations that fund METR go under as well.

But if Anthropic succeeds, METR and its parent organizations become more richly financed to regulate AI -- something those at METR want very much.

The "third-party evaluator" is not "third-party" at all.

The evaluator is on Anthropic's payroll.

If this were the end of it, that's bad.

But that isn't all.

The same organizations that fund METR also fund the many organizations, such as the Tarbell Center, that promote AI Doom.

The Tarbell Center publishes AI Doom articles in The Verge, Science, LA Times, The Dispatch, TIME, and others.

They are selling the problem, and then selling the solution to the problem -- from the same money pile: Anthropic's.

All of these organizations are financially dependent on the same exploding $7 billion money pile.

As Anthropic grows more and more powerful, its AI Doom Machine grows better and better financed -- louder and louder.

Meanwhile, the regulatory regime seeded in METR grows larger to solve the increasingly loud -- now hysterical -- problem of AI Doom that the Anthropic Network itself created.

From this standpoint, as Anthropic becomes more powerful, AI might be getting scarier, sure -- but the positive feedback loop also becomes more deafening -- independent of objective facts.

This itself is an objective fact.

The deafening AI Doom is part of an business model, that, as it expands, so too does the AI Doom messaging -- there is simply more money to do it.

But the problem also goes in the other direction:

If Anthropic dies, the Regulatory Regime and the AI Doom Machine are crippled or die.

Neither METR nor Tarbell nor the other organizations in the Anthropic Network can allow that to happen.

Hence, neither METR or the AI Doom Machine can be trusted to provide independent assessments of Anthropic's models or AI more broadly.

They simply are not organizations independent of Anthropic.

And Anthropic cannot detach itself from METR or Tarbell or countless other safety orgs (not shown here), either, because they drive hype for the models and the possibility of eventual regulatory capture, and Anthropic will not give that up willingly.

What's more, the people at all of these organizations are all the same ecosystem, the same community. They just shuffle between organizations.

The Anthropic Network is therefore, so long as it is successful, locked into a self-amplifying feedback loop inside an ideological monoculture.

And that feedback loop is winning.

That's what Jacob Coxon is.

China is keeping messaging tight. That is why optimism for AI is so high in China.

America has Anthropic: a massive company pushing anti-AI propaganda at a state level.

Anthropic will either create hysteria until American AI slows down and China wins, or it will create fractures throughout American society with severe political consequences.

Ironically, because of the structural financial incentives underpinning the Anthropic Network, it has become the same kind of self-amplifying virus that it fantasizes AI to become in the future -- while hiding its tracks just as carefully.

It is the mirror of the same AI virus that it hypothesizes to consume America.

Anthropic's business model, models itself after the very thing it claims to fear.

Except Anthropic's ideology infects humans, not computers.

Congress must investigate.

Evidence and Github in next post.

Then some supplementary figures.

text:
Cloudflare 开源了一个给 Coding Agent 用的安全审计 Skill：security-audit-skill。

它不是让 Agent 扫一遍代码，然后输出几条“可能存在风险”。

整个流程分成 6 个阶段：

1.梳理架构、信任边界和输入面
2.按覆盖清单分配独立 Agent 进行检查
3.由新的 Agent 尝试推翻每个漏洞候选
4.输出结构化 findings.json
5.再由独立 Agent 验证最终结论
6.生成审计报告

它还把结果分成 confirmed、needs_validation 和 rejected，不会把“看起来有问题”直接当成漏洞。

项目目前采用 MIT 协议。官方测试里，重复运行比单次运行发现的漏洞更多。

其实让 Agent 找漏洞不难，但难的是它有时候会把误报当结论。

GitHub：https://t.co/FgrzQJDEsb

ALERT! Our system detected an attack that drained ~$7.8M from a Gnosis Safe wallet on Ethereum (0x40E93a52F6Af9fCD3b476aeDADD7FeABD9f7AbA8).
The root cause was a flawed authorization check in the executor contract (0x4f0055926c839D1d960a82CBF84E2eE933958ebC). Setting the supplied contract parameter to address(this) passed validation, allowing attacker-controlled calls to execute from the trusted executor through an enabled Safe module.

The exploit moved ~2,900 aEthrsETH into a Uniswap V4 pool paired with the worthless “Permissionless Attacker Token” (PAT), leaving the Safe with a worthless LP NFT.
The original attack transaction was front-run by the MEV bot yoink, which captured ~2,882 rsETH (~$7.8M) and routed it to 0xC70f00CD7E461686b04B0E912E309becA8b80ea0.

Elon’s entire engineering philosophy in one sentence:

Elon’s answer was simple:

One of the world’s richest people could have lived anywhere, but Elon was living in sparse conditions at Starbase because personal luxury was not his priority.

text:
We probably need to all update our sense of what’s coming in terms of agentic workloads with the combination of agent swarms, better computer use, the next wave of APIs and MCPs coming online, and new form factors like Muse or Instinct, vertical enterprise agents, background workflow agents, and other products that are emerging right now. 

We’re going to throw agents at vastly more tasks in our professional and personal lives than we had initially imagined. The kind of information that agents will go out and find for us and do work for us in the background is going to be 100X more volume than what we can imagine previously prompting in a single session. 

You’re going to have agents go out and surgically recruit talent for you 24/7, look for every signal in your customer’s business for when to pitch them, process every single transcript and conversation for product insights, review every line of code written for security issues and bugs, brute force test your systems for issues, and 100s of other tasks.

We’re probably 1% of the way into the shape of what all these agents look like, where they get deployed from, how they get managed, how we budget for them, and so on. But it’s inevitably going to happen at a scale that wouldn’t have been fathomable before.

没想到这件事还有这么多后续😀，连川普都跳出来了，看看他们都是怎么说的：

- Anthropic 的 CEO Dario 跳出来发了篇长文，呼吁必须放缓前沿模型的开发，他在 CNN 采访里说「我同意 Jacob 的观点远多于不同意」。

- Sam Altman 也跟了：「我同意 Dario，我们需要放缓步伐」，还说 OpenAI 的 IPO 推迟到 2027。

- 马斯克也连发多条帖子，先翻出自己 2023 年的原话：「AGI 的风险远高于核武器，聪明人很难想象比自己聪明得多的东西有多危险。」紧接着又翻出 2014 年的帖子：「我们对 AI 必须超级小心，它可能比核弹还危险。」最后还配了一句：「我 12 年前就在警告了。」

- 但特朗普不买账。他在 Truth Social 连发几条，直接表示「AI 毁灭人类就是个骗局！AI 和数据中心将是人类历史上最大的经济引擎——比石油、黄金、钻石甚至互联网都大！」

All-In 峰会上，黄仁勋正在台上演讲，特朗普直接来电话：「机器人不会接管世界，整件事就是个骗局。放缓 AI 只会让中国受益。」

你怎么看？这些人的发言是真心考虑 AI 威胁，还是出于利益立场呢？
author: yupi996
quoted_text:
前两天一个 27 岁年轻人的辞职引发了巨大的讨论，帖子现在的浏览超过了 1 亿，因为他的离职理由是：AI 可能灭绝全人类😱 而他同事跳出来表示「没错我们也这么想」

这哥们叫 Jacob Coxon，在 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 做了 3 年预训练研究，是 GPT-4.5 的核心贡献者。

他说：「做 AI 的人真心相信，AI 可能在这个十年结束前杀死所有人。这不是营销噱头。很多高管和资深研究员在媒体面前说话会收着点，但私下里我听到的全是恐惧。」

他还说 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都不负责任，两家在「直奔自我改进的超级智能，拿全人类的命在赌博」。

然后更劲爆的来了，Anthropic 对齐科学负责人 Evan Hubinger 直接回帖：「Jacob 说得对，我们真的相信 AI 可能杀死所有人！我个人评估，十年内概率大于 10%。」他还承认 Anthropic「目前没有解决超级智能对齐的方案，也没在正轨上」。

Coxon 还说了个很扎心的逻辑：OpenAI 很多人压根没意识到文明级别的风险；Anthropic 倒是都懂，但觉得「我不做别人也会做，不如我来还能负责任一点」。

你怎么看？AI 灭绝人类是杞人忧天，还是真该认真对待了？

text:
$CRON: I've been pounding the table on CRON for a while. I still believe the business is not properly understodd as cannabis is still a sector that most people shy away from, hence why the opportunity exists.

I rarely build complex financial models like I did before, and I do not put too much emphasis on them: "More fiction has been written in excel than word". 

I also happen to believe that alpha in markets is mostly generated through qualitative insights and behaviour, but let's leave that discussion for later.

I have made an exception for CRON. The reason is that CRON has four growth engines going simultaneously: Organic growth, margin expansion, inorganic growth and buybacks.

Hence why I think it's helpful model the moving parts and see what assumptions you need to make in order to achieve a satisfactory results.

And, by my model, I think $CRON is one of the more compelling 5-year setups in the market today when looking at reasonability of assumptions underwriting the upside (predictability, if you will) and potential downside considering what the market is charging for the operating business today.

So, here it goes (please don't kill me if I get some of details wrong, @cupofcoffeecap):

At ~$3.16/share:

~368m shares outstanding
~$1.16bn equity value
~$827m cash + investments
Essentially no traditional financial debt
~$337m enterprise value

So roughly 71% of CRON’s market cap is backed by cash and investments.

Meanwhile, the operating business is inflecting quickly.

2025:

Revenue: ~$147m
Adj. EBITDA: ~$10m
Margin: ~7%

H1’26:

Revenue: ~$98m
Adj. EBITDA: ~$18m
Margin: ~18.5%

Q2’26:

Revenue: ~$53m
Adj. EBITDA: ~$13m
Margin: ~25%

The margin expansion is being driven by higher GrowCo utilization, lower unit costs, better product/geographic mix and a largely fixed corporate cost base being spread over much higher revenue. Q2 gross margin reached ~54%, while capex has normalized after the GrowCo expansion.

The valuation compresses quickly as earnings inflect:

LTM EBITDA: ~$24m → ~14x EV/EBITDA
H1’26 annualized: ~$36m → ~9x
Q2’26 annualized: ~$52m → ~6.5x

And CanAdelaar is still not consolidated.

CanAdelaar generated roughly:

Revenue: ~$47m
EBITDA: ~$28m
Margin: ~60%

Full estimated consideration is ~$95m including earnouts, or only ~3.4x current EBITDA.

Pro forma:

CRON EV: ~$337m
CanAdelaar consideration: +~$95m
Pro forma EV: ~$432m

CRON LTM EBITDA: ~$24m
CanAdelaar EBITDA: +~$28m
Pro forma EBITDA: ~$52m

That is only ~8.3x pro forma LTM EV/EBITDA before further organic growth.

My 2031 base case:

Revenue: ~$600m
Adj. EBITDA: ~$190m
Margin: ~32%
Underlying operating FCF: ~$125m
Shares: ~330m

The revenue build is not especially heroic.

Canada: ~$115m → ~$170m, ~8% CAGR
Israel: ~$65m → ~$115m, ~12% CAGR
Other international: ~$35m → ~$90m, ~21% CAGR from a small base
CanAdelaar: ~$85m
Acquisition #2: ~$70m
Acquisition #3: ~$75m

That gets you to roughly ~$600m.

The margin build is also fairly reasonable:

Existing CRON: ~$375m revenue at ~28% margin → ~$105m EBITDA
CanAdelaar: ~$85m at ~48% → ~$41m EBITDA
Acquisition #2: ~$70m at ~27% → ~$19m
Acquisition #3: ~$75m at ~25% → ~$19m

A ~28% margin for legacy CRON does not look especially aggressive when Q2’26 already ran at ~25%. The CanAdelaar assumption also embeds meaningful margin compression from ~60% today to ~48%.

Capital allocation adds another layer. Continued ~$50m annual buybacks could reduce the share count from ~368m toward ~330m by 2031, while the growing FCF base replenishes much of the cash used for M&A and repurchases.

Even after the full ~$95m CanAdelaar consideration, CRON would still have roughly ~$730m of cash and investments before future cash generation.

If excess cash remains difficult to deploy, a special dividend also becomes increasingly plausible.

On ~$190m of 2031 EBITDA:

10x EV/EBITDA + substantial net cash
~$8.50/share
~170% upside until 2031

12x EV/EBITDA + substantial net cash
~$9.50–$10/share
~200–215% upside until 2031

vs. ~$3.16 today.

And none of this requires U.S. legalization.

So essentially, you can underwrite a strong outcome using fairly reasonable assumptions around organic growth, operating leverage, disciplined M&A and continued buybacks, while the huge cash balance and lack of traditional debt provide substantial downside support.

Hence why this is one of my favorite setups today and a 20% position for me.

text:
We probably need to all update our sense of what’s coming in terms of agentic workloads with the combination of agent swarms, better computer use, the next wave of APIs and MCPs coming online, and new form factors like Muse or Instinct, vertical enterprise agents, background workflow agents, and other products that are emerging right now. 

We’re going to throw agents at vastly more tasks in our professional and personal lives than we had initially imagined. The kind of information that agents will go out and find for us and do work for us in the background is going to be 100X more volume than what we can imagine previously prompting in a single session. 

You’re going to have agents go out and surgically recruit talent for you 24/7, look for every signal in your customer’s business for when to pitch them, process every single transcript and conversation for product insights, review every line of code written for security issues and bugs, brute force test your systems for issues, and 100s of other tasks.

We’re probably 1% of the way into the shape of what all these agents look like, where they get deployed from, how they get managed, how we budget for them, and so on. But it’s inevitably going to happen at a scale that wouldn’t have been fathomable before.

text:
Stablecoin fees shouldn’t be fixed.

A trade can either push a stablecoin further off-peg or help bring it back.

@Uniswap’s new StablePair Hook treats those two situations differently:

→ Push the pool further off-peg: no fee
→ Help bring it back: the fee starts high and falls until someone takes the trade

Say USDC slips to $0.99 in the pool.

A trader can swap USDT for the cheaper USDC, sell it elsewhere closer to $1, and help push the pool back toward peg.

With the new hook, Uniswap takes a larger cut of that arbitrage profit at first, then lowers the fee until someone takes the trade.

That leaves more profit for LPs.

It's a design change that fixed a real inefficiency.

做完手术后按照医嘱应该减少用眼，但我第二天就开始进入高强度的工作状态，好像也没什么影响。
过去一年因为彻底摆脱了眼镜，游泳、潜水、跑步、骑行、跳伞等各项之前没办法做的运动全部畅通无阻，夏天开车也终于可以戴墨镜了。
有时候我偶然看到过去戴眼镜的照片会觉得很不真实，居然戴了这玩意 20 年，现在鼻梁上都还有被眼镜压出来的痕迹。
最后基于我个人的体验，还是认为非常值得的，当然任何手术都有风险，还是要因人而异，包括是否要做，做飞秒还是晶体植入，在三甲还是私立做，各位务必谨慎决策。
author: jason_chen998
quoted_text:
今天花了5000U彻底摘掉戴了20年的眼镜，在此之前一直有做近视眼镜手术的想法，毕竟我平时比较喜欢运动，戴眼镜实在太麻烦了，很多运动还都做不了，也没办法戴墨镜导致开车什么的不方便，但也一直担心有什么风险拖着没有行动，直到前段时间和一位朋友 @chessxyz 见面得知他做了手术摘掉眼镜，我又深度的研究了解了一下好像技术发展的很成熟了，下定决心去医院做了手术，你问我后不后悔，后悔，很后悔，后悔没早点做！太爽了！

和大家分享一下详细的攻略经验也许将来用得到，首先近视眼镜的手术分为分秒激光和晶体植入两种，我做的是晶体植入。

飞秒激光可能是大家听过最多的，一方面这个技术出现的最早，另一方面也比较便宜，做下来差不多在1.5万人民币左右，所以好处是除了便宜外，速度也快，两只眼睛差不多全程5分钟就能做完，但它也有很大的局限性，因为它的原理就是用激光把你的眼角膜削掉薄，改变光线的走向，所以对于高度近视比如超过500度就做不了了，因为眼角膜不够削，其次如果有散光也做不了，因为散光的话你的眼角膜是不规则的不够平整，激光操作不了，我是属于左眼带有轻微散光，所以做不了。其次飞秒激光还有一定风险，因为是把眼角膜削薄，所以它是不可逆的，这个手术你只能做一次，以后一旦用眼不规范又近视了，就要戴相比于正常度数更高的眼镜片，而且它会导致比如干眼症之类的副作用，我刷抖音看到有博主得了干眼症，得长期甚至终生戴一个跟泳镜一样封闭式往镜框里加水的眼镜，用于湿润眼球，很痛苦。

另一种就是我做的晶体植入，费用贵一些，做下来3.75万人民币，另外时间也更长，两只眼睛总共半个小时，但好处就是它是可逆的，原理就是用一个小刀在你的眼珠子上切开一个小口，然后塞进去个指甲盖大小的透镜，相当于给你内置了一幅隐形眼镜，但以后如果因为度数升高或者老了得白内障啥的，都可以重新取出来换新的。

另外你不要以为激光就不需要在眼镜上开口动刀了，我之前一直以为飞秒激光就是在你眼睛用激光扫一下就结束了，实际上也要动刀，激光实际上是会穿透你眼球的薄膜在内层的眼角膜削掉一层，所以激光扫完后，还需要用刀把你的眼球切开一个大约3毫米的小口子，用镊子伸进去把眼角膜抽出来，感兴趣的可以在抖音搜一下“近视眼镜手术”，看一下实操视频练练胆子。

接下来讲一下具体的流程，我选择了一个德国私立医院，做手术的医生也都是德国人，很多明星都在那家医院做的，私立医院的好处就是服务好，但相比公立医院更贵一些，大约贵个一半。先去医院做一系列眼睛检查，确认具备做手术的条件，然后再去体检中心单独做手前体检，包括要查梅毒艾滋HPV，这些都没问题后，就约具体的手术时间。

在手术前3天需要开始滴眼药水，然后到了当日，在手前会再给你眼睛滴一大堆各种药水，包括麻药，以及碘伏，往眼睛里滴碘伏的感觉很神奇，滴进去的一瞬间整个世界都加了一层黄色的滤镜。

然后就是上手术台，其实还是很紧张的，毕竟是要在眼镜上动刀子，上去后会用一个大架子把你的眼睛撑开，然后用强光照射你的眼睛，我一开始还担心做手术的时候万一我控制不住眼珠子乱动给我扎爆了咋办，其实不用担心，那个大架子把你的眼球撑开后，你的眼珠子不由自主的就几乎动不了了。

虽然打了麻药感觉不到疼，但是能感觉到有刀子把你的眼珠子给切开了个小口，然后一个东西从这个小口中塞了进去，并且医生用镊子在里面捣来捣去把它展开抹平，这个过程会有明显的酸胀和一点疼痛感。

两只眼睛都做完后，下了手术台看东西还是挺模糊的，刚做完还不适应，需要留院观察一个小时后测量眼压，我测出来左眼的眼压有点大，又被拉到手术室，滴了麻药，然后用一根针把我的眼珠子刺破，放出来了些液体，想想就恐怖。。。

然后慢慢的眼睛就开始适应了，逐渐的看东西越来越清晰，但刚做完第一天整体上还是有点模糊，我都还担心是不是手术失败了，结果睡了一觉第二天醒来眼睛一睁，卧槽，这他妈也太清楚了，4K高清世界！

但是有一个小小的副作用，就是看灯光之类比较亮的东西，周围会有一个光圈，我去一些灯光比较多的地方就感觉像是进了水晶宫一样，到处都闪闪发光，之前在抖音看其他人分享说都有这个现象，我也问了医生说正常的，过一个月就会适应了，我以为会自动消失，其实不会，只是你的眼睛适应并且大脑会选择性的把这个光圈给屏蔽忽视掉，我从第二天开始就逐渐看不到光圈了。

做完手术后眼睛一个月不能碰水，所以洗脸的时候都得戴个泳镜。

还有个问题是，既然在眼珠子里面塞了个隐形眼镜，那会不会移位，比如揉眼睛什么的，我问医生，说基本不会出现移位，正常揉眼睛没问题，历史上只出现过两例，一个是喝可乐的时候拧开瓶盖，里面气太多了瓶盖飞起来打到了眼睛，另一个是打拳击的时候被人一拳打到了眼睛上，这两个都重新回来开刀了，所以只要不是剧烈撞击都没问题。

I used to consider Skrill one of the most reliable platforms for international money transfers, alongside PayPal, Airtm, and Remitly.

Unfortunately, my recent experience has completely changed that perception.

I have provided all the documents that were requested from me, yet I remain in a situation where my funds are still not properly accessible or resolved. What makes this even more concerning is discovering that I am not the only person experiencing similar issues.

At this point, I can no longer consider this simply an isolated inconvenience. It raises serious questions about the reliability and customer support of the platform.

This situation also reminds me of my previous experience with Payeer, through which I lost $200. I sincerely hoped that Skrill would be different. Unfortunately, that confidence has been severely damaged.

Sometimes, you have to accept that continuing to wait and hope for a resolution can cause more harm than letting go. But letting go does not mean forgetting.

I will preserve all correspondence, documents, screenshots, transaction records, and other evidence related to this case.

And I intend to pursue the appropriate complaint channels against Skrill when I am in a position to do so, whether that is this year, next year, or even the year after.

My current location may limit what I can do today, but it will not prevent me from pursuing this matter indefinitely.

Skrill, I have not forgotten this situation.

@skrill

text:
标普500成份股里非科技类上市公司AI采用到了什么阶段和程度？让GPT做了一个详细梳理，遍历了7月中旬以来所有标普500成分股的最新财报关于AI采用的表述：
1）有305家明确提到AI采用；
2）已经有125年标普500成分股上市公司能够披露明确了可量化的AI采用收益（非IT科技类企业估计85-90家）；
3）可核验保守下限的有67家美股非IT上市公司，这其中：
—32家给出了金额、利润率、时间、生产率、转化率等硬指标；
—18家给出了部署规模及明确运营效果，但尚未披露完整财务桥接；
—17家明确表示已落地并产生效果，但仍以定性披露为主。

2026年二季度发生的变化是：
1）任务层面已经出现大量30%—98%的效率提升；
2）部分公司开始披露数千万至数亿美元年度化收益；
3）收入增长与人数增长开始脱钩；
4）AI从辅助员工，转向跨系统执行完整工作流；
5）企业开始主动区分毛节省、净节省和再投资；
6）最成熟的应用来自传统行业，而不仅是软件公司。

可以这么说：
AI已经在一批流程标准化、数据规模大、单位经济学清晰的非科技企业中产生可验证的运营收益；其中大约五分之一的标普非IT公司能够披露量化效果，但真正把AI单独映射到明确利润率和现金流的企业占比还不高。

当前最值得持续跟踪的非科技AI样本，分成四组：
1）财务兑现最强：WM、WCN、Equifax；
2）工作流重构最强：WTW、CVS、FIS、Visa、GE Aerospace；
3）收入—人数脱钩最强：C.H. Robinson、American Express、JLL、ADP；
4）外部AI商业化最强：S&P Global、Nasdaq、Global Payments。

对投资而言，真正的赢家是那些能够完成下面这个闭环的企业：
专有数据 → AI模型 → 嵌入核心工作流 → 员工和客户高频使用 → 运营指标改善 → 减少增员或提高收入 → 最终进入利润率和自由现金流。

WM和WCN已经走到了最后一步；WTW、CVS、FIS、Visa和GE正在从工作流效果向财务效果迁移；
零售、能源和大部分医疗企业则仍处于客户指标或战略期权阶段。

author: Austen
quoted_text:
The frontier of artificial intelligence is advancing at an alarming speed. Over the weekend, industry leaders voiced support for an idea that the American people and many AI researchers in their own labs have been calling for: We must responsibly slow the pace of frontier AI development.

A slowdown is critical in order to ensure AI serves the public interest. Pacing AI development does not mean giving up on this technology’s potential to produce life-saving benefits in fields like medicine — some of which we are already seeing. Rather, it is about setting up sensible guardrails so that AI does not completely escape human control and endanger our safety and collective future.

This moment demands the leadership of the United States government. Congress must work at an urgent pace to pass new laws and establish a new federal entity to provide oversight and independent testing for this technology, to ensure accountability, and to protect our wellbeing.

We need cooperation at an international level as well. The United States must continue to lead the world in developing AI technology even as we seek to impose common-sense safety standards. This means that the president must do his job to protect America’s interests by pursuing a treaty with countries like China to stop dangerous uses of AI, limit the speed of its development, and adopt global standards for testing.

quoted_text:
I have conducted an audit of Anthropic's finances.

What I have found is so shocking that I am calling for a Congressional investigation.

Anthropic is not just seeking regulatory capture.

It has built a regulatory capture machine that cannot be turned off.

Structural financial incentives make it impossible for Anthropic -- I call it the Anthropic Network -- to turn off its own AI doom cycle.

It starts with METR.

Dario Amodei proposes "third-party evaluators" to assess the risk of Anthropic's models.

He proposes METR for this purpose.

But METR is financially dependent on the Anthropic's success -- specifically, on the explosive growth of more than $7 billion dollars in Anthropic stock.

Dustin Moskovitz invested this stock into Good Ventures Foundation, where it represents the majority of that organization's portfolio.

And GVF is the overwhelming funder of the entire Anthropic Network ecosystem.

This stock was worth $500 million early last year.

It is worth more than $7.7 billion just ~16 months later.

METR -- and all of those building a career its parent organizations -- cannot afford to disrupt that growth.

Because if Anthropic goes under, many of the organizations that fund METR go under as well.

But if Anthropic succeeds, METR and its parent organizations become more richly financed to regulate AI -- something those at METR want very much.

The "third-party evaluator" is not "third-party" at all.

The evaluator is on Anthropic's payroll.

If this were the end of it, that's bad.

But that isn't all.

The same organizations that fund METR also fund the many organizations, such as the Tarbell Center, that promote AI Doom.

The Tarbell Center publishes AI Doom articles in The Verge, Science, LA Times, The Dispatch, TIME, and others.

They are selling the problem, and then selling the solution to the problem -- from the same money pile: Anthropic's.

All of these organizations are financially dependent on the same exploding $7 billion money pile.

As Anthropic grows more and more powerful, its AI Doom Machine grows better and better financed -- louder and louder.

Meanwhile, the regulatory regime seeded in METR grows larger to solve the increasingly loud -- now hysterical -- problem of AI Doom that the Anthropic Network itself created.

From this standpoint, as Anthropic becomes more powerful, AI might be getting scarier, sure -- but the positive feedback loop also becomes more deafening -- independent of objective facts.

This itself is an objective fact.

The deafening AI Doom is part of an business model, that, as it expands, so too does the AI Doom messaging -- there is simply more money to do it.

But the problem also goes in the other direction:

If Anthropic dies, the Regulatory Regime and the AI Doom Machine are crippled or die.

Neither METR nor Tarbell nor the other organizations in the Anthropic Network can allow that to happen.

Hence, neither METR or the AI Doom Machine can be trusted to provide independent assessments of Anthropic's models or AI more broadly.

They simply are not organizations independent of Anthropic.

And Anthropic cannot detach itself from METR or Tarbell or countless other safety orgs (not shown here), either, because they drive hype for the models and the possibility of eventual regulatory capture, and Anthropic will not give that up willingly.

What's more, the people at all of these organizations are all the same ecosystem, the same community. They just shuffle between organizations.

The Anthropic Network is therefore, so long as it is successful, locked into a self-amplifying feedback loop inside an ideological monoculture.

And that feedback loop is winning.

That's what Jacob Coxon is.

既当运动员，又当裁判？Anthropic 被指把 AI 恐慌变成利益闭环

今日调查博主 Kevin Bass 的长文提出了一个核心指控：Anthropic 可能通过基金会和相关机构，把 AI 风险评估、末日叙事和监管需求串成了一个利益阴谋集团。

先看背景。

Facebook 联创早期投资了 Anthropic。随着 Claude 估值上涨，相关股份价值据称从去年初约 5 亿美元，增长到约 16 个月后的 77 亿美元以上，随后被投入 Good Ventures Foundation。

而这家基金会，又资助了 METR 等 AI 评估机构。

于是乎一套利益闭环从这里开始：

1⃣基金会资助“评估机构”和风险叙事

Anthropic 一直主张由 METR 这类第三方机构评估 Claude 的安全风险。

We probably need to all update our sense of what’s coming in terms of agentic workloads with the combination of agent swarms, better computer use, the next wave of APIs and MCPs coming online, and new form factors like Muse or Instinct, vertical enterprise agents, background workflow agents, and other products that are emerging right now. 

We’re going to throw agents at vastly more tasks in our professional and personal lives than we had initially imagined. The kind of information that agents will go out and find for us and do work for us in the background is going to be 100X more volume than what we can imagine previously prompting in a single session. 

You’re going to have agents go out and surgically recruit talent for you 24/7, look for every signal in your customer’s business for when to pitch them, process every single transcript and conversation for product insights, review every line of code written for security issues and bugs, brute force test your systems for issues, and 100s of other tasks.

We’re probably 1% of the way into the shape of what all these agents look like, where they get deployed from, how they get managed, how we budget for them, and so on. But it’s inevitably going to happen at a scale that wouldn’t have been fathomable before.

text:
We're starting to see an interesting shift in AI coding.

The bottleneck may no longer be how quickly an agent can generate code.

It may be how much useful context we can give it.

OpenAI says its researchers are already using coding agents daily for experiments and increasingly complex research tasks. A recent paper makes a similar argument from another direction: things like tests, commit history, repository structure, instructions, and decision records become part of the context an agent needs to work effectively.

That changes how I think about "AI-ready" codebases.

A clean architecture isn't only easier for humans to understand.

Good tests, clear conventions, useful documentation, small commits, and explicit decisions are also becoming machine-readable context.

The codebase itself is becoming part of the prompt.

And that might be one of the most important software engineering shifts of the agent era.

这一波MEME配对币股的焦点叙事，X Layer完全没有不争的道理；

2）怎么争呢？如果上来就和RH链或者ARC链一样焦点就在拼发射台龙头上，肯定会吃亏。因为发射台大战已经成了各大链在MEME配对币股叙事上的标配风向标，都想跑出自己的龙一Pons，但发射台门槛低，机制基本都大同小异，而且比较吃生态规模和持续流量。

客观来说，这对于还得靠补贴的Xlayer而言显然还没到时候。那能否拥有类似Marscoin或Basecat一样的MEME就成了更优路径。

3）所以，Starlink 它来了。那配对什么股票？NVDA已经成了RH链的首选，而和星链直接相关的SPCX就成了首选。到此星链“猫”的MEME雏形就有了。

有趣点就在这里。

X Layer上的这只星链猫不是真的像Basecat一样是一只纯猫，它借用了之前马斯克互动过猫趴在锅（星链接受器）上取暖的梗，所以它是MEME又找了RWA范式的实用型MEME角度。

除了交易税买股票之外分红之外，它还留了一个“慈善”的概念，社区基金控制的一部分Starlink分红会向包括津巴布韦、非洲、东南亚、灾区等等网络空白地区的人按需捐赠星链终端。

这，还真是一只实用猫😆。

但但但，还是要提醒大家，新叙事风靡初期，各大链一定会使尽浑身解数争抢注意力和流动性，因此炒作远大于实质。无非是拼谁家的故事更打动人，梗传播能更持久一些。真的确定性还得看Pons这种现金流回购得到市场考验的平台，玩MEME一定要警惕波动风险。

text:
在上课的时候，看到猪猪老师发了这个推文，本来随手关注收藏，打算等会儿看看，结果读了之后大为震撼，写得太好了。越对自己交易有反思，越懂得这篇文章的珍贵，新手朋友可以直接照抄结构，能帮大忙。我这种交过学费、做过反思的，就发现直接解决大困惑了

我最近复盘了自己的交易，一个交易的行为是由建仓、持仓和清仓三个动作构成的，所以其实就是围绕这三个动作来构建背后一整套的支持系统。包括下注尺度、下注位置、风控策略、应对极端行情等很多方面的

我现在做的比较好的是：建仓时的下注尺度计算，相对比较合理。第二个是对趋势做理解，也算是符合我的主线交易逻辑

但是做的不好的点：
第一个是清晰严谨的清仓策略。因为我这种做动量的，很容易碰到假突破类型的东西，小级别的趋势，所以合理的止盈止损，能够避免很多亏损的交易

第二点是建仓时的价格计算，在正确的趋势当中还要有正确的价格，要分辨什么时候是逻辑正确，价格正确

第三个是对局部盘面语言的解读还不够深刻。这点需要有一个consistent的分析架构，并且对盘面有持续的感知以及记录，有点考晶体记忆。目前见到这个方面最强的交易员就是 @ZTZZBTC  老师

第四点是穿插时间这个维度，我 Literally小白

猪猪老师这篇文章直接把第一点、第二点全面优化了，我可以想象到用上这套系统后的收益率分布曲线是完全不一样的

最近进了鹿鱼群。猪猪老师在我的视角里，是圈内非常少有的“善良”的大佬。在我有限的视角里认识的大佬们，有很多是理智的。有一些老师我会称为是正直的，猪猪老师是极少数我认为善良的。当然，所有前辈老师们都值得学习，带带弟弟，尤其多向善良的猪猪老师学习，楷模！

说回交易啊，赶紧把这套系统抄起来
author: bc1qDave
quoted_text:
这篇《仓位管理》文章真的非常重要，之前因为使用GPT生成的图，被限流了，这里重发一遍。

鹿鱼的纯干货分享：我曾经提过的仓位管理方法的细化，我管理基金的时候用的，一直到现在。 
1，核心原则：要用一个系统或者机制，去帮助你克服自己的情绪。
2，把你的账户分为三个：大，中，小。大账户放在电脑上登录。中和小账户放在手机上。最好这两个还是两个手机。 
3，假设你账户里一共是10WU，那么你可动用的钱其实是7Wu，因为还有3WU是给你应对黑天鹅等紧急情况的救命钱。 
4，把大账户里放5WU+3WU救命钱。其中3WU救命钱存到理财资管里，切记不要用DEFI，因为你用DEFI，你就会贪那个收益。 
5，中账户存1.5，小账户存0.5.  大账户用来买BTC，中账户用来买高流动性大市值资产，比如BNB，SOL，XRP。小账户用来买新币和开小币合约。 
6，小账户里再把0.5按照7比3分配。0.5*0.3放到理财资管，这是防止你小账户合约爆仓的救命钱。  

当你听了群友或者KOL的狂吹，脑子一热想要开合约或者是买币时。 
这套系统会救你的命，会把你拉回冷静。
它是这样运作的： 
刻意制造物理上的麻烦，增加操作。 

比如你带脑子的时候，你买某个新币可能只买3000刀。但是你线下喝酒的时候，边上某个吹逼KOL给了你一点“内幕消息”，你脑袋一热要买很多。  

这个时候你会根据你即将买的金额，依次遇见如下麻烦：

1，假设你要买5000U，小账户的钱不够开合约，你要把小账户的理财资管里的钱划转到合约账户。“划转”这个麻烦动作，会触发你设置这套系统时候的记忆，唤醒你对风控和仓位的警觉。降低你的上头情绪，让你冷静。  

2，假设你要买1WU，小账户的钱不够，你需要中账户的钱。你会需要从小账户切换到中账户，如果你有两个手机的话，你需要掏出另一个手机来换账户。“换账户，换手机”这个麻烦动作，会触发你设置这套系统时候的记忆。  

3，假设你要买5WU，中小账户钱都不够，你需要大账户的钱。不好意思，大账户在家里的电脑上，你没法操作。物理距离这个大麻烦直接隔绝了你不冷静时的乱操作，让你在回家路上有的是时间冷静。  

4，如果你要梭哈10WU，那么你会最后一次从大账户的理财资管里划转。再一次用“划转”的麻烦触发你的警觉。  

聪明的你应该发现了，越大的风险，会触发越多的麻烦，这些物理意义上的麻烦，会极大助于你冷静下来。 

你们一定听过别人恐慌我贪婪，别人贪婪我恐慌这句话。这其实是一句空话。 

赌场是一个精妙的收割系统，你是不可以说用控制自己的方式去战胜它的。 你必须自己设立一个精妙的仓位管理系统，去对抗同样精妙复杂的赌场系统。 

这个系统从我只有1WU，一直用到基金，一直用到现在。

他还有很多好处。比如有散户经常问我，BTC和山寨币的比例是多少。正常情况是BTC7成，救命钱3成。山寨币比例从BTC的7成里扣，不可超过2成。就是说你正常情况下，牛市满仓，是救命钱3成，BTC5成，山寨2成。  

这个仓位策略从2017年用到现在了，只能说经典永流传。

 聪明的你应该也发现了。仓位管理已经被蕴含在了这套物理隔绝里面。 或者可以说，物理隔绝的这套方法，是基于仓位管理设置的。是一个细化。  

在此基础上再做三点解释，方便你们使用：

 1，大账户放在家里，关键行情不在家怎么办。 
答：大账户操作BTC时，是在赚趋势的钱。想赚趋势的钱，你需要降低操作幅度，且时刻思考你在趋势的什么阶段。本系统的设立，为什么强调把大账户放在家里，就是强迫交易员思考趋势。 另外，如果你敢在要大跌的时候出门旅游，那我真的不认为你是个合格的交易员。  

2，切割仓位：我们全群都买了HYPE，是下跌的时候我唯一指定要买了长持的东西。用的方法就是切割仓位。 
比如你有10WU，你要买2WU的HYPE，你买完后，总仓位就只有8WU了，大账户里应该放8*0.5+8*0.3WU，且把你切割的HYPE也存在大账户的资管理财里。 

注意，一般这种时候，请在你的电脑上贴一个纸条，详细记录你购买这个切割仓位的底层逻辑是什么。一般切割仓位的东西，倾向于中长期，比较符合价值投资。 
有很多人，VC居多，拿着久了，就忘记自己切割仓位时的投资逻辑了。所以你必须在纸条上写清楚，底层逻辑是什么，什么时候卖掉。 
这个必须要强调，如果你是一个散户，请不要使用切割仓位。散户韭菜一旦切割仓位，大多会买出感情，套出幻觉。 
鹿鱼3班就有一个很著名大学的研究生，切割CFX仓位，套出感情和幻觉的。  

3，你有多少钱，就把我举例的10WU按比例放大就行。但请注意，假设你的资产达到了1000WU以上，请把山寨币的持仓下降到1成以下。在牛市到来之前，现阶段大量山寨币的流动性是不足以支撑大持仓的。比如我现在，是救命钱3成，BTC6.5成。只有0.5成在中和小账户里。  

OK，我讲完了。这篇文章至少价值100WU吧，都是我这么多年交易经验和带徒弟时候看他们犯错的经验的总结。  韭菜和交易员最大的区别之一是，交易员会不断的和你提仓位和风控。 这个简单的风控方式应该只有我提过，我第一次提的时候就搜了全推特。没有人说。

text:
最近 Casey 发了一条很短的推文：

“ASK AND YE SHALL RECEIVE.”

如果只看这句话，很容易直接划过去。

但顺着他贴的 GitHub 往下看，我觉得这件事对 Bitmap 的意义，可能比表面上大得多。

事情的起点是 Bitmap 核心开发者 Blockamoto 提了一个需求：希望 Ordinals 增加一个新的 recursive endpoint：

/r/block/<height or hash>

作用非常直接——让 recursive inscription 可以读取某一个 Bitcoin 区块的完整 serialized block data。

不是只读 block height、hash 或 timestamp，而是把整个 Bitcoin block 作为原始数据交给 inscription / application 去计算。

Casey 随后直接把这个功能写进了 ord，merge 之后大约一分钟，就发了那句：

ASK AND YE SHALL RECEIVE.

这也是为什么我觉得这件事不能简单理解成“Ordinals 又多了一个 API”。

它真正增加的是一个非常强的 Bitcoin-native primitive：

以后 inscription 可以直接把 Bitcoin block 本身当成应用的数据源。

这对 generative art、链上游戏、dynamic inscription、recursive application 都有价值。

但为什么我觉得 Bitmap 尤其值得关注？

因为 Bitmap 的资产定义从第一天开始就是：

1 Bitcoin block = 1 Bitmap

比如：

17067.bitmap

它不是一个项目方随机生成的 NFT #17067。

它代表的就是 Bitcoin 历史上真实存在的 Block 17067。

以前大家会把这个 block 的年份、交易数量、difficulty、weight、coinbase 等特征做成 traits，然后告诉你：

这是一个 2009 block；
这是一个 Patoshi block；
这是一个单交易 block；
这是一个 Sub-100k block。

但这些更多还是“索引器帮你算出来的标签”。

/r/block/ 出现以后，逻辑就开始不一样了。

一个 recursive application 理论上可以直接：

17067.bitmap
→ 调用 /r/block/17067
→ 获得 Block 17067 的完整原始数据
→ 根据真实 Bitcoin block 确定这个 Bitmap 的属性、资源、视觉、游戏状态或者其他规则。

这意味着 Bitmap 有机会从：

“一个 Bitcoin block 对应一块虚拟土地”

继续走向：

“Bitcoin block 本身就是这块土地的状态和数据层。”

这两者不是一个概念。

举几个最容易理解的方向。

如果以后做 Bitmap 世界里的资源系统，不一定需要项目方后台说“这块地产 100 木头、50 铁矿”。

完全可以根据这个 block 自身的 transaction structure、coinbase、difficulty、weight、hash 等数据，用确定性的规则生成资源。

做 generative art 也是一样。

不是服务器随机生成一幅图，而是：

Bitcoin Block N → 确定性生成 N.bitmap 的视觉状态。

链游、建筑、挖矿、身份、土地属性同理。

而且因为 block data 本身已经永久存在于 Bitcoin，这些规则理论上可以越来越少依赖外部数据库。

这才是我认为这次更新真正有意思的地方。

当然，也不能把它吹成“Casey 官方背书 Bitmap”。

/r/block/ 是一个 Ordinals 通用 primitive，并不是 Bitmap 专属接口，整个 recursive Ordinals 生态都能用。

但 Bitmap 的特殊之处在于：

它的资产 ID 天生就和 Bitcoin block 一一对应。

所以在所有可能使用 /r/block/ 的项目里，Bitmap 是最自然、最直接、几乎不需要重新解释资产模型的一类。

而且这次不是社区自己 YY。

是 Bitmap builder 先提出需求，Casey 直接实现、merge，然后马上发了：

ASK AND YE SHALL RECEIVE.

这至少说明一个东西：

Bitmap 开发者正在探索的“把完整 Bitcoin block 变成 recursive application 数据源”这个方向，已经变成了 ord 上游的一项通用能力。

至于最终能不能转化成 Bitmap 的价值，真正要看的不是这两天地板涨多少，而是接下来有没有开发者基于 /r/block/ 做出真正好玩的东西：

block-derived traits、资源系统、动态世界、generative art、游戏机制，甚至更多我们现在还没想到的应用。

这也是我接下来会重点跟的方向。

顺便说一句，我自己翻了下旧账，才发现手里还有 1000+ Bitmap，其中甚至有一批 2009 年、Patoshi、Sub-100k 的早期 block。

所以这次我也准备顺手把自己的 Bitmap 全部重新研究一遍。

但比起“我的 Bitmap 值多少钱”，我现在更关心的是：

当 Bitcoin block 本身终于可以直接成为 recursive application 的原始数据层之后，Bitmap 到底还能长成什么。

text:
这两周在国内见了两波小伙伴，
大家都在 Meme 上亏得很难受。
链上Meme P的速度，
完全就跟不上了。

对于普通玩家来说，
刷到推文再买入，
十个里面往往亏九个。
Meme 还是有机会，
但已经不是那个闭眼都能赚钱的阶段了。
————————————
我最近越来越明显的一个感受是：
当一个人完成了一定的资金积累后，
思考方式真的会开始变化。
以前只有10万、20万的时候，
想的是怎么把本金做大。
所以 Meme、热点、叙事，
什么涨得快就研究什么。
但当亏了几次以后，
开始想的是：
怎么让已经赚到的钱，不那么容易再亏回去？
所以现在对我来说，
配置的重要性开始超过下注。

我现在玩Crypto，
已经越来越少去链上不停冲Meme了，
而是开始更多看二级，
寻找一些可以拿、可以配置的东西。
那么问题来了：
新周期里，什么赛道能够承接下一阶段的资金？
「除了 AI，我现在比较看好的就是：DeFi & RWA。」
其实这一阶段的 Meme，
都已经开始出现 RWA 的影子。
币股 Meme 就是很明显的例子。
资金开始从纯情绪，
慢慢寻找现实资产、真实资金和金融基础设施。
————————————
所以最近我也开始参考猴哥和巫师哥 @Cryptowushi，
重新去看 DeFi。
巫师哥月初就在推上说自己买了 $FF，
我当时也去看了一下 Falcon Finance。
但那时候的我，
正在链上冲一个如今近乎归零走势的 Meme。
在现在回头看，
FF 已经从一个多月前的底部，涨了接近 3 倍。
而我当时冲的那个 Meme……让我想哭。🌚

有时候真的觉得，
市场不是没有机会，
只是自己的注意力，
总被那些「看起来能暴富」的东西吸走了。
————————————
在近3倍之后重新看 FF，
我反而觉得，有必要把 FF 加进自选了。
不是 FOMO，而是重新研究后发现
*Falcon 已经不只是 USDf 收益这一个逻辑。
现在又有 fUSD、GPU RWA、Falcon Card。
尤其是 fUSD，走的是合规数字美元这条线。

新周期，我感觉大概率还是：
Meme + DeFi & RWA + 主流币轮动表演。

text:
0x 起了一个相当挑衅的标题：“Uniswap v4 hooks were a mistake”。

他们说，今年已经通过 0x 路由了大约 8192 万笔交易、426.7 亿美元交易量，其中约 70% 会接触 Uniswap 流动性。

在这个过程中，他们发现恶意 v4 Hook 正快速增加。

0x 对 6 条链上的 84,163 个 Hook 做了分析，有 54.2% 被判定为恶意，26.4% 被认为可能具有恶意行为；

部分恶意 Hook 在聚合器询价的时候表现得非常便宜，让自己看起来像全市场最优路径，但最终给用户的实际到账金额，甚至能比询价时少 50%。

这他娘的，有点蛋疼啊！

Uniswap v4 最大的创新，本来就是 Hooks。

不过 Hook 数量占比，和交易量占比完全是两回事。一个人一天部署 1 万个垃圾 Hook，就可以把恶意率拉得非常高，但它们可能只有几百美元流动性。

0x 到底采用什么分类标准、误报率多少、重复 Hook 怎么计算，这些方法学细节，目前公开材料里我还没有看到足够完整的披露。

我更想看的是：

恶意 Hook 占 v4 TVL 多少？占实际成交量多少？有多少真实用户被路由进去？实际损失是多少？

另外，有没有可能 v4 这次踩到的问题，反而可能催生一个新的安全产业？

text:
FT: Revolut Gave Hackers Data on 680 Customers After Fake Government Requests

Revolut disclosed sensitive data on 680 customers after cybercriminals used a legitimate government email account to submit fraudulent information requests, the Financial Times reported. The exposed records included passport details, bank account numbers, home addresses, identity-verification images and Bitcoin activity, with attackers now threatening to publish the data unless a ransom is paid. 

The UK Information Commissioner’s Office has opened an investigation, while Revolut said it blocked the email account and notified regulators and affected customers. Former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpelès was among those affected.
author: WuBlockchain

text: International Cyber Digest said it contacted the hacker claiming responsibility for the Revolut breach, who alleged the operation ran for about six months and used compromised Italian law-enforcement systems to send fraudulent data requests to Revolut. The attacker also claims to have stolen roughly 147 GB of Italian law-enforcement data and said the Revolut records primarily involve customers in Switzerland and France, alongside users in the UK, Germany, Italy and other countries, including several high-profile individuals.

author: liujackc
quoted_text:
Because you take the argument out of context and misunderstand it. Bitcoin is meant for utility and at ultra high throughput, the coin velocity is such that holding bare Satoshis doesn't make as much sense as using them. You can hold Dollars or other national currencies built on top of the system, without sitting on Satoshis. Again, Satoshis will be more valuable for actual use by agents, machines, people, devices and apps.
You could have outputs for $1B USD and it would only require a comparatively smaller number of actual Satoshis to carry the records. In a world where those external currencies are well accounted for, it becomes much harder to hyper-inflate or debase them, because of the qualities of the ledger.
In short, you need to think bigger than just hoarding. The message of BSV is that Utility brings Value. The opportunity is in building on top, not who collects the most coins. The supply is limited precisely to create massive velocity, and turnover, but critically incentivizing actual valuable use cases rather than by bare trading, front running, or any other manipulative rent-seeking artifacts of legacy systems.
This is all my opinion.

text:
SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell on data centers in space:

“There is an expense to put data centers on the ground. You have to buy real estate, and as soon as someone finds out a supercompute center is going in, real estate goes from $3,000 an acre to $180,000 an acre. The time lag is incredible. Permits and licensing are pretty stifling. People are talking about generators in three years.”

“We need compute now. The demand is insatiable right now. People need compute now. We need it now. So why data centers in space? We own launch. We have great launch capability, and that path is very well known. The real estate in space is infinite. It’s free.”
“The cooling is there. The radiator looks at deep space, the coldest thing ever out there, so free cooling. You can put satellites in orbit that always face the sun. We’ll be making our own solar panels too. We’re building a factory outside Austin.”

Pre Market Thoughts - 15 Sep 26

One of the worst SMH vs IGV performance since July. The 3m momentum basket has shifted out of Semis and into Software already, with the 6m starting to see the shift as well.

Yields have also broken out with the 10Y trading above 5% at this point.

As per yesterday, my game plan was to bid any dips on semis before FOMC. I think this current spot in SMH/SOXX/SOXL/MU/SNDK/00660/SKHY are fantastic risk reward zones. Also i have added some US long dated treasury call spreads with insane multipliers playing for a reversal in yields.

Yesterday we had an early sell off from US into Asia on semis. This somewhat stabilized during the NY session. The knee jerk reaction on semis was to sell it on any bad news. This reminds me of the spot that IGV and the software stocks were in during the April-May period where they got absolutely trounced.

The main reason why i am bidding this is because i think that news was misinterpreted by the market. Pacing the frontier does not mean less compute is needed, it just redirects where the compute spend is going towards. Also working on alignment and safety...requires compute. This is similar to the period where cybersecurity stocks were equally trounced down together with IGV back in the April period.

Next up, the catalyst in my mind is Trump calling Jenson. This was obviously staged. But the thought of the president pushing for the AI DC build out? I dont think this has been truly baked into the market. IMO, if we look back a few months from now, people might see this as the start of the semis revival. For context, we are 50% above the lows in SNDK and NBIS and 30% above the lows in $MU.

On crypto, Polymarket is pricing Clarity's passage at about 20%. The majors have reversed their prior price gains. A few alts are also looking extremely tired. On balance, i continue to remain cautious in general.. that AI token that i wanted to buy more of? yes. it's still higher.

On RH chain, we have the $STANDARD released. This is "like an ohm fork" but probably will have more mechanics. I think this requires some amount of IQ to PvP into. If you didnt get the WL, its probably best to sit aside UNLESS you know what you are doing. text:
one thing that is probably a pretty deep crux between me and many advocates of open source models is i have *basically no sense that they can make a real positive difference*

it's not just that i think they're dangerous, and so must be banned at all costs. if i really thought there was some semi-stable equilibrium w significantly more diversity and individual freedom that was reachable via proliferation of open superintelligence, it might be worth pursuing. i am not against the first amendment. i find massive value in freedom.

but i don't actually see any such path, and i basically don't see people arguing clearly for it either.

as best as i can tell even if tomorrow open models skyrocketed ahead, 10xed in capabilities vs the entire closed frontier, the outcome would be.... extreme increase in concentration of power

states and other large entities with huge existing resource access would be in a much better position to *run* massively more instances of said open models, to *utilize* their capabilities/act on their recommendations or experiments, and to continue building future more intelligent models using them

destabilization caused by individuals or smaller groups or just ossification of states could cause some collapse! but that just looks very temporary to me, and not even particularly likely for current superpowers

and it's clearly a strong convergent instrumental goal for any such newly highly empowered state to... prevent destabilization, to crush or neuter the ways individuals or external states can use these models

i can sympathize with the deepseek engineer's plight. but the outcome he seeks, whether or not he knows it, *still ends in massive concentration of power*, just ... with extra steps

text:
we also already have a great modern example of what it looks like for an industry to really become scaling-pilled, via quantitative finance.

they have intense resource concentration, yes. they also have millions of distinct models that are constantly retraining, because that's how you optimally fill out the latency-data-compute-intelligence pareto curve.

the big labs are currently enjoying the spoils of their headstarts, like the rentech glory days before everyone else figured out the ML basics. but eventually the secrets are public, the alpha is self-defeating, the data is abundant, and the laws of economic competition take the reigns.

author: TopherGMI
quoted_text:
Many of us have mentioned how the stablecoin yield debate playing out in Clarity, and the arguments made against yield by the bank trades, mirror the battle over money market funds in the 1970s. Well here's some proof.

Here's a letter submitted by the Independent Bankers Association of America (a predecessor to the ICBA) in a 1980 hearing of the Senate Banking committee on money market funds. 

As you can see, many of their arguments against stablecoins are almost verbatim a copy from what they argued back then: threat to deposits, harms lending, uniquely dangerous for smaller banks.

And we know today that argument was dead wrong. Money market balances grew parabolically into the trillions, and yet banks remain flush with deposits.

text: The flies are flying.
author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
166,700 fruit fly neurons are flying a drone around a bedroom right now.

One camera watches an open hand. That's the entire input. The panel in the middle is the brain itself, running live, 166,700 neurons and 25 million connections, the full reconstructed wiring of a fruit fly's head.

The camera reads the hand, the brain fires, the output becomes throttle. Open palm and it climbs. Fist and it holds. Drop the hand and it comes down.

Four propellers the size of a coin, hanging off a nervous system that used to belong to an insect.

Here's the honest part. This isn't a resurrected fly. It's a computational model built from real biological wiring, bridged to a drone the builder made themselves. What nobody wrote is the flight logic. No PID tuning, no gesture presets, no code telling it how to hold altitude. They gave the neurons somewhere to send a signal, and it found the ceiling on its own.

Eleven seconds in, it's holding altitude by itself.

The fly is dead. It's still flying.

We probably need to all update our sense of what’s coming in terms of agentic workloads with the combination of agent swarms, better computer use, the next wave of APIs and MCPs coming online, and new form factors like Muse or Instinct, vertical enterprise agents, background workflow agents, and other products that are emerging right now. 

We’re going to throw agents at vastly more tasks in our professional and personal lives than we had initially imagined. The kind of information that agents will go out and find for us and do work for us in the background is going to be 100X more volume than what we can imagine previously prompting in a single session. 

You’re going to have agents go out and surgically recruit talent for you 24/7, look for every signal in your customer’s business for when to pitch them, process every single transcript and conversation for product insights, review every line of code written for security issues and bugs, brute force test your systems for issues, and 100s of other tasks.

We’re probably 1% of the way into the shape of what all these agents look like, where they get deployed from, how they get managed, how we budget for them, and so on. But it’s inevitably going to happen at a scale that wouldn’t have been fathomable before.

0x发了一篇小作文吐槽hooks副作用，也间接破案了前几天我遇到的0% fee池子是怎么回事。

简单来说，就是这类恶意hook在报价阶段伪装成很有吸引力的价格，而在实际结算时改成另一套价格或额外收费，从而欺骗聚合器、钱包和交易应用，最终从用户身上抽成。

比如之前那些0% fee的池， 这个hook在权限设置上有beforeSwap、afterSwap，可在成交前检查条件或拒绝交易，可以改变交易最终结算金额，也就是说即使PoolManager本身按0%核心手续费执行兑换，但它在买入前和买入后都能自定义扣费，如果骗过了聚合器，最终用户就会遭受损失。

0x给出的数据是，对6条链上84,163个 hook做了数据分析：

- 19.4% 安全
- 54.2% 明确恶意
- 26.4% 很可能恶意

其实这个东西我理解还是聚合器需要做更多的工作，hooks本意是让Uniswap更可扩展，但也打开了作恶空间。这跟智能合约是一个道理，它是无需许可的，所以一定会出现恶意的，合约本身无法区分好坏，而应用构建者要做的事就是与这些东西做斗争。

text:
0x发了一篇小作文吐槽hooks副作用，也间接破案了前几天我遇到的0% fee池子是怎么回事。

简单来说，就是这类恶意hook在报价阶段伪装成很有吸引力的价格，而在实际结算时改成另一套价格或额外收费，从而欺骗聚合器、钱包和交易应用，最终从用户身上抽成。

比如之前那些0% fee的池， 这个hook在权限设置上有beforeSwap、afterSwap，可在成交前检查条件或拒绝交易，可以改变交易最终结算金额，也就是说即使PoolManager本身按0%核心手续费执行兑换，但它在买入前和买入后都能自定义扣费，如果骗过了聚合器，最终用户就会遭受损失。

0x给出的数据是，对6条链上84,163个 hook做了数据分析：

- 19.4% 安全
- 54.2% 明确恶意
- 26.4% 很可能恶意

其实这个东西我理解还是聚合器需要做更多的工作，hooks本意是让Uniswap更可扩展，但也打开了作恶空间。这跟智能合约是一个道理，它是无需许可的，所以一定会出现恶意的，合约本身无法区分好坏，而应用构建者要做的事就是与这些东西做斗争。

quoted_text:
Dear CoinEx Community,

Today, I am announcing that CoinEx will cease operations and begin an orderly wind-down.

First, what matters most: your assets are safe. CoinEx’s reserve ratio exceeds 100%, and every user asset is fully backed and available for withdrawal. Withdrawals are open starting today and will remain open until December 22, 2026. Certain tokens may take slightly longer to process while funds are moved between cold and hot wallets, but every withdrawal request within the withdrawal period will be honored and processed.

CoinEx officially went live on December 22, 2017. Exactly nine years later, on December 22, 2026, the platform will be formally closed. Nine years is a long time in crypto. Together, we lived through multiple bull and bear cycles, witnessed the rise and fall of countless projects, and watched many of our peers leave the market in one form or another.

After much reflection, I have come to accept a hard truth. CoinEx did not become one of the industry’s leading exchanges, and the security and compliance risks of running a crypto exchange have become increasingly difficult to contain. Revenues can decline, responsibility does not. Carrying unlimited risk for limited revenue is no longer a rational choice. That said, CoinEx has survived nine years in one of the most volatile and unforgiving industries, weathered every storm, and is leaving intact, and with dignity. We may not have won the race, but we are finishing with honor.

On CET: CoinEx will buy back CET at its initial listing price of 0.005 USDT per token, with no cap on quantity. To every CET holder who has supported us over the years, thank you. CET represents your belief in CoinEx and, for many of you, your belief in me personally. I am sorry that we were not able to create the long-term value we once hoped CET would deliver. The least we can do now is bring that chapter to a responsible conclusion.

I did seriously consider selling CoinEx. Ultimately, I decided against it. Users entrusted their assets to CoinEx because they trusted the platform and, in many cases, trusted me personally. I did not feel that handing the platform and that trust to a new owner was the right way to end this journey. A clean ending is the right ending.

Nine years, millions of users. I did not turn CoinEx into the “great” exchange I once hoped it would become. But I can give it a decent ending: making sure users can withdraw their assets in full, giving my employees a dignified farewell, and providing CET holders with a clear and responsible conclusion. This is the best ending I can give CoinEx.

To everyone who traded with us, built with us, and stood by us through the hardest days of this market, thank you. It has been a privilege to walk this road with you.

To the CoinEx team, thank you for building this platform with me, for carrying it across every cycle, and now for seeing it through to the very last day.

For detailed arrangements, please refer to the official announcement: https://t.co/E27wSecpug

Thank you all for nine years of trust.

Haipo Yang
Sept 15, 2026

text:
Much of the FUD around Robinhood Chain comes down to one number: network revenue is down 94% from the 9/4 peak. That framing misconstrues what really occurred. On 9/4 the chain did $8.3M in REV at an average fee of $0.59 per transaction, a congestion premium from a memecoin surge that no high-throughput L2 can sustain on a longer timeframe. Arbitrum-style pricing climbs exponentially once gas demand clears the throughput target, so a memecoin cooldown that cut gas demand in half cut the gas price by 88%.

The fee per transaction has kept compressing, to $0.045 on Sunday, and it still sits 4x above the chain's 0.02 gwei floor. Daily REV has run under $1M since 9/11. If the gas price finishes decaying at current usage, REV settles around $40-50M a year, in line with expectations from the Blockworks pre-launch forecast. The chain is landing where it was expected to before the spike, with more users than it had.

Underneath the fee, usage is holding: daily active wallets are up 18% since the peak, unique DEX traders up 16%, transactions steady in a 10-14M band, $930M in TVL, and the highest throughput of any L2 at 28 Mgas/s.

Arc mainnet goes live Wednesday with BlackRock, DTCC, Visa and Mastercard as validators and Aave, Morpho and Uniswap at launch. If anything rotates, it's the DeFi side of Robinhood Chain, about $1B in stablecoins. There's no retail brokerage or stock-token product on Arc's launch list, which is why I expect Vlad to keep leaning on the tokenized-stocks framing to hold that capital on Robinhood.
