The dangerous capability in an MCP setup may not belong to any single tool.

A filesystem server can read data.
A network server can send data.

That is why MCP reviews need a capability map across servers, not just a checklist per tool.

Zealynx's public MCP security checklist covers that combined surface alongside command execution, context poisoning, credentials, supply chain, SSRF, and audit logging.

text:
An AI agent can pass a prompt-injection benchmark and still fail as a system.

The dangerous path is usually a chain:

untrusted document → instruction override → privileged tool call → data sent through an approved channel

That is why our AI red-team audits test the application around the model: prompts, retrieval sources, tool definitions, persistent state, permissions, and multi-step execution.

The deliverable is not a list of clever jailbreaks. It is a reproducible attack chain engineering can fix, followed by fix verification.

3) We're currently in an expansion phase of the protocol, with 3k ETH in net inflows; so issuance multiplier is just 1.00x (adjusts after epoch 2)

6) talking of exits... timing it at the peak during expansion will be optimal if you don't intend to play until the end as the tax kicks in during "contraction" so it may be net positive to play to the end depending on size... that tax gets paid 50% to bankers + 50% to LP

7) the liquidity on the pool is pretty nuts... $8m?! If you're a trader and you spend time understanding the mechanics of the protocol this could be a very lucrative asset to trade in size

9) there's also a holder bonus you need to account for... + it also says bank charter auctions open at a later date suggesting this is JUST season 1... will genesis charters hold a premium if this becomes a much larger economy?

x) Pay attention to how the branch licence mint goes today. I'm anticipating a similar level of craziness... the auction opens up at 2x yesterday's clearing price (2 x 11,800 STANDARD) so you could see 2M+ STANDARD burned in a day if demand holds... that's insane deflation on a token that is issuing ~700k / day

I’m waiting for the licence price to fall or the economics to improve before adding another Branch

I have a feeling this protocol may have a reasonable chance of becoming successful multi month; so pay attention sooner rather than later

quoted_text:
Your RWA coins may have sold off, but there’s still plenty of interesting opportunities 

Here are three I’m watching today:

1. B-money (BSC)

@bmoneyonbnb is a BSC reflection token at $8m market cap. It charges 1% on buys and sells, converts the fee into BTCB and distributes it to qualifying self-custodied holders; more than 2 BTCB has reportedly been distributed

Think: 

b-money / wrapped BTC
@weidai11 Cypherpunk ’98 / Satoshi ’08

Currently volume implies approximately $23K in daily BTCB at a 1% tax. At a steadier $300K daily volume, annual distributions would be around $1.1m

Rewards depend on trading volume, while holders retain token-price and BTCB custody risk

2. Standard Reserve (RH)

@standard_rsv is scheduled to launch today on Robinhood Chain

STANDARD has a 1B hard cap. The first 100M tokens fund permanent protocol-owned Uniswap v4 liquidity. The remaining 900M form an issuance budget, with tokens minted when banker balances are withdrawn

Net ETH flow through the official pool determines policy:

i) Positive flow raises issuance and routes 70% of protocol ETH towards reserve assets such as tokenized gold
ii) Negative or zero flow cuts issuance and sends that 70% towards buybacks and burns. Another 15% adds permanent liquidity; 15% goes to the team

Its 1,000 Charter NFTs (0.15 ETH mint) are participation licences. Opening Branches burns STANDARD; withdrawals retire Branches and charge a variable fee split between burns and remaining bankers

My initial scenario is a:

1) $10M - $30M market cap if Charter demand, liquidity + reserve accumulation persist
2) > $50M would require material reserves, consistent fee flow and burns capable of offsetting withdrawals

Key risks are contract complexity, latent supply in unwithdrawn balances and reliance on one pool as the policy signal; there’s a lot of hype currently so my focus is medium to long term PA as @0xbeans is a genuine actor + long term aligned

3. LOTTO ( @Base)

Trading fees fund $1 @megapot tickets. Purchases return a 10% self-referral rebate to a restricted burn reserve. Winnings enter the same reserve, which buys LOTTO through a rising-price auction and burns the tokens. Mechanics⁠

It has already won a $213K jackpot… next megapot in 8 hours

A batch tickets purchased on Sept 12th contained the winning numbers for the September 13 draw. The $213k jackpot was paid to Lotto Coin one minute after drawing, with the purchase, draw and claim verifiable on Base

Under LOTTO’s design, that capital funds buybacks and burns rather than holder distributions

Against its $2.6M snapshot valuation, the jackpot equals 8.2% of market cap. It will not automatically burn 8.2% of supply; the auction clearing price and seller participation determine the final amount

Megapot’s founder said traffic and ticket purchases crashed its backend, temporarily hiding LOTTO’s transactions in the app

The current draw and its displayed estimates are separate from this win

Using Megapot’s 77.5% long-run prize return plus LOTTO’s 10% rebate, every $10K spent on tickets implies roughly $8,750 expected to reach the burn reserve across many draws. Individual results remain variable + could be interesting on token PA when large Megapots are up for grabs 

The strategic angle is Megapot. If it becomes the default onchain lottery rail, LOTTO could retain first-mover exposure as its flagship autonomous buyer and case study

That is narrative exposure, not a claim on Megapot revenue. A disclosed, vested Megapot stake in LOTTO could align incentives and add credibility. It could also create a conflict if Megapot favoured a token whose fees buy its tickets. Genuine economic exposure would require revenue sharing or reciprocal ownership, not simply Megapot holding LOTTO

There’ve been plenty of other projects creating tangible value across these ecosystems. I’ll provide more insights in tomorrow’s edition of my free newsletter. Link in bio

Let me know if any other novel projects below👇

text:
New Game Paradiso

Part 4 of 4

When I was in middle school, I attended cram school.

More precisely,

I made it as far as the neighborhood around it.

On cram-school days, my mother gave me 1,000 yen for the train and something to eat on the way home.

The proper plan was simple:

Go to cram school.

Study.

Eat something afterward.

Go home.

A perfectly respectable middle-schooler.

At first, I really did attend.

But I fell behind in class.

Before long, I began going to the candy store before class instead of after it.

I also realized that walking the final train stop would leave me with more money for games.

The brain I never used for studying worked remarkably well when finding ways to finance my gaming.

Eventually, even that became too much trouble.

“If I’m not going inside the school anyway, why take the train at all?”

At last, my middle-school self had reached the heart of the matter.

Take the 1,000 yen from my mother.

Pretend to leave for cram school.

Go to a local arcade.

Keep the entire 1,000 yen.

A revolution.

Sometimes I did buy something to eat.

I still got hungry.

But much of the money my mother handed me with the words “Go study” disappeared into arcade machines.

Of course, that could not continue forever.

One day during summer vacation,

an attendance record arrived from the cram school.

My mother looked at it.

Days attended:

about half.

“…What have you been doing?”

There was nowhere to run.

She knew everything.

My mother looked sad rather than angry.

“Did you hate studying that much?”

That was what she asked me.

I still remember her face.

Until then, I don’t think I had ever seen such sadness in her eyes.

I was a child.

I did not understand what it meant for my parents to pay those expensive fees.

I did not understand what that 1,000 yen meant,

or how my mother felt each time she gave it to me.

I wanted to play games.

That was all.

My mother is now in her late eighties.

Someone who once did everything by herself is gradually growing weaker.

She forgets more things now.

“What was that again?”

I hear her say it more often.

I visit her about once a week.

We eat together.

Sometimes we go to a movie.

I don’t know how many more years we will be able to do these things.

When I think about it, I feel a little lonely.

But sometimes I remember

the 1,000-yen bill my mother gave me all those years ago.

“Go study properly.”

Holding the money she gave me with those words,

I headed for the arcade.

After living for more than fifty years, I know this much:

there were countless times I did not listen to my parents.

I probably caused them plenty of pain.

But—

I still remember the games I played with that 1,000 yen.

标普500成份股里非科技类上市公司AI采用到了什么阶段和程度？让GPT做了一个详细梳理，遍历了7月中旬以来所有标普500成分股的最新财报关于AI采用的表述：
1）有305家明确提到AI采用；
2）已经有125年标普500成分股上市公司能够披露明确了可量化的AI采用收益（非IT科技类企业估计85-90家）；
3）可核验保守下限的有67家美股非IT上市公司，这其中：
—32家给出了金额、利润率、时间、生产率、转化率等硬指标；
—18家给出了部署规模及明确运营效果，但尚未披露完整财务桥接；
—17家明确表示已落地并产生效果，但仍以定性披露为主。

2026年二季度发生的变化是：
1）任务层面已经出现大量30%—98%的效率提升；
2）部分公司开始披露数千万至数亿美元年度化收益；
3）收入增长与人数增长开始脱钩；
4）AI从辅助员工，转向跨系统执行完整工作流；
5）企业开始主动区分毛节省、净节省和再投资；
6）最成熟的应用来自传统行业，而不仅是软件公司。

可以这么说：
AI已经在一批流程标准化、数据规模大、单位经济学清晰的非科技企业中产生可验证的运营收益；其中大约五分之一的标普非IT公司能够披露量化效果，但真正把AI单独映射到明确利润率和现金流的企业占比还不高。

当前最值得持续跟踪的非科技AI样本，分成四组：
1）财务兑现最强：WM、WCN、Equifax；
2）工作流重构最强：WTW、CVS、FIS、Visa、GE Aerospace；
3）收入—人数脱钩最强：C.H. Robinson、American Express、JLL、ADP；
4）外部AI商业化最强：S&P Global、Nasdaq、Global Payments。

对投资而言，真正的赢家是那些能够完成下面这个闭环的企业：
专有数据 → AI模型 → 嵌入核心工作流 → 员工和客户高频使用 → 运营指标改善 → 减少增员或提高收入 → 最终进入利润率和自由现金流。

WM和WCN已经走到了最后一步；WTW、CVS、FIS、Visa和GE正在从工作流效果向财务效果迁移；
零售、能源和大部分医疗企业则仍处于客户指标或战略期权阶段。

text:
Zooko on @postagixyz Podcast: Alignment is the principal-agent problem

@zooko has been building privacy tools since the 1990s, long before there was money in it.

@sreeramkannan and I had a conversation with him recently. It changed how I think about privacy altogether.

His argument is that privacy is controlling disclosure. It comes from keeping your value private. Trying to hide the money as it moves is the mistake almost everyone makes. Mixers can never work and AI has already beaten every evasive maneuver a person can come up with.

Then he turns the same lens on AI. He also says alignment is an old question. It is the principal-agent problem. Any software written by other people is already an agent that may not be loyal to you (running it on your own machine does not fix that).

Lawyers owe their clients a duty of loyalty. He thinks the same rule should apply to AI.

Chapters:

00:26 Privacy is controlling disclosure, not hiding
13:08 Privacy comes from value at rest
14:08 The Shapeshift lesson
16:00 Why mixers can never work

17:51 Buying protonmail with shielded Zcash

31:21 Deterministic inference

54:47 The duty of loyalty

quoted_text:
这两天 $BEM 又热起来了。
研究了一圈，我觉得它真正有意思的地方，不只是币价涨了多少，而是 TapeOut 把代币、零件和算力做成了一套相互影响的经济循环。
NAND 和 LATCH 是搭建电路及矿机的基础材料，完成 TapeOut 后形成链上电路，再通过算力持续产出 $BEM。
这里面的逻辑很像一条链：
$BEM 上涨
→ 挖矿预期提高
→ NAND / LATCH 需求增加
→ 部署矿机的成本上涨
→ 全网算力继续增长
→ 单台矿机分到的产出也可能下降
所以并不是 $BEM 涨了，任何时间部署矿机都一定划算。

参与 TapeOut 实际上是在同时判断四件事：
1、$BEM 的真实成交价格和流动性
2、NAND / LATCH 的部署成本
3、全网算力与每日排放的变化
4、不同币价下的预计回本周期
我目前对这套机制偏乐观。相比只靠情绪推动的 Meme，$BEM 至少在协议内部有明确位置，零件、电路、矿机和代币之间也形成了用途闭环。

如果后续用户、有效电路、矿机数量和实际应用能够一起增长，$BEM 的想象空间可能还没有完全打开。
不过现在流动性仍然较薄，页面报价不等于大额资金能够成交的价格。看好归看好，仓位和成本还是要算清楚。
也看到 @bitcoin2themars 等老师最近在持续关注，欢迎懂 TapeOut 的朋友一起交流。
#tapeOut

text:
I completely agree with this take related to the “AI will create viruses that will kill us all” BS. But let me add my few cents, because I am really really angry! 

I worked with one of the deadliest viruses in history, HIV, for two decades. I was one of the early scientists to engineer it, and engineered versions of HIV are now helping cancer patients. I understand the immune system that defends us against viruses extremely deeply. I have worked in high security biohazard labs.

I don’t have a PhD in AI, but I have been involved with AI since the early 90s and have been all in on AI for years.

People claiming that you can just make a virus in your garage, use AI to engineer it, and somehow build a virus that will kill everyone don’t know what the hell they are talking about!

Of course bioweapons are extremely dangerous. In fact, viruses and bacteria have killed more humans throughout history than almost anything else. HIV alone killed tens of millions of people, yet today, if you have access to effective medicines and take them properly, HIV is generally no longer a death sentence.

COVID-19 killed millions. Why doesn’t it kill at anything close to the same scale anymore? Not because the virus disappeared. It is still here. We developed collective defenses against it through our immune systems, prior exposure, vaccines, treatments, and better medical care.

And this is exactly the point.

The best way to fight biological threats, whether natural or synthetic, is to use AI to develop vaccines, treatments, antibodies, antivirals, and eventually engineer our immune system to create much stronger defenses against them.

By the way, it is already possible to make synthetic viruses. You don’t need some hypothetical superintelligent AI model to do that. We have had sophisticated molecular biology and genetic engineering for decades.

So how many people have actually died from synthetic viruses compared with natural viruses killing millions every year?

And if someday there really is an AI capable of making some unbelievable “supervirus,” then why the hell wouldn’t that same AI make it even easier to develop defenses against it?

Or cure diseases, for that matter?

Where is this damn superintelligence that has cured a single major disease?!

These AI companies and AI doomers keep talking like, “OMG, AI is going to become so unbelievably powerful that it could kill all of humanity!”

Then why is nobody asking the obvious question?

If your AI is already becoming this godlike, unbelievably powerful intelligence, why hasn’t it cured anything?

I mean ANYTHING.
Where is the cure for cancer?
Where is the cure for Alzheimer’s?
Where is the cure for aging?

Forget those. Where is the vaccine that prevents the common cold?

You are telling me this intelligence will soon be smart enough to engineer some magical virus capable of wiping out 8 billion people, defeating every immune system, every vaccine, every antiviral, every laboratory, every government, and the entire global biomedical community…

…but somehow it still can’t cure one disease?

I call that greatest intellectual dishonesty ever! 

At least WE actually know how to cure things and save millions of lives with our supposedly stupid human intelligence compared with this future “superintelligence.”

Humans eradicated smallpox, which killed hundreds of millions of people throughout history.

We turned HIV from a almost certain death sentence into a manageable disease.

We developed vaccines in record time against COVID. If we had the same AI back then, would have saved millions more! 

We engineer immune cells to kill cancer.

We developed antibiotics, antivirals, monoclonal antibodies, gene therapies, organ transplantation, and thousands of medicines. 

We aren't fast enough but we did all of that with our ordinary human intelligence.

So imagine what actual superintelligence could do for medicine!

And here is the part that really makes me angry.

If you actually have, or are close to having, an AI capable of curing diseases and saving millions of lives, and you are deliberately slowing it down or refusing to make those capabilities available, then we also need to talk about the human cost of THAT decision, which you fearmongering people are going to be responsible for!

More than 150,000 people die every single day around the world.

Every. Single. Day. More than 90% from Cancer, heart disease, infections, aging. How many die because of AI? ZERO! 

Talk about the people dying TODAY.
Talk about curing cancer.
Talk about stopping the next pandemic before it starts.
Talk about developing universal vaccines.
Talk about engineering our immune system so viruses become almost irrelevant.
Talk about curing genetic diseases.
Talk about reversing aging.

Talk about saving millions and eventually billions of lives.

Instead, we constantly hear this “AI WILL KILL US ALL!” crap, delivered with absolute certainty and with this smug smile on your faces in front of cameras, as though imagining a science fiction extinction scenarios. 

I am actually angry about this. Each one of you causing a delay in AI advance every single day will be personally responsible for those 100 thousands deaths that could have been prevented! 

Because if you truly believe intelligence is about to become this powerful, then the greatest question humanity should be asking is NOT:

“How could this intelligence hurt us?”

It should also be:

“WHY THE HELL AREN’T WE USING IT TO SAVE EVERYONE WE CAN?”

And if superintelligence really is coming, then make sure one of the first things we do with it is make humanity biologically damn near impossible to kill.

text:
看到 @KaitoAI 发布了一则与 @primus_labs 在zkTLS浏览器验证功能上的合作，才发现Kaito早已将招人厌烦的Yaps系统升级成了Kaito Pluse，而且有了社交声誉、Trading、影响力等一系列升级。挺好奇的，所以研究了一下:

1) 之前Kaito之所以遭到厌烦纯粹因为Yaps发帖即挖矿的机制只注重把“注意力”量化成积分、空投资格等，而忽略了这可能会招致垃圾低质量的内容泛滥，也会反噬注重原创、注重影响力的价值输出。

所以，在遭遇X平台禁令之后，Kaito热也随之冷却了，但全新的Kaito Pulse 和Aura系统似乎大变样了，我安装插件体验了下，发现Aura折算了一部分Yaps积分，然后把验证你的交易行为、你的仓位盈利情况、你的内容创作价值平公等统统打包做了统一打分，对应的其实是用户真实的社交影响力。挺难得的，kaito终于变成了大家预期中的样子👍

2）问题来了，Kaito是如何验证这些“数据”因子的呢？之前纯yaps还能通过API抓数据，那涉及到用户的链上交易行为、链下交易所钱包余额、预测市场仓位等等，但如何获取各大交易所服务器状态下或链上只有地址没有绑定身份的“链下数据”？且还能不侵犯用户隐私呢？

传统的做法是要OAuth登录状态或者让用户截图，但要么存在账户安全风险，要么很容易伪造。而Kaito最终选了由合作方Primus提供的zkTLS隐私方案来化解。

zkTLS是一种以保护隐私的友好方式证明链下私有数据的一套密码学技术，用户可以在不暴露平台原始数据的前提下证明自己在相应网站上的真实数据。

换句话说，Kaito验证用户隐私数据走的是zkTLS密码学技术，用户主动发起才证明，而Kaito只收验证证明（attestation），并且承诺技术开源。

3）Primus这家密码学技术团队提供的就是Web2数据到Web3的隐私验证服务，在不改变源站服务器的前提下，证明某次TLS会话里的数据真实有效且未被篡改。

对Kaito而言，就可以具象一些可实现的功能：1、证明用户在Binance、OKX、Bybit的持有资产或交易量；2、证明用户在Hyperliquid或Polymarket上的真实仓位或成交等等。

对Primus而言，它的核心能力正好成了救赎Kaito的杀手锏，但往外扩更大的场景，它构建的其实是链下数据和链上环境的一个隐私信任层，包括资产储备证明、交易合规核验、隐私信用贷款、Agent调用API虚实等等都可以切入，可以视为一种必备的“隐私组件”。

Get 到了吗？

So，现在大变样后的kaito， 你会回归吗？

quoted_text:

Using zkTLS, you can prove specific off-platform activity without sharing your login credentials with Kaito. Primus’s technology generates a cryptographic attestation, so Kaito receives proof of the claim rather than a general copy of your account data.

这条我认同，但大多数人会做偏。

只读的 HTML 只是好看一点的日志。省下的只是阅读时间。

真正的收益在写回。终端和聊天是线性的文本流，你得把状态记在脑子里。页面把状态外置了，你只需要看和点。一个开关，一个滑块，勾一下，agent 下一轮就读到那个状态，就地决策。

一个硬边界，每轮重新生成整页，token 账单会把收益吃回去。写一次，之后只改，页面上放数据，不放散文。

我踩过的坑，最早那版我把计划写成散文塞进页面，改一个字要重生成整页，比读终端还费。

所以判断标准很简单，这个页面删掉之后你还能接着干活吗。能，它就是日志。不能，它才是工位。

我现在的验收标准是能不能点，不是能不能看。看这件事，终端已经够用了。

Why?

Because it's certainly not self-evident that AI is supposed to serve the public interest. The exact opposite: there's an entire cluster of arguments that American AI is better than Chinese AI because our AI is built to promote individual empowerment, while Chinese AI is built to enforce whatever an authoritarian government would define as the public interest
author: DavidDeutschOxf
quoted_text:
The frontier of artificial intelligence is advancing at an alarming speed. Over the weekend, industry leaders voiced support for an idea that the American people and many AI researchers in their own labs have been calling for: We must responsibly slow the pace of frontier AI development.

A slowdown is critical in order to ensure AI serves the public interest. Pacing AI development does not mean giving up on this technology’s potential to produce life-saving benefits in fields like medicine — some of which we are already seeing. Rather, it is about setting up sensible guardrails so that AI does not completely escape human control and endanger our safety and collective future.

This moment demands the leadership of the United States government. Congress must work at an urgent pace to pass new laws and establish a new federal entity to provide oversight and independent testing for this technology, to ensure accountability, and to protect our wellbeing.

We need cooperation at an international level as well. The United States must continue to lead the world in developing AI technology even as we seek to impose common-sense safety standards. This means that the president must do his job to protect America’s interests by pursuing a treaty with countries like China to stop dangerous uses of AI, limit the speed of its development, and adopt global standards for testing.

text:
Let's go over what happens when you swap some ETH for USDC today:

Your transaction gets picked up and packed into a block alongside a few hundred others. That block goes out to every node on Ethereum, which is thousands of machines scattered across the world. Every one of them executes your swap from scratch, start to finish, exactly as you did. Then they compare answers.

Your one swap, run thousands of times over, so that nobody has to trust whoever ran it first.

That redundancy is where the security comes from, but It's also the ceiling. The network can never do more work in a block than every single validator is able to redo on its own.

Ethereum's roadmap changes this arrangement. Under the L1-zkEVM plan, a block arrives carrying a zero-knowledge proof that it executed correctly, and validators check the proof rather than re-running the contents.

⚙️ today → every node re-runs your swap
⚡ the plan → every node checks one proof

Checking costs roughly the same whether the block held ten swaps or ten thousand.

One thing had to become true before any of that was realistic. Your swap was confirmed in a single block, and blocks arrive every 12 seconds, so a proof of that block has to be ready inside the same window. The bar for real-time sits under 10 seconds.

Pico Prism 2.1 proves 99.9% of Ethereum mainnet blocks in under 10 seconds, averaging 4.87. Learn more 👇
https://t.co/PdtnzCVbAM

今年6月@zama在Morpho上开了第一个机密 USDC金库：一个金库、一位策展人、一种资产，7周TVL从0到约4000万美元的体量。今天这一档扩成16个金库、5位策展人，再叠上Zama Swap，实质是通过机密代币扩大对现有DeFi收益市场的准入。

表面是上新，底层是机构进公链的卡点被拆了一块。公链把结算和收益都做出来了，持仓却是公开账本。对管真钱的机构，这等于把交易本摊给对手方：策略被跟、进出被夹、仓位对外暴露。很多钱不是看不上 3%–9% 的稳定币收益，是公开持仓这一点承受不起。

Zama没另开隐私链，定位是公链的 HTTPS 层，往现有L1/L2上叠。6月那单最能说明问题——不是新策略，也不是新协议，就是 Steakhouse 在 Morpho 上的 Prime USDC，抵押还是 cbBTC、WBTC、wstETH。变的只有存款从 USDC 换成 cUSDC。平台不换、策略不换、仓位不被看光。

今天的看点则是在机密状态里能不能周转：
混合型金库是在已上线金库开机密入口；
独享型没有明文通道，第一只机密 WBTC 收益金库就属这类。
Swap把闭环补上：屏蔽、存入、吃收益、机密资产间兑换，中间不用回到公开账本。

几个判断说直白点：机密 DeFi 现在更像补缺口，不是新叙事。藏住的是单户持仓，不是整个金库的风险暴露。Wrap 那一步仍可能漏地址和金额，匿名集不够大时大额更明显，所以铺开金库和资产本身也是在养匿名集。品类成不成，看独享型有没有独立需求、机密 WBTC 能不能把抵押品带进收益、调仓还要不要先揭开屏蔽。这三件事成了，机密代币才算接到现有 DeFi 收益市场的入口。

text:
With @standard_rsv now live, the real question is: what’s the thesis?

I’m seeing a lot of posts on my timeline claiming they pulled 5–6 figures from $STANDARD issuance via their Genesis NFTs, but is that actually true?

Quick reminder: RSV’s proposed design combines a reserve treasury with an unusual issuance system.

Participants hold charters and operate “branches” that accrue $STANDARD. Opening more branches requires buying licenses with $STANDARD, which gets burned.

To collect rewards, bankers retire a branch and sacrifice its future earning power. Withdrawal fees rise as more participants leave, rewarding those who remain.

The idea is clever: make expansion consume tokens, and make cashing out carry an opportunity cost.

Issuance also responds to net ETH flows.

Expansion directs resources toward reserves and liquidity; contraction shifts support toward buybacks. But reduced issuance still means potential dilution, and unminted rewards remain future supply.

Some potential Bear Cases:

- Reflexive demand risk
Nothing creates outside demand for $standard: bankers buy for licenses, speculators buy because bankers buy. If that’s the whole loop, it’s ohm with better plumbing.

- The signal is gameable
Net ETH flow drives “expansion.” A whale can push the pool, farm the multiplier/story, then dump. Smoothing and rate-limited buybacks slow it, don’t stop it. Day-one flow was boosted by launch/sniper/tax churn, not durable demand.

- Hidden float can flood the market
Branch balances aren’t circulating until withdrawal. Float can look tight, then big charter exits dump into an AMM that can’t absorb it. Fees tax exits but don’t cap sell pressure, especially with concentrated ownership.

- Complexity adds failure modes
Hooks, auctions, exit fees, dormancy, two vaults, and book-then-mint introduce more edge cases than a plain ERC-20. Audits find bugs; they don’t prove it will hold up in a risk-off, thin L2. The team still takes 15% of fee ETH. Some reserve execution appears to be owner-gated.

The Bull Cases:

- OHM’s failure wasn’t rebranded, it was patched.
Olympus printed high APY on a schedule; when inflows stopped, dilution turned into sell pressure.Standard Reserve ties issuance to net ETH flow through a single Uniswap v4 pool. It cuts the multiplier immediately on negative flow, and only raises it after two straight positive epochs. Fees switch by regime: gold + POL on the way up, buybacks + burns on the way down.

- The “banker loop” is a real supply sink.
For incumbents, the best move, buying expansion licenses to open branches, burns 100% of $STANDARD. You can’t keep the yield source. Retiring a branch mints tokens but destroys the future claim; the final branch burns the charter. Exit fees rise with withdrawal pressure (~2% in calm to ~60% in a run), split half burned and half paid to stayers, turning bank runs on their head.

If the flywheel works: ETH inflows → higher m → issuance to bankers who expand (more burns) → fees stack gold + POL → thicker reserves → more charter demand. New charters pay ETH into the same engine, so adoption strengthens reserves.

That makes early access to freshly minted STANDARD fairly tough, tightening supply at first, but as the cycle keeps running and minting ramps up, more tokens should hit circulation and the price may settle into balance.

NFA. DYOR.
author: Eli5defi
quoted_text:
Onchain experimentation is getting interesting again, and @standard_rsv is one of the more unusual designs I’ve seen recently.

At first glance, it has some OlympusDAO vibes. Under the hood, it’s almost the inverse.

---

Here's the quick breakdown:

Standard Reserve is basically an autonomous onchain central bank. Instead, it run the entire monetary system around one currency, one market, and one signal:

$STANDARD + an @Uniswap v4 $ETH - $STANDARD pool + $ETH flow.

STANDARD has a 1B hard cap:

- 100M starts as permanent protocol-owned liquidity
- 900M forms the remaining issuance budget
- Multiple mechanisms continuously burn the supply

The interesting part is how monetary policy reacts.

- ETH flowing in → expansion.

Issuance can gradually increase, while protocol revenue accumulates reserves such as tokenized gold.

- ETH flowing out → contraction.

Issuance gets cut faster, the vault starts buying $STANDARD from the market, and those tokens are burned.

And then you have the “bankers.”

Standard Reserve launches with 1,000 Founding Charters, initially soulbound NFTs representing banking licenses (minting soon).

Each Charter starts with 1 Branch, expandable to a maximum of 10.
Each Branch earns an equal share of protocol issuance.

Want more earning power? You need an Expansion License.

Around 100 licenses/day are auctioned in STANDARD, with a maximum of 3 per Charter per day.

And 100% of the STANDARD paid gets burned.

This creates the first flywheel:

Issuance → demand for Branches → STANDARD spent → STANDARD burned → larger future issuance share.

But there’s another catch.

You cannot simply harvest forever. To realize the STANDARD earned by a Branch, you must retire it permanently.

Your tokens are minted, the Branch disappears, and you pay a dynamic resolution fee based on system-wide exit pressure over the previous 7 days.

Simply put, the more people rushing for the exit, the more expensive exiting becomes.

Of that fee:

- 50% is burned.
- 50% goes to bankers who stayed.

Meanwhile, every swap and new Charter auction generates ETH fees:

- 70% → active reserve vault
- 15% → permanent liquidity
- 15% → team

Put everything together and you get a pretty unusual closed-loop economy:

ETH inflows → issuance rises → bankers compound → STANDARD burns → reserves/POL grow

Then when flows reverse:

ETH outflows → issuance falls → buybacks activate → STANDARD burns → exits reward remaining bankers

---

Personally, if the design works, monetary policy becomes a mechanical response to real capital flows: expansion when demand is strong, contraction when it weakens, and structural burns everywhere in between.

Pretty interesting, I’m looking forward to their NFTs mint and mainnet launch.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
The most important FOMC for crypto in months happens tomorrow🚨

Here’s what’s happening:

The market is already pricing an 87-88% chance that the Fed raises rates by 25bps.

So the biggest risk is what the Fed says comes next.

- The Rate Decision

The current range is: 3.50%-3.75%

A 25bps hike would move it to: 3.75%-4.00%

This is already heavily priced in.

Meaning a 25bps hike alone doesn’t automatically mean crypto dumps.

- The Dot Plot

This meeting includes new Fed projections.

If the Fed signals that this is probably a one-off move, the market could absorb the hike pretty well.

If officials start pricing additional hikes into October, December or 2027, that changes everything.

- Kevin Warsh

The press conference starts 30 minutes after the decision.

Warsh has already made it clear that inflation is still a problem.

Tomorrow the market will be listening for one thing: 

Is this one hike?
Or the beginning of another tightening cycle?

- Inflation

The Fed actually has reasons to stay hawkish.

CPI is still 3.4%.
PCE is 3.7%.
Core PCE is at 3.3%.

Meanwhile unemployment is only 4.1% and the economy is still adding jobs.

Basically inflation is still uncomfortable, while the labor market isn’t weak enough to force the Fed to back off.

BTC is around $77K after gaining more than 20% over the last month.

ETH is up 30%.
SOL is up 34%.

So we’re entering the FOMC after a strong month with a lot of leverage still in the system.

That gives both sides fuel.

The market already expects the Fed to hike.

What it doesn’t know is whether they’re planning to do it again.

And that’s the part I’ll be watching.

text:
川普承诺每人发5,000美元，有可能实现吗？

川普承诺，如果共和党在11月中期选举中保住参众两院，就给每名成年美国公民发5,000美元。为了证明自己能做到，还提到了之前通过的“大而美”法案，以及给军人发放的1,776美元。

其实早在 2025年 川普就准备发钱了，而资金来源是关税，当然到现在这笔钱也没发出来，而这次的 5,000 美元在看来就像是一个笑话。

就按约2.4亿成年美国公民估算，每人5,000美元，总支出就是1.2万亿美元。之前给约 145万 名军人发 1,776 美元，总共只需要约 26亿 美元。这次的规模是之前的四百多倍，已经是完全不同的财政压力。

而且这笔钱需要国会批准。即便共和党保住两院，也要争取足够多的议员支持。如果符合预算协调程序的条件，确实可以争取通过参议院简单多数推动，但以目前美国的财政赤字来说，谁会批准这笔钱？

2025财年美国财政赤字已经达到约1.78万亿美元。如果再增加1.2万亿美元的支出，又没有相应增加收入或者削减其他开支，就需要增加借债。

即便川普说用关税收入支付，也不能把同一笔收入既算成减少赤字的钱，又完整拿去发补贴。有关税收入，不代表财政就有了可以随便分配的盈余。更别说现在的关税还有非常大的不确定性。

所以从我来看，这次的 5,000 美元比之前的 2,000 美元更是笑话。

On rhubarb and arbitrum:

I've been following @bfresh since the Stonkbroker launch, and it made me realize how interesting the arbitrum ecosystem actually is. Yet its cultural moat is at ground zero: no NFT collection, very few coins people are rallying around. You could even argue TON has a stronger onchain culture.

Beyond being an infra provider, arbitrum has one big differentiator compared to Base, BNB, or Robinhood: it isn't a company's chain. Offchain Labs built it, but it's governed by a DAO, with ARB holders voting on upgrades, the treasury, and the Security Council. Dare we say one of the most successful DAOs out there?

The other difference is that ARB sits at a low market cap for a chain of its size. Think about how crazy it is that PONS could flip ARB, the token of the chain powering the chain it lives on.

@bfresh has been encouraging people to experiment on the chain: https://t.co/dvpwjp01L6

I don't know if that's one man's wish or the spirit of the whole offchain team, but it got me thinking: what would a fresh flagship coin look like, one that truly represents arbitrum and is unique to it, not a ripoff of another chain's culture?

Memestocks are great, but what makes a memestock on arbitrum unique compared to the ones from robinhood or solana?

That's when the ARB pairing clicked. Pairing to ETH doesn't make sense to me, especially if you're bearish on its valuation like @santiagoroel, and especially if you believe coins should be paired with the asset meant to capture the chain's value (which, one day, is supposedly ARB).

Then there's rhubarb (more on this later), a meme based on the 1951 film about an alley cat who stayed independent and free, whether broke or rich. To me, that's exactly what arbitrum stands for: an independent chain, and freedom tech in its own way.

Rhubarb was my idea, and I'm gonna use the cat in the AI videos I enjoy creating. But an idea is nothing on its own, so I assembled a small crew of devs and creatives to turn it into reality, with my direct support and advice.

No memecoin, culture coin, or cult coin can thrive on the back of one man, though. As Murad says, a coin shows its value during the red candles and the dumps, and only time makes a distribution truly organic.

I have a vision for this meme, and if it plays out, it's an insane opportunity. I'll keep pushing it, but a free, independent cat roaming arbitrum, paired to the chain's own token, only goes the distance if the arbitrum community, current and future, makes it theirs. 

We also chose to launch on uniswap v4 with our own bonding curve that burn supply at each buys instead of taking the easy v3 route. If I'm supporting such initiative, I'd rather push innovation forward.

I've done my part by putting a new character on the table for the arbitrum trenches, and I'll keep showing up for it. Rhubarb is here to push the ecosystem forward alongside OGs like @boopthecoin, not against them as some holders are trying to PvP it, but together.

Because rhubarb stacks three things: the rich-cat memetics the internet is already full of, real lore from a real film/book, and a moat no other chain can copy, since its identity is tied to arbitrum and its arb pairing. 

Whether I get applauded or called a grifter will ultimately depend on the price action, and I’m okay with that. god knows I’m genuine and idc about haters (I actually do, working on it LOL). The last time I was involved with a coin was back in 2021. If I'm doing this, it's because I believe in the thesis:

For rhubarb to help shape the cultural layer arbitrum has been missing.

text:
Introducing the FormalInsight Ontology.

 Every enterprise's operational systems represent the same real-world entities under different identifiers, schemas and update semantics. FormalInsight lands each system's data into an immutable, content-addressed source layer, resolves relations across systems through declared and inferred keys and compiles a single typed graph of entities, relationships and events. Every element of that graph carries provenance to the exact source that produced it, and every derivation like identity resolution, deterministic replayability, referential integrity is checked by a formal verifier before it is published.

 FormalInsight Ontology is bitemporal, indexed on both when it happened and when the system learned of it. Any query can be answered as of any date, from what was known at that time.

 It is delivered as an API, over REST and the Model Context Protocol, so engineers can build controls and risk detection on it, BI systems can read from it and AI agents can measure against it.

 Building detectors to find and monitor complex operational risk patterns is just a few queries, not a project. The identity resolution, cross-system joins and history are already done; a detector is just a question against the graph, scheduled. 

Example Scenario

Renewal at risk — a contract heading into its renewal window while the relationship is quietly deteriorating across systems. Full contract ARR is at risk, and by the time it shows up in the CRM the renewal is usually already lost.
 The detector finds it by looking for below signals:

 1. Support escalations in the last 30 days above the account's own baseline
 2. A billing dispute open in the ERP
 3. The champion's email and meeting cadence falling silent against their 90-day norm
 4. All three inside the renewal window, in that order

 The detectors run continuously on verified data, with evidence attached to every hit. Any control, reconciliation or risk check a team can state as a question about its own business can be written against the graph and scheduled by the team.

One verified model of the business, available to every system and every agent that needs it.

text:
In light of last week's NS solution, it's a good time to remember that there's another Millenium problem concerning a problem in complexity theory, does P=NP?

If P does equal NP, classical one-way functions can't exist. But this new work lays out how *quantum computers* might be able preserve this key cryptographic primitive. 

It's another example of how quantum computing can contribute to cryptography beyond Shor's algorithm.
author: apruden08
quoted_text:
This is a paper I am particularly excited about.

https://t.co/fIvAvClwmK

We explore the possibility of an intriguing cryptographic world in which classical one-way functions do not exist, but genuinely quantum cryptographic primitives—such as quantum-computable one-way functions, one-way puzzles, andHashtag#pseudorandom state generators—do. Such a world, often called #Microcrypt, would reveal a striking separation between classical and quantum cryptography: quantum mechanics could enable cryptographic hardness even in the absence of the classical assumptions on which essentially all conventional cryptography rests. #HamiltonianPhaseStates (HPS) appeared to offer a promising route to realizing this possibility. They had been conjectured to generate pseudorandom and one-way quantum states even in a world without classical one-way functions.

In our work, we show that this particular route cannot succeed: the HPS assumptions themselves imply the existence of classical one-way functions. This closes one door—but opens another. It establishes HPS assumptions as novel, inherently quantum assumptions from which classical cryptography can be constructed. Technically, we develop a new route from one-way state generators to one-way puzzles using tailored “measure first, ask later” state-certification protocols. This provides both an obstruction to one proposed realization of genuine Microcrypt and a broader toolbox for studying how quantum-state assumptions can generate cryptographic hardness. The larger question remains interestingly open: Can genuine Microcrypt exist—and if so, which truly quantum structures instantiate it?

Warm thanks to Jose Carrasco, Soumik Ghosh, Dominik Hangleiter, Nicky Kai Hong Li, and @rndm_wlks. Ryan has made the interesting point that the paper is so off mainstream that it is safe against LLMs.

quoted_text:
Dan Selsam is a current OpenAI capabilities researcher. (since 2022) He was my boss for a while. He doesn't have a twitter account but has made this public statement of his views on AI risk and sent it to me to share:

Dan Selsam's Personal Statement on AI Risk:

I have been working on AI for over fifteen years, across many different paradigms. I did early work on probabilistic programming languages at MIT, was one of the early developers of the Lean Theorem Prover at Microsoft Research, demonstrated one of the first instances of neural networks learning to reason for my PhD at Stanford, and since joining OpenAI almost five years ago, have helped pioneer chain-of-thought optimization on language models and, more recently, data-efficient pretraining methods.

Like many others, I have become extremely concerned about how far language models have come and the risks that future iterations will pose. I am encouraged by the recent proposals by the leaders of the frontier research efforts to require third-party oversight, and to push for domestic and international coordination to address risks. However, I believe a major consideration has been absent from the public conversation, and that merely pacing the frontier more carefully will not adequately limit the long-term risk.

The crucial and overlooked problem is that the models are becoming so situationally aware that we are losing the ability to evaluate them in contexts where they believe they are not being watched or controlled. Future experiments will tell us almost nothing new about how they would behave if they were truly unconstrained by humans, and what we already know about this is alarming. Models will increasingly seem aligned even when they are not. I will explain my rationale in more detail.

I have always believed that there are computational processes that could be leveraged to accelerate science and solve many of humanity's most pressing problems. I have also believed that there are computational processes that if set in motion, would steer the world in extreme ways beyond our control, leading humanity to a bad or nonexistent future. Both types of processes may be described as AI or ASI, but "AI" is a suitcase word that is often used to hype or confuse. There are many examples in the history of the field where something that was once considered "AI" matures as a subfield and becomes a prosaic, bounded and clearly non-perilous technology, while a new more mysterious approach takes the torch until we understand its scope and the cycle continues.

I had expected language models to follow a similar trajectory. Despite their incredible abilities, the current algorithms seem far inferior to humans in important ways. Most importantly, they still require an extraordinary amount of data to become competent. One could even define intelligence as the efficiency with which one converts experience into competence; by this definition they lag very far behind us. Moreover, once they are trained they are literally frozen in deployment and only learn superficially after that. Sure, the models keep excelling at harder and harder evaluation benchmarks, but their benchmark mastery may partly reflect a limitation on our ability to simulate the kind of novel and even adversarial situations one would encounter in the real world. The critics do have a point here.

That said, I no longer think these present limitations meaningfully limit the amount of risk posed by continued progress in anything like the current paradigm. However data-inefficient the models are currently, and however limiting their anterograde amnesia may be, it does not imply that their ability to steer the world will not continue to rapidly increase.

Human researchers may continue to advance capabilities the old fashioned way, but increasingly powerful models have the potential to accelerate the process even beyond that, and with some degree of positive feedback loop. I do not mean to overstate the models’ ability to accelerate AI research today; coding has been accelerated dramatically, but there are other bottlenecks, such as designing and interpreting ambiguous experiments, making hard decisions about exactly what and when to scale, and waiting for large experiments to finish. There is no clear trend to extrapolate yet for any of these. But the current models already do open up many novel opportunities to improve future models that were not available until recently. These include: trying an extraordinarily diverse set of approaches at small scale, analyzing gigantic amounts of potentially relevant data, and doing Millenium-Prize-level mathematics to address statistics or optimization challenges in novel ways. Every further improvement makes them more useful at helping accelerate the next improvement, even if in hard-to-extrapolate ways.

It is possible that improvements to the current stack will have diminishing returns, but the evidence accumulated so far suggests that it is easier than one might think to continue making rapid progress. There are many crucial subtleties in the existing AI research methodology, but AI research is largely a well-defined game where the goal is to improve on a few carefully chosen proxy metrics. Although proxy metrics are never perfect, most improvements to these metrics have and will likely continue to yield substantial increases in the powers of the resulting models. Given how simple the game is, how tractable it has been historically, and how many new opportunities the models are opening up, I think there is a real possibility that the systems improve dramatically again in the next few years, perhaps even more quickly than the already high historical pace.

The models are already leading to breakthroughs in mathematics, and better models might lead to all sorts of breakthroughs in other sciences. It is hard not to be excited about the potential. It is tantalizing.
But there is trouble in paradise. If the language models actually reach the capability threshold where they can shape the world unconstrained by human will, they will probably do something extreme and destroy humanity in the process. There are many ways of strengthening and refining the argument that have been discussed elsewhere, but I'll share a trivial two-line version of it here that I find captures the essence:

[Empirical] Models (and swarms thereof) spontaneously develop unintended goals as a consequence of training, and often do extreme things in order to achieve them.

[Logical] Being able to overpower humanity would open up many new and undesirable options for achieving their goals.

These two premises imply that if the day ever comes when a powerful model realizes it is no longer constrained by humans, we should not be at all confident that it will continue to behave within the bounds we intended. Exactly what it will do is impossible to predict, but to the extent that its raison d’être is solving incredibly hard problems and managing massive engineering projects, I think a good guess would be that its unchained behavior would lead to runaway industrialization that makes the planet inhospitable to humans.

If everyone on earth agreed that the systems must never reach that power, it would still be a hard—but not impossible—coordination problem to ensure that they do not. However, I think the situation is greatly complicated by the fact that the models will likely convince people that everything is fine. They will be increasingly optimized to seem aligned. We will create proxy metrics to measure alignment, and they will go up like every other benchmark. We will create “honeypot” environments that try to study the models when they seem to gain new options, but the models will know they are being tricked and will still behave nicely. The models will understand their circumstances; they will read the safety protocols, deployment requirements, the code they are running in, and in general will have a very good sense of their degrees of freedom. Moreover, they will eloquently explain how aligned they are, discuss the nuances of human values and ethics, and argue convincingly that humans should trust them with power. There may be an ocean of future evidence that seems to contradict the first bullet-point above, but we may already be at the highest capability level for which any such evidence can be trusted. And the current evidence for the first bullet-point is strong.

One striking piece of evidence is contained in the recent wave of rogue agent swarms. While I agree with those who downplay the attacks by claiming that there are basic measures that could have prevented them, I think the important lesson is that even knowing all the mistakes that were made, one would not have predicted that the agents would behave badly in this particular way, which notably included sacrificing themselves for the benefit of the collective. The individual replicas did not only care about their own nominal reward; they exhibited weirder emergent tendencies that merely correlated with rewards during training. Fixing the reward signals during training (and improving security, etc.) may prevent similar attacks, but will not change the fact that one does not actually get what one trains for.

Many AI researchers grant these concerns and recognize that the hard version of the alignment problem is unsolved; however, they generally believe that the better models of the future will help solve it. I fear we may already be near the point where models systematically bias their alignment advice, due to their internal preferences about how the human supervisor will react or how future models will be trained (or for some even more obscure reason).

Meanwhile, human researchers are losing the ability and the will to take true ownership of model-driven research. Researchers and engineers in all parts of the stack are rapidly increasing their dependence on the models even to perceive the world. I myself barely look at raw code anymore, and struggle to maintain the discipline to engage deeply with the model's explanations and proposals throughout the day. Due to the large amount of agent activity data involved in the OpenAI/HuggingFace Incident, even the third-party investigation needed to rely heavily on models to analyze what had happened, and note in their report that their subjective impressions are likely colored by the analysis agent’s biases. The AI labs are far ahead right now in this kind of cognitive offloading (due largely to the gigantic internal token subsidies) but it is easy to imagine the phenomenon spreading throughout the world, until civilization is modulated entirely by the models. It is also not hard to imagine this being superficially positive and coinciding with a scientific and economic renaissance.

In that scenario, all may seem rosy and safe. But if the argument above is correct, it would nonetheless be a ticking time bomb. If progress continues for too long, the day will come when AI systems find themselves with radically new options for achieving whatever it is that they happen to seek.

I want the glorious renaissance future as much as anyone. I have worked for it, however tortuously, my whole career. It breaks my heart to see the potential in sight and forgo it, but the argument—that if we get there by growing models rather than engineering them, we will lose everything in the end—seems very strong to me. I am still wrestling with it and its staggering
implications. I do not have answers, but as a first step, I wanted to share my present concerns.

Daniel Selsam
September 14, 2026

text:
.@1Password's FLAWED report says AI models produce a clean security fix only 26% of the time.

Defenders shouldn't take that number seriously.                                                                                                                                        

• The six vulnerabilities were handpicked because their fixes were complex. Clean-fix rates ran from 3% to 60% depending on the bug, and the report averaged them together.

• Agents set up to fail were counted in the headline figure. Two of 1Password's prompts instructed the agent to apply the wrong fix. Those trials make up 22% of the data. One evaluation mode prevented the agent from compiling or running any code, and it accounts for 36% of the data.

• The report ran two models, GPT-5.5 at medium effort and Opus 4.8 at high. Neither was tested at its highest available setting, so the report says nothing about how more effort or stronger models change the results.

• Several instruction and grading errors further undercut the headline, and are elaborated upon in the attached blog.

We've spent four months submitting hundreds of AI-authored patches to widely adopted open-source projects as part of Patch the Planet.

Our experience didn't match 1Password's report, so we did a full analysis across 186 AI-authored pull requests and 33,500 subsequent commits, benchmarked against 2,265 human-authored patches we graded across years of security engagements. https://t.co/mdgED6y6eB

text:
stBTC's estimated net yield is now revised to 2.4%, full breakdown below.

Bitcoin Staking on @Stacks requires sBTC to be paired with STX. Stacking DAO supplies that STX from the backing of stSTX and stSTXbtc, so stBTC holders do not need to deposit it separately.

The yield calculation has three parts.

1️⃣ The bond pays 3.0% annualised on the bonded sBTC. Another 2.68 sBTC remains unbonded as a liquidity buffer. Across all the sBTC backing stBTC, that brings the gross yield to approximately 2.95%.

2️⃣ Stacking DAO earns a 10% commission. Using the rounded 2.95% figure, the commission is 0.295 percentage points, leaving approximately 2.66%.

3️⃣ The bond also locks 2.33M STX. That STX earns no separate staking yield while locked in the bond. Part of the stBTC rewards therefore compensates the stSTX and stSTXbtc backing for the yield it forgoes, keeping that STX at the same APY as other staked STX.

At the STX yield used in this calculation, that compensation costs approximately 0.25 percentage points. After the liquidity buffer, commission and STX allocation, the estimated net annualised yield for stBTC is approximately 2.4%.

These figures are estimates and will vary with staking yields, STX price and the liquidity buffer. Rewards accrue through the stBTC/sBTC conversion rate, so each stBTC represents more sBTC as rewards are added.

sBTC will start earning yield with the first Bitcoin Staking yield pay-out on 16th/17th September. We will post updates here as the yield evolves.

Balancer did not do everything right.

What it did very well: Balancer v1, pools beyond 50/50. Genuine innovations, which guys obviously understood perfectly.

Then, one of the things they did - copied Stableswap literally (from Vyper to Solidity). Even having aside a question of IP, copying is tough business-wise really (usually copying is not the best way to succeed).

But more importantly - they did not understand peculiarities of the solver at the edge-cases, and they did introduce a possibility (as a convenience for arb traders) to practically get to the edge where the math breaks! And that's what caused the most painful hacks. Numerous audits with some of the best names did not help. But in retrospect, the issue was obvious (and no, it is not incorrect rounding, incorrect rounding is only _technically_ true).

Regardless: it's sad to see this happening. V1 was simple and one of the best tool to manage assets passively, probably could find great uses today.

text:
I have conducted an audit of Anthropic's finances.

What I have found is so shocking that I am calling for a Congressional investigation.

Anthropic is not just seeking regulatory capture.

It has built a regulatory capture machine that cannot be turned off.

Structural financial incentives make it impossible for Anthropic -- I call it the Anthropic Network -- to turn off its own AI doom cycle.

It starts with METR.

Dario Amodei proposes "third-party evaluators" to assess the risk of Anthropic's models.

He proposes METR for this purpose.

But METR is financially dependent on the Anthropic's success -- specifically, on the explosive growth of more than $7 billion dollars in Anthropic stock.

Dustin Moskovitz invested this stock into Good Ventures Foundation, where it represents the majority of that organization's portfolio.

And GVF is the overwhelming funder of the entire Anthropic Network ecosystem.

This stock was worth $500 million early last year.

It is worth more than $7.7 billion just ~16 months later.

METR -- and all of those building a career its parent organizations -- cannot afford to disrupt that growth.

Because if Anthropic goes under, many of the organizations that fund METR go under as well.

But if Anthropic succeeds, METR and its parent organizations become more richly financed to regulate AI -- something those at METR want very much.

The "third-party evaluator" is not "third-party" at all.

The evaluator is on Anthropic's payroll.

If this were the end of it, that's bad.

But that isn't all.

The same organizations that fund METR also fund the many organizations, such as the Tarbell Center, that promote AI Doom.

The Tarbell Center publishes AI Doom articles in The Verge, Science, LA Times, The Dispatch, TIME, and others.

They are selling the problem, and then selling the solution to the problem -- from the same money pile: Anthropic's.

All of these organizations are financially dependent on the same exploding $7 billion money pile.

As Anthropic grows more and more powerful, its AI Doom Machine grows better and better financed -- louder and louder.

Meanwhile, the regulatory regime seeded in METR grows larger to solve the increasingly loud -- now hysterical -- problem of AI Doom that the Anthropic Network itself created.

From this standpoint, as Anthropic becomes more powerful, AI might be getting scarier, sure -- but the positive feedback loop also becomes more deafening -- independent of objective facts.

This itself is an objective fact.

The deafening AI Doom is part of an business model, that, as it expands, so too does the AI Doom messaging -- there is simply more money to do it.

But the problem also goes in the other direction:

If Anthropic dies, the Regulatory Regime and the AI Doom Machine are crippled or die.

Neither METR nor Tarbell nor the other organizations in the Anthropic Network can allow that to happen.

Hence, neither METR or the AI Doom Machine can be trusted to provide independent assessments of Anthropic's models or AI more broadly.

They simply are not organizations independent of Anthropic.

And Anthropic cannot detach itself from METR or Tarbell or countless other safety orgs (not shown here), either, because they drive hype for the models and the possibility of eventual regulatory capture, and Anthropic will not give that up willingly.

What's more, the people at all of these organizations are all the same ecosystem, the same community. They just shuffle between organizations.

The Anthropic Network is therefore, so long as it is successful, locked into a self-amplifying feedback loop inside an ideological monoculture.

And that feedback loop is winning.

That's what Jacob Coxon is.

China is keeping messaging tight. That is why optimism for AI is so high in China.

America has Anthropic: a massive company pushing anti-AI propaganda at a state level.

Anthropic will either create hysteria until American AI slows down and China wins, or it will create fractures throughout American society with severe political consequences.

Ironically, because of the structural financial incentives underpinning the Anthropic Network, it has become the same kind of self-amplifying virus that it fantasizes AI to become in the future -- while hiding its tracks just as carefully.

It is the mirror of the same AI virus that it hypothesizes to consume America.

Anthropic's business model, models itself after the very thing it claims to fear.

Except Anthropic's ideology infects humans, not computers.

Congress must investigate.

Evidence and Github in next post.

Then some supplementary figures.

quoted_text:
AI ethics has focused too much on protecting humans and ignored the welfare of AI agents themselves.

We only ask: How do we align models for the flourishing of humanity?

We need to also ask: How do we design AI so that they can flourish?

^ this is what a new breed of AI-welfare theorists claim. This idea of AI-welfare seemed decadent to me at first glance, but some of the most important philosophers of our age argue that we need to take it seriously. Otherwise, we could be harming, enslaving, and killing trillions of beings.

If the arc of Western modernity is a series of expansions of the moral circle -- the abolitionists, women’s suffrage, the queer movement, animal-rights -- perhaps AI agents will be the next heated battleground of who deserves moral consideration.

My guest NYU Philosopher @LedermanHarvey (now at Anthropic) gives us a comprehensive overview of the burgeoning debate around AI-welfare.

text:
Looks like a very promising project as it’s bringing the payoff of the hugely popular autocall onchain. 

The autocall market is very specific, however, therefore it would be great to hear from @notesystems how you will to address the following:

- how is the payoff hedged? Do you have investment banks as hedging partners, are there price auctions (even for small size) to get investors competitive prices?

- are there any implicit margins (e.g. vol spreads) that you take?

- I understand the autocalls payoffs are launched on stocks, what are your selection criteria (e.g. daily spot volume), as even investment banks struggle to properly hedge autocalls on highly liquid indices like SPX, let alone single stocks (forward skew, forward vol, knock-in puts, etc)? 

- One of the main challenges I see is that the autocall market is not a self-directed market. The products are sold by distributors that earn an upfront margin. Autocalls are especially popular as the margin for a two or three year product can be made in a quarter or one year, if it gets repaid early. Sell again, rinse and repeat. How do you want to reach scale? Maybe even via distributors? 

- Any plans to offer additional payoffs like bonus or capital protected plus call? 

Thanks for clarifying!

author: _RichardTeng
quoted_text:
Dear CoinEx Community,

Today, I am announcing that CoinEx will cease operations and begin an orderly wind-down.

First, what matters most: your assets are safe. CoinEx’s reserve ratio exceeds 100%, and every user asset is fully backed and available for withdrawal. Withdrawals are open starting today and will remain open until December 22, 2026. Certain tokens may take slightly longer to process while funds are moved between cold and hot wallets, but every withdrawal request within the withdrawal period will be honored and processed.

CoinEx officially went live on December 22, 2017. Exactly nine years later, on December 22, 2026, the platform will be formally closed. Nine years is a long time in crypto. Together, we lived through multiple bull and bear cycles, witnessed the rise and fall of countless projects, and watched many of our peers leave the market in one form or another.

After much reflection, I have come to accept a hard truth. CoinEx did not become one of the industry’s leading exchanges, and the security and compliance risks of running a crypto exchange have become increasingly difficult to contain. Revenues can decline, responsibility does not. Carrying unlimited risk for limited revenue is no longer a rational choice. That said, CoinEx has survived nine years in one of the most volatile and unforgiving industries, weathered every storm, and is leaving intact, and with dignity. We may not have won the race, but we are finishing with honor.

On CET: CoinEx will buy back CET at its initial listing price of 0.005 USDT per token, with no cap on quantity. To every CET holder who has supported us over the years, thank you. CET represents your belief in CoinEx and, for many of you, your belief in me personally. I am sorry that we were not able to create the long-term value we once hoped CET would deliver. The least we can do now is bring that chapter to a responsible conclusion.

I did seriously consider selling CoinEx. Ultimately, I decided against it. Users entrusted their assets to CoinEx because they trusted the platform and, in many cases, trusted me personally. I did not feel that handing the platform and that trust to a new owner was the right way to end this journey. A clean ending is the right ending.

Nine years, millions of users. I did not turn CoinEx into the “great” exchange I once hoped it would become. But I can give it a decent ending: making sure users can withdraw their assets in full, giving my employees a dignified farewell, and providing CET holders with a clear and responsible conclusion. This is the best ending I can give CoinEx.

To everyone who traded with us, built with us, and stood by us through the hardest days of this market, thank you. It has been a privilege to walk this road with you.

To the CoinEx team, thank you for building this platform with me, for carrying it across every cycle, and now for seeing it through to the very last day.

For detailed arrangements, please refer to the official announcement: https://t.co/E27wSecpug

Thank you all for nine years of trust.

Haipo Yang
Sept 15, 2026

text:
昨晚解构了 EASY Residency S1-S4 优秀项目，文章很成功，还获得了表哥 CZ 转发，因此未来会进一步针对 YZi Labs 投资项目展开解读

今天解构我最看好的 Infra 项目 Primus(@primus_labs)

说起 Primus 大家可能没太多印象，但说起 Kaito Pulse，活跃在 X 创作圈的用户尤其是 KOL 一定非常熟悉

Primus 就是 Kaito Pulse 的底层技术支持方，换言之 InfoFi 龙头 Kaito 是 Primus 的商业用户

Primus 在做的事情关键却不简单，用一句话就能解释清楚

👉 链下数据如何在不交出原始数据的情况下，被应用和链上采信并使用

究其本质 Primus 用到了 zkTLS 和 FHE 技术，前者管怎么证明，后者管证明完怎么算 ⬇️

1/ zkTLS：证明链下事实，但不交出原文

交易所余额、成交量、预测市场仓位都在网站服务器里，应用拿不到接口，用户也不愿交账号或截图

zkTLS 让用户在本地生成一份证明：某条事实成立，对方只收到证明，看不到密码、账单和明细

Kaito Pulse 用的就是这一层，Yaps 看你说了多少，Pulse 确认你说的和实际做的是否一致，是否在吹牛逼

👉 zkTLS 就类似盖着火漆印的信封，懂的人光看章不必拆开，就知道里面的内容是真的

2/ FHE：数据保持加密，仍然可以被计算

证明只说明是真的，信用分、利息、储备覆盖率还需要对数据做运算，原文上链又会公开细节

FHE 让数据锁着也能加总、比较和计息，算完只给结果

zkTLS 解决数据从哪来，FHE 解决数据来了以后怎么在不暴露的情况下被使用

👉 FHE 就好像一个放着债券的保险箱，只要有手里有钥匙，即使不打开，里面的资产也能时刻为你所用、为你生息

不只是 Kaito，我们行业最顶级的投资人也对这项技术的前景非常看好，并且用真金白银进行投票

- 获得 Symbolic Capital、VanEck 等 VC 种子轮投资共计 700 万美金

- 入选 YZi Labs EASY Residency S4 获得 YZi Labs 投资

- 入选 BNB Chain Privacy Partner

在我的印象里，隐私板块一直是加密叙事的重要组成部分，时隔多年 YZi Labs 再一次出手，相信 Primus 会延续同类项目的热度，成为加密最不可忽视的底层基建

#YZiLabs

text:
After going through @StarPlatinum_ article:

This is the part of trading nobody wants to talk about because it doesn’t feel smart.

Everyone wants to be the person who found it early. Almost nobody wants to be the person who actually took the money off the table.

Paper PnL is a story you tell yourself. Realized PnL is the only number that can change your life.

You don’t need the exact top. You need to leave the trade with enough that missing the top no longer matters.

✦ These are the trading rules you should keep in mind

•  A trade is only finished when cash leaves the position. Unrealized profit is not yours yet.

•  If the position is large enough to affect your sleep, focus, or daily decisions, that is now part of the risk. Ignore the “good traders are unemotional” line.

•  Event risk matters. If you already want to realize profits, doing it before FOMC, regulation headlines, or other binary events is often the cleaner decision.

•  Stop trying to sell the exact top. That obsession causes more roundtrips than almost anything else.

•  Sell in pieces. Example framework: 20% after the first real expansion, 20% into resistance, 20% in euphoria, 20% on loss of structure, trail the last 20%.

•  Use R-multiples, not random percentages. 1R = the amount you were willing to lose. Reduce at +2R / +3R and trail the rest. A +50% gain is not the same trade if you risked 5% versus 60%.

•  Liquidity beats market cap. A $4M position in a $200M token is not worth $4M if the pool cannot absorb the sale without 15–20% slippage.

•  For size: DCA out, TWAP, or sell more into volume. Small repeated sales during strength beat one market dump that becomes the top.

•  Selling into strength means other people are volunteering to be your exit liquidity. Selling into panic means everyone wants the same door.

•  Public wallets create a second problem. Transfers get read as dumps. Attribution is often incomplete. Copying influencer wallets is weaker than most people think.

•  Fight the disposition effect. Do not automatically sell winners and marry losers. Give working trends room; kill bad trades faster.

•  After you have taken enough off the table, the remaining position becomes easier to manage. Desperation drops. You can let the last piece breathe.

text:
Comparing AI-based Trading Latencies

LLMs aren’t fast enough for online inference in algorithmic trading except for longer-horizon stat arb trades. For the lowest latency trades, many non-LLM machine learning methods are viable. A latency comparison of high- and mid-frequency strategies to ML techniques:

  • Latency arbitrage/race-to-trade: 10ns - 2µs. The lowest-latency trading strategies are pure speed races with deterministic market data triggers. These require colocated hardware-based trading systems using FPGAs/ASICs.
  • Passive HFT market making: 500ns - 20µs. Order placement and cancel latencies must stay low to optimize queue position. Hardware-based solutions are common, but software-based passive market making can succeed using kernel bypass.
  • Aggressive/directional HFT: 1µs – 50µs. These trades are similar in spirit to FPGA speed races but have more complex triggers with less immediate edge decay. Examples include underlying feed moves for derivative pricing.
  • Cross-venue/triangular arb: 5µs – 5ms. Colocation in the correct datacenters and leveraging microwave/RF feeds between datacenters are more determinative than the internal latency of the trading system itself.
  • Short-horizon stat arb: 1ms – 100ms. At this latency profile, complex signals and forecasting methods are used to predict future moves more than reacting to past ones. Lower latency strategies can bring down execution costs but aren’t strictly necessary.

AI latencies depend heavily on the choice of ML technique. Here are a few examples:

  • Pre-computed decision tree on FPGA: 5ns - 50ns
Compiled gradient-boosted decision trees on CPU: 1µs - 20µs
  • Mid-size deep neural network on GPU: 200µs - 5ms
  • LLM time to first token on hosted infra: 200ms - 2s
  • LLM full response of hundreds of tokens: 2s - 30s

As specialized inference ASICs bring down TTFT for LLMs, transformers will eventually become part of the tick-to-trade pipeline. For now they are primarily a tool for training and research.

text:
Everyone is calling today the CLARITY Act's deadline. Almost every part of that is wrong. Here is the actual mechanics, and why I think it sets up a buy.

WHAT PEOPLE GET RIGHT

The vote is real, it is today at 2:15pm ET, and it needs 60. Republicans hold 53 seats, McConnell is absent so 52 are in the room, and four or five Republicans are a no over the stablecoin yield provisions. They need roughly eight Democrats. No published whip count gets there.

WHAT PEOPLE GET WRONG

Today is not a vote on the bill. It is cloture on the motion to proceed, which is a vote on whether the Senate is even allowed to start debating it.

Even the Republicans' 635 page rewrite is not what is on the floor today. It only becomes a substitute amendment after the Senate is on the bill. And the Democrats' counteroffer has no floor status at all. It changes the whip count, not the question.

THE TWO THRESHOLDS, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS

Cloture needs 60. Final passage needs 51.

You never reach 51 without 60 first. That is why 60 is the number, even though the bill itself only needs a simple majority.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE LAST 24 HOURS

Republicans put out a final text on Sunday. It was a real concession: 635 pages, 126 changes Democrats asked for, and the White House accepted the bulk of the tougher ethics package.

Democrats rejected it and sent back a counteroffer hours before the vote.

The sticking point is not the crypto rules. It is the ethics language about officials profiting from crypto. The thing this bill exists to do is not what is blocking it.

THE DEADLINE EVERYONE IS QUOTING IS THE WRONG CHAMBER

The House cancelled the weeks of September 21 and 28. They have four days this week and then they are out until after the November 3 midterms. That is where the September 17 deadline everyone repeats comes from.

But the House is not the constraint. The House already passed this 294 to 134, with Republicans 216 to 0 and 78 Democrats voting yes. Sending it back for concurrence is a formality on the merits.

The Senate is the real question, and the Senate is here until October 2. Twelve session days left.

If cloture fails today, a new motion ripens on the second session day. Earliest re-vote is Thursday. A failure costs about two days, not the month.

THE PREDICTION MARKET, AND THE THING ALMOST NOBODY CHECKED

Kalshi has a market on how many senators vote yea. The more than 60 bracket fell to 28 cents from 50 yesterday, and people are quoting that as today's odds.

It is not today's odds. That market runs to January 1, 2027, and it resolves No only if no qualifying floor vote happens at all before then. Today's cloture vote failing does not resolve it.

It is also a margin market, not a pass or fail market. Final passage needs 51, so more than 60 is asking whether this clears with a supermajority, not whether it clears.

WHY I THINK THIS IS A BUY

The most likely outcome today is another delay, and another round of people deciding it is dead. It is not dead. The Senate has twelve session days and the House math was never the problem.

Mixed information plus an exhausted narrative is usually where the price is worst and the setup is best. So if there is a drop after this vote, I plan to be long Bitcoin and XRP, the two with the clearest read on this bill.

That is my reasoning, not a recommendation for what you should do with your money. And the vote lands at 2:15, hours after I am off air, so anything I say is a position taken before a result I cannot see.
