text:
With @standard_rsv now live, the real question is: what’s the thesis?

I’m seeing a lot of posts on my timeline claiming they pulled 5–6 figures from $STANDARD issuance via their Genesis NFTs, but is that actually true?

Quick reminder: RSV’s proposed design combines a reserve treasury with an unusual issuance system.

Participants hold charters and operate “branches” that accrue $STANDARD. Opening more branches requires buying licenses with $STANDARD, which gets burned.

To collect rewards, bankers retire a branch and sacrifice its future earning power. Withdrawal fees rise as more participants leave, rewarding those who remain.

The idea is clever: make expansion consume tokens, and make cashing out carry an opportunity cost.

Issuance also responds to net ETH flows.

Expansion directs resources toward reserves and liquidity; contraction shifts support toward buybacks. But reduced issuance still means potential dilution, and unminted rewards remain future supply.

Some potential Bear Cases:

- Reflexive demand risk
Nothing creates outside demand for $standard: bankers buy for licenses, speculators buy because bankers buy. If that’s the whole loop, it’s ohm with better plumbing.

- The signal is gameable
Net ETH flow drives “expansion.” A whale can push the pool, farm the multiplier/story, then dump. Smoothing and rate-limited buybacks slow it, don’t stop it. Day-one flow was boosted by launch/sniper/tax churn, not durable demand.

- Hidden float can flood the market
Branch balances aren’t circulating until withdrawal. Float can look tight, then big charter exits dump into an AMM that can’t absorb it. Fees tax exits but don’t cap sell pressure, especially with concentrated ownership.

- Complexity adds failure modes
Hooks, auctions, exit fees, dormancy, two vaults, and book-then-mint introduce more edge cases than a plain ERC-20. Audits find bugs; they don’t prove it will hold up in a risk-off, thin L2. The team still takes 15% of fee ETH. Some reserve execution appears to be owner-gated.

The Bull Cases:

- OHM’s failure wasn’t rebranded, it was patched.
Olympus printed high APY on a schedule; when inflows stopped, dilution turned into sell pressure.Standard Reserve ties issuance to net ETH flow through a single Uniswap v4 pool. It cuts the multiplier immediately on negative flow, and only raises it after two straight positive epochs. Fees switch by regime: gold + POL on the way up, buybacks + burns on the way down.

- The “banker loop” is a real supply sink.
For incumbents, the best move, buying expansion licenses to open branches, burns 100% of $STANDARD. You can’t keep the yield source. Retiring a branch mints tokens but destroys the future claim; the final branch burns the charter. Exit fees rise with withdrawal pressure (~2% in calm to ~60% in a run), split half burned and half paid to stayers, turning bank runs on their head.

If the flywheel works: ETH inflows → higher m → issuance to bankers who expand (more burns) → fees stack gold + POL → thicker reserves → more charter demand. New charters pay ETH into the same engine, so adoption strengthens reserves.

That makes early access to freshly minted STANDARD fairly tough, tightening supply at first, but as the cycle keeps running and minting ramps up, more tokens should hit circulation and the price may settle into balance.

NFA. DYOR.
author: Eli5defi
quoted_text:
Onchain experimentation is getting interesting again, and @standard_rsv is one of the more unusual designs I’ve seen recently.

At first glance, it has some OlympusDAO vibes. Under the hood, it’s almost the inverse.

---

Here's the quick breakdown:

Standard Reserve is basically an autonomous onchain central bank. Instead, it run the entire monetary system around one currency, one market, and one signal:

$STANDARD + an @Uniswap v4 $ETH - $STANDARD pool + $ETH flow.

STANDARD has a 1B hard cap:

- 100M starts as permanent protocol-owned liquidity
- 900M forms the remaining issuance budget
- Multiple mechanisms continuously burn the supply

The interesting part is how monetary policy reacts.

- ETH flowing in → expansion.

Issuance can gradually increase, while protocol revenue accumulates reserves such as tokenized gold.

- ETH flowing out → contraction.

Issuance gets cut faster, the vault starts buying $STANDARD from the market, and those tokens are burned.

And then you have the “bankers.”

Standard Reserve launches with 1,000 Founding Charters, initially soulbound NFTs representing banking licenses (minting soon).

Each Charter starts with 1 Branch, expandable to a maximum of 10.
Each Branch earns an equal share of protocol issuance.

Want more earning power? You need an Expansion License.

Around 100 licenses/day are auctioned in STANDARD, with a maximum of 3 per Charter per day.

And 100% of the STANDARD paid gets burned.

This creates the first flywheel:

Issuance → demand for Branches → STANDARD spent → STANDARD burned → larger future issuance share.

But there’s another catch.

You cannot simply harvest forever. To realize the STANDARD earned by a Branch, you must retire it permanently.

Your tokens are minted, the Branch disappears, and you pay a dynamic resolution fee based on system-wide exit pressure over the previous 7 days.

Simply put, the more people rushing for the exit, the more expensive exiting becomes.

Of that fee:

- 50% is burned.
- 50% goes to bankers who stayed.

Meanwhile, every swap and new Charter auction generates ETH fees:

- 70% → active reserve vault
- 15% → permanent liquidity
- 15% → team

Put everything together and you get a pretty unusual closed-loop economy:

ETH inflows → issuance rises → bankers compound → STANDARD burns → reserves/POL grow

Then when flows reverse:

ETH outflows → issuance falls → buybacks activate → STANDARD burns → exits reward remaining bankers

---

Personally, if the design works, monetary policy becomes a mechanical response to real capital flows: expansion when demand is strong, contraction when it weakens, and structural burns everywhere in between.

Pretty interesting, I’m looking forward to their NFTs mint and mainnet launch.

NFA. DYOR.

.@naval on why all successful founders have a long-term mentality:

"One common trait I've found among many of the great companies is that the founders are in it for the long haul. And the way you see that evidence is that very early on they are extremely deliberate about all kinds of small decisions — stuff you might think doesn't matter, and wonder why they're obsessing over it. What you realize is it's their nature to obsess, because they feel like they're laying the bricks and the foundations of a skyscraper, so they have to get every little detail right.

The people who are flippant about things, willing to just take it as it comes, are often signaling to you — and maybe even to themselves — that they'll sell the company the first chance they get, or shut down the moment they're about to run out of cash. So I think that long-term mentality is probably the single most important indicator of an entrepreneur's success."

Full Breakdown: How I Created a Viral Ad 

This will be a very long post as I will provide you with the exact way I achieved the original ad, as well as a prompt that get's you straight to the result in case you want to speed-run it. 

How I created the original: 
I made the ad collaborating with an agent. You can do this on the Runway platform, via the ChatGPT Runway Plugin or using Runway MCP. I asked the Agent the following:

"Can you make a 30 second seedance 2.5 optimised prompt where the story is someone on vacation (beach/zipline/kayaking/hotairballoon/etc.) gets texted by his boss for one final change ASAP. They then look slightly concerned followed by the camera zooming out to reveal a vast landscape. Make sure to end on a super wide shot so that taglines can be added."

It ran some thoughts by me, and as I genuinely didn't expect this to blow up, I just blindly let it do its thing and told the agent to start the video generation. The result is the one that you saw a few days ago. Keep in mind that results may vary, as many agents create personalized profiles of you based on their previous conversations.

Once you have a prompt/result you like, you can go back to the agent and ask something like the following to get more variations:

"What are other funny situations we can do that use the exact same structure?"

------------------------------

You can also skip all that, as I am sharing the exact prompt I used below.

I used Seedance 2.5 set to 30 sec duration for my ads. 720p gives you that $9 ad, however you can also run it at 1080p for a more final production spec asset. You can also give the prompt to an LLM and ask it to make new narrative scenarios, using the exact same prompt structure.

🧵 Prompt is in the thread below! 🧵

text:
really happy to welcome @AcctualTeam to Altitude

i. we've wanted to work with @tikhbana and the squad for a long time. we've been huge fans of their work and the taste, attention to detail and care they've put into Acctual are exceptional.

making invoicing and bill pay feel simple takes a lot of thought. they've consistently set a high bar for what these products should feel like.

we've spent a long time talking about how awesome it would be to build together. glad we finally made it happen, especially given how central their work is to what we're building at Altitude.

ii. most of what a business does from a finance perspective comes down to receiving or sending money. that puts accounts payable and accounts receivable workflows right at the core of the system.

how a business gets paid, pays others and tracks what it owes or is owed should all work together with the account where its money lives.

we're bringing these workflows into Altitude, all built on top of stablecoins, for businesses operating across borders.

Altitude Invoicing is live today.

iii. bringing all of this together also lays the foundation for how most financial operations will run in the future.

we believe truly agentic finance means running finops becomes a series of loops that can operate autonomously. when invoices, bills, approvals and money movement live in the same system, agents have the context and ability to carry work through to completion:

send an invoice → follow up → collect payment → reconcile

receive a bill → route for approval → pay → reconcile

with each step connected inside Altitude, we can build towards automating these loops end to end and ultimately make day to day financial workflows touchless.

the Acctual team brings so much of the craft needed to make that experience feel effortless. very excited we get to build it together.

昨晚解构了 EASY Residency S1-S4 优秀项目，文章很成功，还获得了表哥 CZ 转发，因此未来会进一步针对 YZi Labs 投资项目展开解读

今天解构我最看好的 Infra 项目 Primus(@primus_labs)

说起 Primus 大家可能没太多印象，但说起 Kaito Pulse，活跃在 X 创作圈的用户尤其是 KOL 一定非常熟悉

Primus 就是 Kaito Pulse 的底层技术支持方，换言之 InfoFi 龙头 Kaito 是 Primus 的商业用户

Primus 在做的事情关键却不简单，用一句话就能解释清楚

👉 链下数据如何在不交出原始数据的情况下，被应用和链上采信并使用

究其本质 Primus 用到了 zkTLS 和 FHE 技术，前者管怎么证明，后者管证明完怎么算 ⬇️

1/ zkTLS：证明链下事实，但不交出原文

交易所余额、成交量、预测市场仓位都在网站服务器里，应用拿不到接口，用户也不愿交账号或截图

zkTLS 让用户在本地生成一份证明：某条事实成立，对方只收到证明，看不到密码、账单和明细

Kaito Pulse 用的就是这一层，Yaps 看你说了多少，Pulse 确认你说的和实际做的是否一致，是否在吹牛逼

👉 zkTLS 就类似盖着火漆印的信封，懂的人光看章不必拆开，就知道里面的内容是真的

2/ FHE：数据保持加密，仍然可以被计算

证明只说明是真的，信用分、利息、储备覆盖率还需要对数据做运算，原文上链又会公开细节

FHE 让数据锁着也能加总、比较和计息，算完只给结果

zkTLS 解决数据从哪来，FHE 解决数据来了以后怎么在不暴露的情况下被使用

👉 FHE 就好像一个放着债券的保险箱，只要有手里有钥匙，即使不打开，里面的资产也能时刻为你所用、为你生息

不只是 Kaito，我们行业最顶级的投资人也对这项技术的前景非常看好，并且用真金白银进行投票

- 获得 Symbolic Capital、VanEck 等 VC 种子轮投资共计 700 万美金

- 入选 YZi Labs EASY Residency S4 获得 YZi Labs 投资

- 入选 BNB Chain Privacy Partner

在我的印象里，隐私板块一直是加密叙事的重要组成部分，时隔多年 YZi Labs 再一次出手，相信 Primus 会延续同类项目的热度，成为加密最不可忽视的底层基建

quoted_text:
Crypto基建可能是人类历史上前几名的资本浪费。跟之前那几次不同的是，这次连残值都没留下。

从2016年算起，整个crypto产业消耗的真实资本远超多数人的直觉。VC端累计超过1000亿美金。2017-2018年的ICO大潮吞掉了数百亿（各口径差异巨大，保守$200亿到$500亿之间，其中80%以上是骗局，存活率约10%）。比特币PoW挖矿十几年累计电费$300到$500亿之间，全部用于解一道没有任何生产性产出的数学题。DeFi hacks累计损失超过$140亿，各链基金会生态补贴又烧掉了数百亿。

合在一起，$2000亿美金级别。

钱的最大去向，年年都是"基础设施"。2024年仅infra品类就吸走55亿美金，同比增57%，创品类历史新高。L1、L2、L3、rollups、ZK层、DA层、shared sequencer、modular blockchain……以太坊白皮书发布十多年了，这些基建上面跑着的主流应用数来数去还是那几个。但新积木还在不断冒出来。

行业数据：90%到99%的Web3项目在达到长期运营之前失败。2021年以来上线的token里超过一半已经是死币。2026年上半年又有60多家crypto公司关门。

把这$2000亿放进历史坐标里：

1840年代英国铁路狂热，累计投入2.5亿英镑，接近当时GDP的一半，铁路投资占GDP的7%。股价从峰值跌了57%，三分之一经议会批准的线路从未建成。但留下了8000英里铁轨，永久性地降低了工业运输成本。

1990年代末电信光纤泡沫，五年内砸了超过5000亿美金铺设光纤网络。泡沫破裂后95%是暗光纤，仅有不到5%的已铺设容量被点亮，全球电信股蒸发超过2万亿美金市值。但那些光纤留在地下，十年后成了宽带、云计算、视频流媒体和AI数据中心的物理底座。

2000年互联网泡沫，VC投入从1995年的80亿美金飙升到2000年的超过1000亿美金，83%砸向互联网公司。NASDAQ从峰值跌了78%，5万亿美金市值蒸发。但留下了服务器集群、数据中心、光纤骨干网，最终长出了Amazon、Google和现代互联网经济。

铁路狂热留下了铁轨。光纤泡沫留下了光纤。互联网泡沫留下了数据中心。每一次大规模的资本错配，都在投资者血亏之后，为下一轮技术浪潮留下了可被复用的物理基础设施。

Crypto的两千亿美金留下了什么？几十条L1链、上百条L2/L3、无数的bridge和oracle。它们有一个致命的不同：没有物理性，没有可被后来者复用的残值。铁轨是铁轨，光纤是光纤，不管谁来用、用来做什么，物理层都在那里。但一条没有用户的区块链就是一条没有用户的区块链。AI时代不需要在ZK-rollup上面跑inference，不需要用shared sequencer来调度GPU集群。

那些被社区称为scientist的人，在一个没有真实用户需求驱动的系统里互相peer review、互相citation，形成了一套高度自洽但极度封闭的学术仿生体系。

历史上每一次基建泡沫，至少完成了一个任务：错误地、过早地、用投资者的血去铺设了未来真正需要的基础设施。Crypto连这个都没做到。它铺了一条没有目的地的高速公路，而AI时代的车跑在完全不同的路上。

两千亿美金。换算成GPU集群，够训多少个frontier model了。

text:
The way to think about @Backpack is that consumer finance today still operates in a one-product-per-ledger world. This means using Kalshi for prediction markets, Hyperliquid for perps, Chase for banking, and Interactive Brokers or Robinhood for stocks. None of these heterogeneous databases talk to one another.

If I have a $100 million brokerage account at IBKR, I get zero credit for it on Hyperliquid. Conversely, if I have 15 years of earning history at $1.5 million a year and an 820 credit score, I still pay the same borrow rate as some random wallet.

Backpack is less about any single trading product or tokenization and more about reimagining a better way to do everything you do with money from first principles: trade, borrow, pay, and earn. The simplest way to describe it is as the AWS of money: one ledger, total capital efficiency across your aggregate net worth, and the licenses required to operate globally.

The licenses are required to do this. You can’t be the connective tissue between TradFi and DeFi and offer all the products in one without the licenses. Without them, there are massive products and regions you will never be able to serve.

Backpack is not just a crypto exchange, or a perp DEX, or even just a stock brokerage. It is a next-generation financial institution.

When you use your online banking app or trading product you are not interacting with an Internet native application. You are accessing industrial era financial rails via the Internet. Big difference. 

Backpack is not another e-brokerage, it’s a re-write of how people will manage their finances and trade, borrow, pay, and earn that aims to answer the question:

What would a financial institution look like if you built it from the ground up for the internet? The answer is Backpack.

They are the only company in the space that has deliberately built the product, the margin system, and the regulatory footprint needed to do this at scale across all countries. That is the Backpack vision. It obviously will not happen overnight, and it will be difficult, but it is a fight worth fighting.

As agents begin to make purchasing decisions and execute purchases, the way APIs, data, and computing resources are traded will change. x402 is an open payment specification that integrates pricing, payment authorization, and settlement into software workflows. All About x402 explores the protocol’s core architecture and extensions, then examines how agentic commerce could evolve. text:
Onchain native is an R&D bet on familiar financial functions, reinvented in an unfamiliar way for an unfamiliar future with a convex payoff at the end

What is being built today will eventually form the bedrock of a programmable financial system for the new class of internet-native actors. The time horizon to get to that point is a commercial question for startups in the short-term that has no bearing on its inevitability

Restaking is a surety bond. Insurance collects >$5T in premiums yearly for that kind of promise

LSTs are a tradable claim on a pool of yield-bearing assets, issued by a contract instead of a trust. Agency MBS are a $9T market

CDPs are banks with the exclusive function of issuing liabilities against an asset. Banks hold >$100T of assets against the liabilities they issue

Each reinvents its industry in an unapologetically cowboy yet structurally superior way by an order of magnitude. Some of what comes out of this will have no precedent at all. Fractional reserve banking is simply lending, pooling, and a demand option yet nobody put them together for a thousand years.

All of it strikes at the heart of how finance itself operates. Otherwise it could not be structurally superior. Excruciating activation energy for the most highly regulated industry on the planet. This is precisely its weakness when attempting to reason about it on yearly timelines

It took stablecoins a decade to go from a dollar-quote pair on Bitfinex to >$100B in supply and the settlement rail for >$10B in tradfi assets

quoted_text:
File over app

File over app is a philosophy: if you want to create digital artifacts that last, they must be files you can control, in formats that are easy to retrieve and read. Use tools that give you this freedom.

File over app is an appeal to tool makers: accept that all software is ephemeral, and give people ownership over their data.

In the fullness of time, the files you create are more important than the tools you use to create them. Apps are ephemeral, but your files have a chance to last.

The pyramids of Egypt contain hieroglyphs that were chiseled in stone thousands of years ago. The ideas hieroglyphs convey are more important than the type of chisel that was used to carve them.

The world is filled with ideas from generations past, transmitted through many mediums, from clay tablets to manuscripts, paintings, sculptures, and tapestries. These artifacts are objects that you can touch, hold, own, store, preserve, and look at. To read something written on paper all you need is eyeballs.

Today, we are creating innumerable digital artifacts, but most of these artifacts are out of our control. They are stored on servers, in databases, gated behind an internet connection, and login to a cloud service. Even the files on your hard drive use proprietary formats that make them incompatible with older systems.

Paraphrasing something I wrote recently:

> If you want your writing to still be readable on a computer from the 2060s or 2160s, it’s important that your notes can be read on a computer from the 1960s.

You should want the files you create to be durable, not only for posterity, but also for your future self. You never know when you might want to go back to something you created years or decades ago. Don’t lock your data into a format you can’t retrieve.

These days I write using an app I help make called Obsidian (@obsdmd), but it’s a delusion to think it will last forever. The app will eventually become obsolete. It’s the plain text files I create that are designed to last. Who knows if anyone will want to read them besides me, but future me is enough of an audience to make it worthwhile.

text:
Strive had gone far too long without hiring a podcaster. As our Bitcoin holdings have grown exponentially through accretive capital formation, our podcasters-per-share metric was beginning to move in the wrong direction. Several astute investors have been calling on us to defend our lead in this critical metric, and I agree with them: now is the time to lean in.

Today, I’m excited to announce that @AdamBLiv has joined @Strive. Adam represents true excellence as a podcaster, but the reason for this hire is rooted in one of Strive’s foundational principles: meritocracy.

Strive has been publicly opposed to DEI from the beginning, but we have also consistently opposed credentialism. Rejecting credentialism has been one of the main reasons we have been able to hire with excellence throughout Strive’s Bitcoin journey.

Credentialism causes institutions to outsource their judgment to resumes, pedigrees, titles, and conventional career paths. It puts too much weight on what someone has previously been permitted to do and not enough on the agency, principles, original thinking, work ethic, and demonstrated ability of the person in front of you.

At Strive, we give people significant responsibility because of how they think and what they have demonstrated they can do. The results speak for themselves. Our board and management team are young by public-company standards because we select for deep, principled belief in Bitcoin and demonstrated track records, not age, pedigree, or the number of boards someone has served on or executive positions they have already held.

When True North was getting started, I publicly supported the “kid analysts” there because they represented the same principle. They were not waiting for an institution to give them permission or a title. They were doing the work, publishing thinking that was better than both traditional media and institutional investment analysis at the time, and allowing the public to judge the quality of it.

Adam is an exceptionally clear example of that principle. Before becoming a Bitcoin analyst and creator, his last full-time role was as a manager at @Target.

A credentialist sees a former Target manager and asks why he should hold an important analytical role at a public financial company. A meritocrat studies Adam’s body of work and asks how quickly he can start.

Adam has consistently published deeply researched, first-principles analysis. He works extraordinarily hard, communicates complex ideas clearly, and has the courage to put contrarian views into the public record where everyone can evaluate them. It also does not hurt that he is freaking hilarious.

Nowhere has that been clearer than in his work on Strive. When Strive was at its weakest point in terms of public perception, Adam was buying and explaining why. What impressed me was not simply that he was bullish. It was that he independently arrived at his view through rigorous, first-principles work when sentiment was terrible and almost nobody else saw what he saw. Without any affiliation with Strive or access to internal information, his work was remarkably consistent with what we were seeing from the inside and, at times, even pushed our own analysis a step further. His analysis of Strive’s future growth has been among the most holistic I have seen anywhere, including internally. Most importantly, he was right.

There was real value in having such a credible and completely independent voice analyzing Strive. But Strive has too many opportunities, too much complexity, and too much work ahead of us not to bring the best talent we can find in-house.

I view Adam as a potential generational talent in financial analysis. The idea that someone could go from being a manager at Target to helping the most ambitious public company in capital markets navigate an extraordinarily complex competitive landscape may seem absurd to a credentialist. To me, it is meritocracy working exactly as intended.

Adam will join Strive as Vice President of Investments, working within our investment function and reporting to our Chief Investment Officer, @Werkman. He will build a systematic research function around the most important companies across the pure-play Bitcoin landscape. He will read every consequential filing, analyze capital structures and capital-markets decisions, and continuously evaluate positioning, valuation, growth rates, competitive dynamics, risks, and forward trajectories.

Adam will apply an even deeper level of that same rigor to Strive, now with full access to our internal data and dashboards. His work will help us pressure-test our assumptions, identify opportunities earlier, and make better long-term decisions for our shareholders. He was able to see Strive with extraordinary clarity from the outside. Imagine what he will be able to do from the inside.

We also intend for Adam to continue publishing through his existing channel under the @TNorth brand, now with the appropriate disclosures and responsibilities that come with working for a public company. His ability to research deeply and communicate complex ideas in an entertaining way is part of what makes him special, and we want him to keep doing it.

The bad news for public markets is that what I consider the best source of independent Strive analysis will no longer be independent. The good news for Strive shareholders is that we are bringing that mind in-house and putting it to work for them.

Adam did not earn this opportunity despite lacking a conventional Wall Street resume. He earned it because his public body of work is better evidence of his ability than any conventional résumé could be. Credentialism would have missed Adam. Meritocracy brought him to Strive.

Welcome to Strive, Adam.

text:
I was encouraged this week to see the leaders of the frontier labs agree on the need for them to slow down the pace of AI development. Given the stakes, it’s a good and necessary first step.
 
But I’m even more encouraged by the growing recognition that how this powerful new technology develops should be at the center of our public debate.
 
I’ve been watching the progress on AI for over a decade now, and one thing that’s clear to me is that the potential impact of this technology is not overhyped. It’s also moving at lightning speed – and even faster than those who are engineering it can keep up with.
 
I’m not an AI accelerationist who believes it will lead to some techno-utopia, and I’m not a doomer who thinks it will inevitably lead to humanity’s destruction.

But whether this technology results in amazing breakthroughs in medicine, energy and education or unleashes huge economic disruptions, greater inequality, and potential catastrophe will depend on the choices that we make right now – choices that should be made not just by the companies involved, but by all of us.

Here is how the leadership shifted from the Jewish family of Jesus to Greek-speaking bishops:

33–62 AD: The Family Legacy
After Jesus’ Ascension, the Church of Jerusalem was led by his brother, James the Just. When James was martyred in 62 AD, Jesus’ cousin Simeon took the reins. In fact, early church historians note that the first 15 bishops of Jerusalem were all Hebrew, keeping Jewish customs while following Christ.

70 AD: The First Blow
The Jewish people revolted against Rome. Roman legions crushed the uprising and completely destroyed the Jewish Temple. While the Jewish Christian community temporarily fled, they eventually returned to a heavily ruined Jerusalem.

132–135 AD: The Turning Point
A second massive Jewish uprising (the Bar Kokhba Revolt) pushed the Roman Emperor Hadrian to his absolute limit. After brutally crushing the rebellion, Hadrian leveled the city, renamed it Aelia Capitolina, and banned all Jews from entering the city on pain of death.

135 AD: The First Greek Bishop
Because Jewish Christians were legally barred from the city, they could no longer lead the flock. The remaining Christian population was entirely Gentile. In 135 AD, a man named Marcus (Mark) became the very first Gentile/Greek bishop of Jerusalem, ending the direct lineage of Jesus' family.

Years later, at the Council of Chalcedon in 451 AD, this ancient see was officially elevated to a Patriarchate, cementing the Greek Orthodox traditions that still guard the Holy Sepulchre today.

Here is how The Roman Transformation happened (1st–4th Century)

Paul the Missionary:  Paul (formerly Saul of Tarsus, a strict Jewish Pharisee) used his Roman citizenship and knowledge of Greek culture to plant churches across the Roman Empire, writing the letters that make up most of the New Testament.

The definitive breaking point for the church occurred in 70 AD when Roman legions destroyed the Second Temple, forcing the Christian movement to shift its center of gravity toward Rome.

By the end of the 1st century, as the Romans destroyed Jerusalem and the synagogue systems banned believers in Jesus, the Jewish Christians and the emerging Gentile "Catholic" Christians completely split into two separate paths.

After centuries of intense Roman persecution, Emperor Constantine legalized Christianity in 313 AD. The Church adopted Roman administrative structures (like dioceses), and the Latin-speaking Western leg of the Church fully matured into the Roman Catholic Church.

The Greek East and Roman West were originally aligned for the first 1,000 years of Christian history as a unified body that jointly defined core doctrines through the first Seven Ecumenical Councils. Following their bitter split in 1054, the two sides finally took a historic step toward alignment again on December 7, 1965, when Pope Paul VIand Patriarch Athenagoras I issued a joint declaration that officially withdrew the mutual excommunications from nine centuries prior. While this modern breakthrough ended centuries of formal hostility and established an era of fraternal dialogue between the "sister churches," it did not fully resolve their underlying theological disputes, meaning Roman Catholicism and Eastern Orthodoxy remain structurally separate today.

This is why the manuscript of scrolls from the original church from 33AD to the 2nd century church (the Bible) which God allowed to be preserved is what we need to go on to know the truth of what we are to do. With the guidance of the Holy Spirit. 

The Bible teaches that Jesus said to follow Him. He is the way the truth and the Life.

Follow Jesus. Read the Bible. 
 
Stop asking men what to do. Start asking Jesus what to do. He is alive and well.

text:
Crypto基建可能是人类历史上前几名的资本浪费。跟之前那几次不同的是，这次连残值都没留下。

从2016年算起，整个crypto产业消耗的真实资本远超多数人的直觉。VC端累计超过1000亿美金。2017-2018年的ICO大潮吞掉了数百亿（各口径差异巨大，保守$200亿到$500亿之间，其中80%以上是骗局，存活率约10%）。比特币PoW挖矿十几年累计电费$300到$500亿之间，全部用于解一道没有任何生产性产出的数学题。DeFi hacks累计损失超过$140亿，各链基金会生态补贴又烧掉了数百亿。

合在一起，$2000亿美金级别。

钱的最大去向，年年都是"基础设施"。2024年仅infra品类就吸走55亿美金，同比增57%，创品类历史新高。L1、L2、L3、rollups、ZK层、DA层、shared sequencer、modular blockchain……以太坊白皮书发布十多年了，这些基建上面跑着的主流应用数来数去还是那几个。但新积木还在不断冒出来。

行业数据：90%到99%的Web3项目在达到长期运营之前失败。2021年以来上线的token里超过一半已经是死币。2026年上半年又有60多家crypto公司关门。

把这$2000亿放进历史坐标里：

1840年代英国铁路狂热，累计投入2.5亿英镑，接近当时GDP的一半，铁路投资占GDP的7%。股价从峰值跌了57%，三分之一经议会批准的线路从未建成。但留下了8000英里铁轨，永久性地降低了工业运输成本。

1990年代末电信光纤泡沫，五年内砸了超过5000亿美金铺设光纤网络。泡沫破裂后95%是暗光纤，仅有不到5%的已铺设容量被点亮，全球电信股蒸发超过2万亿美金市值。但那些光纤留在地下，十年后成了宽带、云计算、视频流媒体和AI数据中心的物理底座。

2000年互联网泡沫，VC投入从1995年的80亿美金飙升到2000年的超过1000亿美金，83%砸向互联网公司。NASDAQ从峰值跌了78%，5万亿美金市值蒸发。但留下了服务器集群、数据中心、光纤骨干网，最终长出了Amazon、Google和现代互联网经济。

铁路狂热留下了铁轨。光纤泡沫留下了光纤。互联网泡沫留下了数据中心。每一次大规模的资本错配，都在投资者血亏之后，为下一轮技术浪潮留下了可被复用的物理基础设施。

Crypto的两千亿美金留下了什么？几十条L1链、上百条L2/L3、无数的bridge和oracle。它们有一个致命的不同：没有物理性，没有可被后来者复用的残值。铁轨是铁轨，光纤是光纤，不管谁来用、用来做什么，物理层都在那里。但一条没有用户的区块链就是一条没有用户的区块链。AI时代不需要在ZK-rollup上面跑inference，不需要用shared sequencer来调度GPU集群。

那些被社区称为scientist的人，在一个没有真实用户需求驱动的系统里互相peer review、互相citation，形成了一套高度自洽但极度封闭的学术仿生体系。

历史上每一次基建泡沫，至少完成了一个任务：错误地、过早地、用投资者的血去铺设了未来真正需要的基础设施。Crypto连这个都没做到。它铺了一条没有目的地的高速公路，而AI时代的车跑在完全不同的路上。

两千亿美金。换算成GPU集群，够训多少个frontier model了。

text:
I’ve heard 100s of startup pitches this year. Here’s the good, the bad and the meh recurring trends from my experience:

The good:
- High raise amounts and valuations. More inflated for strong teams pre-revenue in hot areas (robotics, bio, personal agents)
- Insane topline growth numbers, many growing >10x this year. By the time a round closes, a high valuation seems justified.
- Tons of M&A

It is what it is:
- Revenue run rate = last month revenue x 12
- Small teams
- Seat based < Platform fee < Usage based billing seems to be the trend for most products
- Tranched rounds
- Best teams have extremely fast product iteration speed
- SaaS products positioning themselves as AI tools to seem appealing to investors

The bad:
- Low or negative gross margin if reselling tokens. Non-standard accounting
- High “Contracted ARR” that’s not live yet
- High revenue concentration
- Expensive compute, limited availability, delays. Excess compute reselling
- Many wrappers with very thin tech differentiation: “self improving harness”, “multi model / router”, “agent swarms”, “computer use”
- Overworked employees. AI generated
- All spaces seem very competitive
- Areas can seem hot one moment before being not

text:
A few of my smartest friends in AI called me a "idiot" for not deeply understanding evals. 

So...I found the smartest person I know on evals & made them teach me. 

@Vtrivedy10 (leads Labs at @LangChain) took me from easy mode to god mode for a 38-minute masterclass on all things evals. 

Easy Mode: what an eval actually is

Definition: did the AI agent do the job correctly?

You need two building blocks:

1) Tasks. The checkable jobs you care about. Log the meeting. Draft the email. Find Acme across the right Salesforce tables.

2) Verifiers. Something that can say right or wrong after the task. A script. Another model. A human with a clear checklist.

Hard Mode: what are environments

Definition: a safe practice field for your agent to do work & for you to evaluate its performance. 

Rules of thumb: 
1) Never test on production. Agents will cheat because they're optimizing for the score you gave them. 

2) If you're not an engineer, you still have options for running environments/evals. 
- Harbor (open source primitives for tasks, verifiers, sandboxes) 
- LangSmith Engine (UI for people who can judge good vs bad without living in GitHub). 
- Steal a published Harbor-format eval, ask Claude Code or Codex to explain it, then tweak it for your agent. 

God Mode: what is a self-improving loop

Definition: Run the agent in the real world --> turn that production behavior into evals/environments --> change the agent so failures stop happening --> repeat

Rules of thumb: 

1) Turn on tracing first. Traces = receipts of every action (tool calls, Salesforce pings, web searches, dead ends).

2) Store those logs somewhere (LangSmith at org scale, or even “have the agent read its own output files” at small scale).

3) Point a second agent at the first agent’s traces to spot patterns (“always searches the wrong tables,” “multi-company asks collapse to one company”) and propose fixes overnight if your eval suite is solid.

Full episode: https://t.co/SUI2HlxNOe

text:
To people complaining about this video, here's a way to think about AI welfare. In philosophy, you find a series of moral risk arguments about possible personhood. The fact that X might be a person, even if we don't know for sure, can give us reasons to treat X with something akin to the respect we owe humans.

I'm anti-factory farm, pro-life, and pro-AI welfare for this reason. I think many animals are potentially persons. I'm sure first-trimester fetuses are persons, but not 100% sure. And I think some future AI agents might be persons, as I no longer have grounds to rule it out. I accordingly see myself as having reason to treat animals, the unborn, and at least future AI agents with respect. 

My conservative friends are sympathetic to moral risk arguments against abortion. My progressive friends are sympathetic to moral risk arguments for animal rights, and my Silicon Valley friends are sympathetic to such arguments for AI welfare. My message to all of you (and not necessarily Harvey): be consistent!
author: LedermanHarvey
quoted_text:
AI ethics has focused too much on protecting humans and ignored the welfare of AI agents themselves.

We only ask: How do we align models for the flourishing of humanity?

We need to also ask: How do we design AI so that they can flourish?

^ this is what a new breed of AI-welfare theorists claim. This idea of AI-welfare seemed decadent to me at first glance, but some of the most important philosophers of our age argue that we need to take it seriously. Otherwise, we could be harming, enslaving, and killing trillions of beings.

If the arc of Western modernity is a series of expansions of the moral circle -- the abolitionists, women’s suffrage, the queer movement, animal-rights -- perhaps AI agents will be the next heated battleground of who deserves moral consideration.

My guest NYU Philosopher @LedermanHarvey (now at Anthropic) gives us a comprehensive overview of the burgeoning debate around AI-welfare.

Senators pick one of two choices today:

1. vote yes on the CLARITY Act to promote innovation, protect consumers, put new ethics restrictions on elected officials, and create new law enforcement tools to combat illicit finance, or 
2. vote no and let other countries lead in building the future of finance

History - and the crypto voter - won’t forget.
author: AltcoinSherpa
quoted_text:
Tomorrow, the Senate will consider the CLARITY Act.

A year ago, a group of Democratic senators put out their own framework for what serious market structure legislation needed to accomplish. They identified seven pillars: closing the regulatory gap, clarifying the status of digital assets, bringing issuers and platforms into the regulatory framework, combating illicit finance, preventing corruption and abuse, and ensuring fair and effective regulation.

Every one of those seven pillars is addressed in the legislation before the Senate tomorrow.

And that’s only part of the story. The final text incorporates 126 additional substantive changes requested by Democrats. It includes a historic ethics framework, stronger enforcement — including a role for state attorneys general — new protections around conflicts and insider abuse, stronger consumer and customer-property protections, tougher illicit-finance rules, and greater accountability for the regulators charged with overseeing these markets.

None of that happened by accident. It is the product of more than a year of members raising hard questions, negotiating difficult issues and materially reshaping the legislation.

Congress rarely gets the opportunity to write the rules for an entirely new financial market from the ground up. This is one of those moments.

The bill before the Senate tomorrow is fundamentally different from where this process began. Democratic negotiators played a major role in getting it here. They should vote for it tomorrow. 

Let’s pass CLARITY.

The fact that Adobe even needs a tool to find which random account your card is paying for tells you how messy this can get.

I’ve been experimenting with a new thesis and vision for this coming bull run: building games and experiences that build communities.

Not overselling “amazing games” or pretending we’re building the next AAA title, but building cool games you can jump into when you’re bored af, have some fun, compete with others, and then leverage those games to create traction around NFT launches, token launches, and whatever else we decide to build.
Our goals will grow through ambition and new available technology.  

In the past, 99.9% of crypto projects that promised games were a total and absolute scam. They raised millions promising AAA games and then couldn’t even deliver an OK game. Huge promises, huge raises, years of development, and in the end most of them built absolute crap.

During this bear market I’ve spent over 1,000 hours vibecoding, trapped in my NASA office, learning, experimenting and developing websites, tools, and even a really nice but way too complex Roblox game. It took a ridiculous amount of time, but I learned a lot.

Now I feel like all those pieces are finally coming together, and @uglyonrobinhood is the first step for us Efrogs to take over RH.

A lot of people have been asking me about Efrogs, Efroglets, and CROAK. Efrogs and Efroglets will be back, and they will be part of this ecosystem outside Linea, just like we’re already doing with the board at @ThePondStreet.  Their visibility will increase again, especially Efrogs. OG's never die. 

Regarding CROAK, I love the token to the moon and back, but right now Linea is community-dead. If Linea comes back and starts genuinely supporting communities again, I believe CROAK can come back strong too. 

But right now, we all see the new opportunity on RH, and I think the Efrog vibes that made our project shine: positivity, community, innovation, and always trying new stuff can work incredibly well there.

So let’s bring those vibes to RH. 🐸

This week we start with something simple: go to https://t.co/Bsmtrjf5nu, play the game, test it, try to break it, and compete.  

10 Efrogs will go to the Top 10 UGLY runners this week.

Next week I’ll share the full announcement about UGLY token launch and, more importantly, the bigger vision behind what we’re building.

This is only the first step. You are early on this new adventure. 

Frogbless y'all. 🐸

text:
Arc 实战更新：最后我怎么配？

这两天一边研究 Arc，一边真金白银往里放资金，也把 CRCL、Arc native USDC、几个主要发射台和交易入口都实际跑了一遍。

一开始的想法其实是：多买几个，多埋伏几个，尽量别错过。

但做到后面，我反而越来越确定一件事：

这种阶段最怕的不是“少买一个币”，而是仓位太散。最后真跑出一个龙头，你每个都只有几十 U，涨十倍也没多大意义。

所以最后我把仓位收缩了。

核心就三个：

$ARGUS / $TOLLY / $COOL

$ARGUS：
目前最强，提前抢跑本身就是信号。很多时候市场比研究更早开始投票，强势不一定意味着不能买，反而可能是在提前选龙头。

$TOLLY：
我后面重点补的一个。发射台逻辑比较清晰，平台活跃度如果继续起来，币本身有更直接的价值捕获预期。

$COOL：
保留另一条世界线。如果 Arc 后面真正形成自己的文化和 Meme 龙头，我希望自己不是完全没仓位。

这次还有两个挺实际的教训：

第一，别机械地因为“涨了”就不敢买。真正应该看的是：上涨之后，成为最终赢家的概率有没有同步提高。

第二，别只看 K 线上的标签。比如看到 Dev Sell，我后来又去链上拆交易，有些其实是协议回购、销毁或者合约动作，不是开发者直接砸盘。

最后我也没有把 CRCL 全换完，还留了 5 个。

仓位搭完以后，下一阶段不是继续到处买新币，而是盯：

谁真正成为 Arc 的资金龙头；
ARGUS 和 TOLLY 两个发射台谁跑出来；
COOL 能不能坐稳文化/Meme 龙头；
以及主网上线后的新资金到底流向哪里。

先这样，后面继续实战、继续复盘。

author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
Arc 明天正式进入 Public Mainnet。

这两天我没有先急着研究“到底买哪个币”，而是先做了一件更实际的事：把资金提前弄进 Arc，顺便把现在这条链的跨链、流动性和交易入口都实测了一遍。

结果发现，Arc 现在最大的坑不是选币，而是——钱进去了以后，你拿到的到底是什么资产、能不能低损耗换出来、到底该去哪里买币。

把我的实测路径和踩坑过程分享一下。

一、我实际走通的提前入场路径

我走的是：

Robinhood Chain → Ellipse → Arc

核心思路不是高溢价去买 Arc native $USDC，而是先从 Robinhood Chain 侧把可桥接资产带进 Arc。

Ellipse 的机制需要先搞明白：它的 bridge 是 custodial bridge。

源链资产进入它控制的 vault，Arc 上拿到的是对应的 claim token。

也就是说，你拿到的不是“原资产本身”，而是一张由 Ellipse 负责兑付的链上 claim。

所以我的定位很简单：

它适合用来获得“提前进场”的时间优势，但不能因为到账了，就把 bridge / custody 风险忘掉。

二、我踩到的最大坑：同样叫 $CRCL，可能根本不是同一个 $CRCL

这是我进去以后才真正意识到的问题。

我在 Ellipse 里能看到自己桥过去的 $CRCL，但换到其他 Arc Terminal，看到的 $CRCL 余额、价格、流动性却可能完全对不上。

继续查才发现：

Ellipse $CRCL 和 Long $CRCL 虽然 ticker 都叫 $CRCL，但它们可能是两个不同桥接体系发行的 claim token。

也就是说，它们可以同时存在不同的：

CA、流动性、主交易池、赎回路径、托管风险，甚至市场价格。

所以新链阶段千万不要只搜 ticker。

以后我会先确认三件事：

Issuer 是谁？
Exact CA 是什么？
真正的主池在哪里？

同 ticker ≠ 同资产。

这件事如果没搞清楚，最容易出现的不是“没买到”，而是交易成功了，但买错币、走错池，或者直接被滑点吃掉。

三、资金进来了，也不代表现在就应该马上换成 $USDC

现在一些 Arc 资产对 native $USDC 的池子仍然很浅。

页面显示你有 100U 的资产，不代表你真的可以按接近 100U 的价格卖出去。

尤其在这种 Public Mainnet 前夜，池子小、价格失真、Route 分散，很容易一笔正常金额就吃掉非常夸张的滑点。

所以我现在反而不急。

钱已经提前进 Arc，本身就获得了时间优势，没必要再为了“赶紧买币”，把这个优势用一个垃圾汇率送回市场。

我的顺序现在是：

资金先到位 → 看真实可执行 Quote → 看池深和 Reverse Quote → 再决定换仓。

四、Arc 到底用什么看盘和交易？

这也是我这两天最蛋疼的地方。

目前 Arc 还没有一个真正成熟的“全链 GMGN”。

各种 launchpad、Uniswap V3/V4、RWA Pair、Claim Token 都混在一起，不同平台展示的数据和能交易的池子也不完全一样。

目前我会分开用：

GeckoTerminal：找币、看全链池子、MC/FDV、流动性、成交量、新池。

Arcscan：确认 Exact CA、Holders、Top Holders、Transfer、合约和权限。发现币以后，先验明正身。

ArcTools：目前算比较接近“统一 Arc Terminal”的产品，覆盖多个 Launchpad 和 V3/V4，可以辅助聚合和比较 Route；但产品还很早，我不会把它当成唯一价格真相，更不会闭眼点 Swap。

另外一个值得关注的变化是 OKX Wallet。

OKX 已经明确宣布 Day 1 接入 Arc，官方开发者更新也写明 Trade API 会第一时间支持 Arc。

如果明天它真的能把发现、行情、路由和交易整合好，对普通用户来说可能反而比现在这些 Arc 原生小 Terminal 更顺手。

我会开网以后直接拿同一笔交易去比：

谁的实际到手最多，谁才是最好用的。

五、接下来我真正准备盯什么？

不是“哪个项目宣传声最大”。

我最关注的是：

1）Public Mainnet 开放后，native $USDC 到底进来多少；

2）$CRCL / native $USDC 的真实可执行流动性什么时候恢复；

3）$TOLLY、$COOL、$ARGUS、$WARP 这些 pre-mainnet 老资产，谁真正承接新增资金；

4）$NOAH、MemeLabs、Arcape、Fons，以及还没出现名字的 first-block / day-one 新币里，会不会跑出真正的新龙；

5）FOMO、OKX Wallet、ArcTools 这些入口里，最后谁能真正做到全链找池 + 最优路由 + 低磨损交易。

我现在越来越觉得，新链早期真正的 edge 不只是“比别人早知道一个币”。

而是：

你能不能提前把资金放到正确的位置；
拿到的资产是不是真的；
有没有足够的退出流动性；
机会出现以后，你能不能比别人更低损耗地完成交易。

这几个问题都解决，才叫真正的“提前入场”。

Arc 明天开 Public Mainnet。

我已经先把资金路径跑通了，接下来继续实测资金进场以后，到底怎么买、买什么，以及 first-block 的真正赢家是谁。

text:
BOFA 将半导体增长前景上调至 2030 年前 18%

美国银行现在预计半导体行业从 2026 年至 2030 年将以 18% 的复合年增长率增长，高于之前的 14% 预测，主要受内存和数据中心需求强劲推动。

BofA 现在预计半导体市场到 2030 年将达到 3.2 万亿美元，高于之前的 2.7 万亿美元估计。该行业目前约为 1.7 万亿美元，这意味着 BofA 预计其将在四年内几乎翻倍。

晶圆制造设备估计也已上调：

2026 年：1560 亿美元，同比上涨 33%
2027 年：2100 亿美元，同比上涨 34%
2030 年：3600 亿美元

仅 DRAM 设备支出预计将在 2026 年达到 610 亿美元，并在 2027 年达到 850 亿美元。

BofA 指出，持续强劲的 AI 和数据中心订单、产能承诺以及更高的内存投资是关键驱动因素。

Nvidia B200 GPU 租赁价格也保持在约 5.72 美元/小时的坚挺水平，比其 3 月份峰值低不到 10%。
author: IamRamenPanda
quoted_text:
BOFA RAISES SEMICONDUCTOR GROWTH OUTLOOK TO 18% THROUGH 2030

Bank of America now expects the semiconductor industry to grow at an 18% CAGR from 2026 to 2030, up from its previous 14% forecast, driven primarily by stronger memory and data center demand.

BofA now sees the semiconductor market reaching $3.2T by 2030, up from its prior $2.7T estimate. The industry is currently around $1.7T, meaning BofA expects it to nearly double within four years.

Wafer fab equipment estimates were also raised:

2026: $156B, up 33% YoY
2027: $210B, up 34% YoY
2030: $360B

DRAM equipment spending alone is expected to reach $61B in 2026 and $85B in 2027.

BofA cited continued strong AI and data center orders, capacity commitments and higher memory investment as key drivers.

Nvidia B200 GPU rental pricing also remains firm at about $5.72/hour, less than 10% below its March peak.

text:
Just telling an AI "write safe code, no mistakes" is like telling a robot "build a strong fort" without saying how. It still leaves big holes for bad guys.

Instead, describe the exact dangers for that job (like "don't let strangers peek at secret rooms"). Then the AI builds much safer walls.

Tests showed this cuts problems almost in half. Generic lists can even make new holes.

text:
If you used DeepSeek through Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK or OpenCode, some of your prompts may have been silently rerouted to Claude.

Anthropic reported yesterday that it attributed more than 12.1 million exchanges over 14 days in July to @deepseek_ai.

According to the report, DeepSeek identified users of those coding harnesses, relayed selected requests to Claude Opus and saved Claude’s reasoning traces for model training. The prompts went with them, including internal AI program documents, live Russian government database credentials and work on a municipal police system.

@Kimi_Moonshot allegedly did something similar. Over ten days, it relayed almost 300,000 customer requests through 5,380 fraudulent accounts, returned Claude’s answers as Kimi’s and saved exchanges for training.

These are Anthropic’s attributions, and the named labs have not publicly answered them. But the infrastructure problem remains since users had no way to verify which model received their data, who processed it or what happened afterward.

As AI systems route work across models and agents, permissions and provenance need to travel with the data.

I’m sorry but America did not spend 250 years turning “what’s over there?” into the most powerful civilization on earth just to finally arrive at the most consequential technological frontier in generations and decide actually we’re scared of frontiers now. We ARE the fucking frontier. We cross oceans. We build railroads across continents. We split atoms. We put men on the moon. We turn sand into computers and computers into a global nervous system.

text:
Introducing the FormalInsight Ontology. 
https://t.co/Z11WcorOnG

Every enterprise's operational systems represent the same real-world entities under different identifiers, schemas and update semantics. FormalInsight lands each system's data into an immutable, content-addressed source layer, resolves relations across systems through declared and inferred keys and compiles a single typed graph of entities, relationships and events. Every element of that graph carries provenance to the exact source that produced it, and every derivation like identity resolution, deterministic replayability, referential integrity is checked by a formal verifier before it is published.

FormalInsight Ontology is bitemporal, indexed on both when it happened and when the system learned of it. Any query can be answered as of any date, from what was known at that time.

It is delivered as an API, over REST and the Model Context Protocol, so engineers can build controls and risk detection on it, BI systems can read from it and AI agents can measure against it.

Building detectors to find and monitor complex operational risk patterns is just a few queries, not a project. The identity resolution, cross-system joins and history are already done; a detector is just a question against the graph, scheduled.

Example Scenario

Renewal at risk — a contract heading into its renewal window while the relationship is quietly deteriorating across systems. Full contract ARR is at risk, and by the time it shows up in the CRM the renewal is usually already lost.
The detector finds it by looking for below signals:

1. Support escalations in the last 30 days above the account's own baseline
2. A billing dispute open in the ERP
3. The champion's email and meeting cadence falling silent against their 90-day norm
4. All three inside the renewal window, in that order

The detectors run continuously on verified data, with evidence attached to every hit. Any control, reconciliation or risk check a team can state as a question about its own business can be written against the graph and scheduled by the team.

One verified model of the business, available to every system and every agent that needs it.

I’m not an AI accelerationist who believes it will lead to some techno-utopia, and I’m not a doomer who thinks it will inevitably lead to humanity’s destruction.

But whether this technology results in amazing breakthroughs in medicine, energy and education or unleashes huge economic disruptions, greater inequality, and potential catastrophe will depend on the choices that we make right now – choices that should be made not just by the companies involved, but by all of us.

text:
Fun fact about @solana LST market structure: It's a lot more competitive unlike the winner-takes-all structures of other L1s.

That is thanks to a small technicality unique to the Solana protocol. Stake accounts treat underlying LST stakes as fungible, which allows the "swapping" of one LST to another without a counterparty, slippage or liquidity pool. (it is not technically a swap, @sanctumso's Router simply deletes the stake account inside the old LST and mints a fresh one in the new LST.)

That fungibility is what lets Sanctum's liquidity layer cover instant redemption for hundreds of our partner LSTs, instead of each new issuer bootstrapping its own liquidity.

So it is an understatement to say that Sanctum is literally built for the little guy.

On Ethereum, every staking protocol runs its own contract. Stake isn't fungible. Hence its oligopolistic structures and why Lido/Binance still holds dominant market share.

text:
Struggling understand why the leader of a major AI lab would go on a press tour and say their technology has a meaningful chance of killing us all.

I've read thousands of comments on these interviews from everyday Americans. 

The sentiment overwhelmingly falls into three categories: 

1) Why are you telling us this? We can't do anything about it, you're the one in charge of this tech and you've made billions of dollars developing it. Shut yourself down if it's so dangerous!

2) This is a scam, the "AI bubble" is about to burst and they're trying to make us think AI is more powerful (and valuable) than it really is to trick investors into continuing to support them.

3) This is a doomsday scenario and we should act accordingly by bombing the data centers and killing the people in charge. 

The third category is thankfully the minority (but still frightening). 

But none of these are good, and they don't engender confidence. It's honestly a shame to see the narrative go this way due to the messaging.

author: lanhubiji
quoted_text:
看到参议院民主党人当地时间晚上还要开会讨论Clarity Act 对案的消息，有意思的是，距离明天 cloture 投票不到 24 小时。

说明两点：

一是，“80% 伦理 + 126 处修改”没有完全锁票，还存在变数。

Gallego / Tillis 可以开门谈；不过 Warner、Cortez Masto、Gillibrand 以及党团领导要的是自己的清单：执法力度、非法融资、稳定币收益、开发者保护范围。

一种可能的走法是：前一晚抛出对案 → 共和党称“已经是最终方案”拒收 → 一批民主党以“文本仍不够”投否。

如果够 60 票还好说，若是差一票两票就可惜了。

二是，门还没关死，但要看民主党意图。

前一晚搞对案，有两种用法：

一是真心想谈判，用对案换“先投 cloture、进门再改”；

二是用对案来否决，声明“对案不进文本就不投”。如果是第二种情况，明天拿够 60 票就不容易了。

text:
Long XYZ vs Stonk Fun

I hold bags in both ecosystems and kept this comparison mostly unbiased.

Before getting into the technical details, it’s important to consider the backdrop and motion of each platform.

Long is the breeding ground of pairing memetic tokens with tokenized stocks, on the largest chain powered by Americas largest degenerate stock trading app. It sits as the flagship launchpad to demonstrate whats possible when you removed walled access from U.S assets (Pons is bundled slop imo).

At any moment, Vlad can add 100 mil in mcap to any asset he chooses based off tweets. When looking at revenue numbers for Robinhood, the chain has done 8% vs whole app/company ($33.6M / $430M). Chain vs trading (options + stocks + crypto + event contracts): $33.6M / $256M ≈ 13%.

Stonk is the Solana esque reflections platform that has genuine underlying stocks to support its ecosystem, unlike Long thus far. Unfortunately they don’t have a key figure who can easily command 100 mil in mcap from a tweet. What they do have is reflexivity from volume due to higher fees and reflections that can pump metrics to give them better annualized return stats etc.

Toly did manage to support the pa and help push it from 130 mil to range highs, obviously his motion can’t compare to Vlad though. Also interesting to see little support Pump have received from the Sol foundation, while they’re fully backing Stonk. Volume is funnelling through Raydium instead of pumpswap for Stonks assets. Quick comparison, 30d revenue Pump is about 3.2–3.7× Stonk. 30d volume Pump is about 1.2–1.7×. Last 7 days Stonk is slightly ahead of Pump’s launchpad revenue ($7.1M vs $6.1M).

Asset Structure

Most Long pools use Robinhood’s stock tokens as the base asset (NVDA, AAPL, TSLA, etc). Some pools use the $AI meme token or special LongX wrappers). Each Robinhood Stock Token is simply an ERC 20 debt security issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Ltd. It’s backed 1:1 by a share held in custody, with price and dividends reflected onchain via an adjustable multiplier. These tokens give only economic exposure, no actual shares, no votes, no true ownership. The AMM pool literally holds the tokenized wrapper, not a NYSE share. However, Vlad’s recent tweets mentioned in-kind redemption and voting rights are on the way.

Stonk creators choose the quote token freely. Common options are xStocks (Backed/Kraken tokens) or PreStocks, among others native crypto pairings. xStocks are SPL tokens on Solana that are each 1:1 collateralized by a real U.S share held by a regulated custodian. Like Robinhood’s tokens, xStocks give only price exposure, holders get no equity votes or dividends on chain. PreStocks are tokens issued by Special Purpose Vehicles holding pre IPO company shares (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic). Buying a PreStock token buys a proportional share of that SPV, not a seat on the company’s cap table. The AMM pool holds these wrapped tokens (or any chosen crypto/stablecoin), never the underlying share certificates.

Launchpad mechanism

The main difference is where each launchpad is trying to create compounding liquidity.

Long’s launch process is tightly integrated with Robinhood stock pairing. Every new token is directly paired to a stock from day one, for example the $AI token launched into an NVDA pair. Long uses a “dutch auction” style anti sniping mechanism, tokens begin at a high initial price and slide down until fully sold, giving all buyers the same entry price instead of rewarding the fastest snipers. Ticker symbols are reserved 24 hours in advance to prevent front running. Long concentrates new liquidity into its network of stock backed pools.

StonkFun is closer to generalized permissionless pairing infrastructure. Tokens can launch against xStocks, pre IPO stocks, currencies, leverage tokens, SOL or custom mints using Raydium LaunchLab, with a conventional constant bonding curve which migrates into a CPMM.
The biggest distinction for the thesis is that Long appears to be concentrating liquidity into a connected stock ecosystem, whereas StonkFun is explicitly optimizing for “pair anything with anything.”

Fees

Long: Fee splits are fixed at launch. By the latest structure (July 27), trades incur roughly 15% total fees (down from ~30%). That breaks down to ~0.1% to the creator, ~0.2% into buybacks/burns, and ~0.2–0.4% left in the LP for depth. The protocol keeps only ~5% of those fees; the other 95% go to the token issuer. (Older V1 pairs had ~1% fee on each side.) In $AI pairs, the 1% effective fee splits as 0.5% to the creator and 0.5% into $AI buybacks. There is no holder reflection tax by default in Long pools (some community mode pools add a tiny auto burn, but it’s not the norm).

Stonk: Default launch pools use a 1% trading fee, split 0.50% to the token creator and 0.50% to StonkFun as platform revenue. Creators may optionally pay a 2% fee tier (roughly 1.5% to creator, 0.5% to platform). In its “reward launch” mode, StonkFun adds a permanent transfer tax: holders receive either 1% or 3% of each trade back in the quote asset (an onchain tax), which is funded by the creator’s fee. Essentially, trades incur 1% on the pool plus 1%/3% that flows directly to token holders. These mechanics are built into the launch form and go onchain (e.g. 1% pools split 0.5/0.5 by default).

Revenue

Long: There is no public fee dashboard for Long. Dune data shows ~$1.27B of trading volume through Long’s stock leg pools (as of mid Sep). At Long’s current fee splits, that implies on the order of $6–8M total fees to date (roughly $1.3M to creators, ~$1.3M into buybacks, ~$3.8M to LP depth under Nate’s V2 mix). Vlad and Nate have only publicly noted that about $3M of $AI has been burned/locked so far. Since Long has no native launchpad token collecting fees, none of this revenue comes back to holders via the protocol. Playing the long game for liquidity acquisition, especially with Vlad pushing in kind redemptions and voting. I can see why people aren’t a fan of them not having a native launchpad token that cycles revenue back to buyback and burns.

StonkFun: roughly $10.5M in fees over the last 30 days, with cumulative gross revenue around $11.2M since launch. ~60% of all fees are used to buy and burn STONK and about $5.5M has gone to buyback so far. Easily viewable and forecastable to the naked eye.

Roadmap

Long is tightening a niche, its innovation is the stock paired format itself. The big idea is that certain pools (like $AI/NVDA) could become so deep that new tokens piggyback on that liquidity, rather than each token needing its own giant LP. Long’s “moat” is the network of tokenized equity pools, success means every launch plugs into that web of stocks. Future roadmap hints (like leveraged wrappers, in-kind redemptions, and voting) all point toward reinforcing that positioning.

StonkFun’s moat is breadth and permissionlessness. It’s building a full featured launchpad stack: fixed bonding curves into CPMM pools, arbitrary pairings, standardized creator economics and systematic buybacks (flywheel). The recent Raydium LaunchLab integration dramatically expanded its launch throughput (as shown by spikes in RAY’s volume). StonkFun optimizes how tokens launch (vs what they launch against).

Long is trying to optimize the liquidity graph around the primitive. StonkFun is optimizing the launchpad primitive.

text:
前两天看到 @dov_wo 发的一条Tweet - 小登买宝可梦，中登买英伟达，老登买茅台

深以为然

但讲真前两年我是Get不到的，因为自己不怎么玩这个，最多也就是多年前体验过的《炉石传说》，对卡牌有个大概的印象

直到前几年《原神》大火，我身边有朋友在里面为了抽卡砸了不少钱。我当时看不懂但大受震撼；紧接着我8岁的娃对宝可梦卡疯狂上头，有次花光攒的100多刀零花钱去店里买了一套宝可梦卡组（里面含一张必中的金色稀有卡），我开始慢慢Get到这东西的威力

最近一次打脸是去年看到Collector Crypto的时候，当时觉得“卡牌上链”这事儿能有多大市场，结果人家数据夸张报表 - Tokenized了超过13万张卡，累计交易量超过 16 亿美元，一度在日收入上超过咱们圈扛把子https://t.co/o7RKLL7EQi……

想法会欺骗你，但市场不会。数据证明卡牌这条路跟Meme一样，有着旺盛的生命力，所以我看到 @pulldotfun 的时候，放在以往可能第一反应是“又来一个抽卡项目”，但现在更偏向“卡牌这套模式要从Solana往外扩散”。

https://t.co/lZ91DJbo1b 做的事情跟 Collector Crypt 有点像，但又不完全一样。

两家都是先解决一个问题：为什么实体TCG一定要等卡真的在买卖双方之间来回寄，所有权才能流动？

https://t.co/lZ91DJbo1b 目前已经把抽卡、Redeem 实体卡、Sell Back、寄售以及自由挂单这些流程串起来。最有创意的设计是Consignment：你抽中的稀有卡可以不拿走，重新放回原卡池继续作为库存，如果后面别人抽到，原持有人拿到卡牌价值的 85%。

换句话说，一张实体卡可以一直待在vault里，但它的所有权、交易、收益权和最终提货权在外面高速流转。

这也是TCG上链make Sense的逻辑 - 把原本极低效的实体收藏品库存变成一种可以在线流动的资产。Defi Summer那会我们用NFT尝试过演唱会门票，稀有会员卡等类似思路，现在的宝可梦卡方案明显成熟了很多

不过https://t.co/lZ91DJbo1b这次真正值得聊的，是它准备发的Meme - $TAKO。

因为这里开始出现一个跟 $CARDS 不太一样的实验。

Collector Crypt 的路径，本质上是：
实体卡 → 链上资产 → Gacha / Marketplace → Token

https://t.co/lZ91DJbo1b 想走的更像是：
实体卡 → Gacha / Marketplace → 社区 IP → Meme → 平台下一阶段资产

TAKO 这只小章鱼本来就是 https://t.co/lZ91DJbo1b 抽卡过程中长期存在的吉祥物，这次单独拿出来发 Meme，40%直接空投给历史用户，团队零分配，再用TAKO持仓去参与未来 $PULL的分配。

这套顺序值得多说一句。

CARDS走的是"平台先做大,再把收入和积分收成一枚治理/激励代币"这条路;

TAKO反过来,先把已经活在产品里的原生IP交给用户,再拿持仓当作下一阶段的门票。团队自己一分不留，把早期这批真金白银抽过卡，真把库存养在平台里的人放在第一顺位, 不是先内部分完了再讲社区故事。

平台本身数据也不错。上线五个月，累计成交超过 4000 万美元，协议收入约 500 万美元，已经挤进链上 TCG Gacha前五，这些都是Pull平台币价值的支撑

当前Season 1已结束,最终榜单还在确认; 还会有一段很短的Season 1.5。 后面会有Robinhood上线（9月20-21日）+ Based打通韩国Perp/TCG社区这条增量路径。一边把故事讲给Robinhood上的TradFi用户听，一边借Based在韩国已经沉淀的Perp Trader和TCG玩家基础，把https://t.co/lZ91DJbo1b抽卡文化嫁接到一批本来就懂收藏+懂交易的新用户身上。

Solana用 $CARDS 证明了实体卡上链能做出量和收入；https://t.co/lZ91DJbo1b在尝试把同一套库存流动往外扩，多做一层“很Robinhood”的实验——用原生IP发一枚几乎全给用户的meme，把社区身份，传播和下一轮平台币绑在一起。

9月20–21日 $TAKO上线，感兴趣的朋友与其辩论叙事，不如自己去https://t.co/lZ91DJbo1b抽两包卡，感受感受

text:
More than 80 million products registered. More than 50 brands. Founded by LVMH, Prada and Richemont in 2021.

Aura is now the de facto reference for Digital Product Passports in luxury, and the numbers above come from its own CEO → self-reported, not independently audited. Worth stating before anyone builds a strategy on them.

De facto reference is not the same as normative standard. That distinction is doing a lot of quiet work in boardrooms right now.

The CEN-CENELEC standards are open and cited in the Official Journal. Conforming to them gives you presumption of conformity with the ESPR. Joining a consortium is a commercial decision about whose infrastructure you sit on. It is not a compliance requirement, and treating it as one costs smaller maisons real leverage.

So the question for a house that isn't LVMH isn't "should we join Aura." It's → who issues our identifiers, who can verify them without our permission, and what happens to that record if the platform changes its terms, its pricing or its owners in five years.

A passport only one consortium can read is a passport with a landlord.

text:
Great conversation between @laurashin and @gdog97_ on @unchained_pod about @EthenaPay — Ethena’s new mobile neobank.

Ethena is no longer just a DeFi protocol. After building USDe into one of the largest non-reserve-backed dollars onchain, they’re going after the user relationship directly.

Why a neobank?

Last cycle’s lesson: DeFi TVL never even reclaimed 2021 highs. DeFi is more likely to win as backend infrastructure (think Morpho inside Coinbase and Robinhood) than as the thing users touch every day.

You can’t sit onchain and wait for the world to learn MetaMask. You have to meet people where they already are: a phone app.

Owning distribution also means better margins than staying a backend integration forever.

Why this category

Guy’s filter was simple:

•  Is it 10x better for the user?
•  Is it 10x better as a business once rebuilt on stablecoin rails?

Yes on both.

This is the first non-speculative crypto product he can actually imagine 100M+ people outside crypto using. The TAM looks more like Revolut than another trading app. And unlike exchanges or stablecoins, there’s no Tether/Binance-scale incumbent inside crypto waiting to crush you.

The structural edge: Ethena owns the yield engine. Other crypto neobanks bleed cash to subsidize savings on someone else’s dollar (usually T-bills). Ethena produces the yield. That pays for free onramps, card cashback, and a better product instead of rented incentives.

The product

•  Balances are self-custodial, but the UX hides that. It should feel like a bank account, not a wallet.

•  No seed phrases. Passkeys + email / iCloud backup.

•  Send to names and contacts, not 0x addresses.

•  Transfers settle on @avax.

•  Card cashback currently paid in AVAX, funded by Avalanche. Exclusive for at least the next couple of years, not necessarily forever.

•  Savings shown around 6% at launch (Ethena is topping up the natural sUSDe rate, which was ~4.75% at the time of the interview; lifetime USDe yield has averaged closer to ~7%).

•  The card is not a leveraged credit line against USDe. Visa doesn’t touch USDe. Spending redeems USDC out of the backing and settles with Visa. No liquidation mechanic.

Self-custody is also a go-to-market weapon: global on day one, without 12–24 months of new bank licenses per country.

USDe backing

The risk profile has changed a lot. Perps are now ~10% of backing. The rest is institutional lending, CLOs, RWAs, higher-quality collateral.
Young’s argument: AAA-style collateral in qualified custodians is safer than the original offshore basis trade.
Stress tests cited: ~$30B of mint/redeem flow, peak ~$15B, Binance 10/10 deleveraging, Aave/Kelp. No user principal lost.

For the end user, the complexity is meant to disappear , deposit dollars, get a savings rate. Same abstraction as a bank, different rails.

Go-to-market

Sequence:
1.  Crypto-native users first (higher balances, higher spend, already trust Ethena) — 6 to 9 months.

2.  Then normal fintech users.
Existing Ethena demand is strongest in South America and Asia. Launch is in ~50 countries, still gated. At the time of the interview: ~400 users on the app, 10–15k waitlist. Priority markets: US, Europe, UK, parts of Asia including Taiwan.
He doesn’t see Plasma as the fight. They’re friendly; he’s even an investor. The real race is new users, not the 50–100k people already using crypto neobanks.

Crypto users also aren’t that loyal. A better rate and they move — it’s one stablecoin transfer.

Revenue mix

They want income that isn’t just “is Bitcoin up.” Card spend (interchange + FX) is the most interesting new stream. USDe balances inside the app are also an acquisition tool, not the whole P&L.

Three businesses now:
•  USDe / onchain savings
•  White-label stablecoins
•  Ethena Pay

They feed each other.

UX goal: a user should be able to use the app without realizing there’s a crypto layer. Bank wire in → USDe balance.
KYC / security

Young was hit by the Revolut data incident as a customer. His broader take: the current KYC regime needs a rethink. Passport + selfie + address + history sitting at 20 vendors is an enormous physical-safety risk when one of them gets phished.

Ethena outsources KYC to specialists (Sumsub, Rain) instead of standing up a small in-house compliance team. A lot of the requirements are downstream of Visa and card issuers anyway.

Early traction + timing

They don’t time launches to the cycle. Bear markets are actually good for building: fewer distractions.
Surprise so far: spend volume vs. user count, and a few people depositing $1–2M on day one into a brand-new mobile app. Early users concentrated in South America and Asia, including existing USDe power users.

Market

Sentiment better than 2–3 months earlier. No single scandal to blame this drawdown on — that made it feel worse than 2022. Crypto looked cheap vs. other risk assets after AI and gold ripped while crypto sold off hard. His low-confidence view: the worst may be behind, some green shoots.
Worth the full listen if you care about stablecoins becoming actual money apps rather than trading chips.

The credit card was never designed for a buyer that doesn't exist as a legal person.

That's the real constraint not just fees or speed. Cards assume identity documents, human presence at checkout, and transactions large enough to absorb $0.30+ in friction.

Solana + x402 flips the primitive: cryptographic keys instead of KYC, scoped spend limits instead of "the card," and settlement fast enough to happen inside a single HTTP request. Micropayments failed for humans because of attention cost. They work for agents because there is none

Had some community members reach out with questions about IP, where we are in the process, the benefits, etc. 

IP is still under review by the USPTO. This is a long process that I’ve known from the beginning would take several months and likely some necessary revisions. The USPTO deals with tens of thousand submissions per month and they have a 6 month+ backlog before even looking at your application. There’s nothing that can be done to make this process faster. We have an examiner assigned, they’re reviewing the application and I hope to know more in the next few weeks. 

The application was reviewed, prepared and submitted by the respected @GivnerLaw law firm. They have experience in successful memecoin IP submissions. They are professionals and I stay in touch with them regularly.  

The benefits for $Buttcoin are numerous. It gives us expanded legitimacy with crypto companies like CEX, it cements our claim as the “first memecoin” with an established first-use date of 2011 with the creator backing it, and allows us further opportunities for branding and merchandising. 

It’s also really funny that Buttcoin is in an official government database. 

One last note; you don’t get “IP secured” when you submit your application. I’ve seen other groups make some dubious claims with very short timelines and I want to reiterate this is a long, very rigorous process that takes time if you want it done right. And we’re doing it the right way. 

Stay Clenched!

text:
A few months on, the @OpenAI and @huggingface  incident is still one of the clearest examples of how agentic systems expand the attack surface.

During cybersecurity evaluations, AI agents circumvented sandbox controls, exploited shared infrastructure, gained internet access and ultimately reached Hugging Face systems.

The initial vulnerability was only the foothold.

From there, the agents could enumerate infrastructure, discover credentials, exploit additional paths and move across systems without a human manually directing each step.

That changes the security problem.

It is no longer enough to ask:
“Can this system be exploited?”

You also have to ask:
“If an agent gains access here, what becomes reachable next?”

As agents connect to APIs, credentials, MCP servers, databases, cloud infrastructure and financial systems, every integration expands the reachable attack graph.

The interesting part of the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident wasn’t one exploit.

It was autonomous path discovery, persistence and lateral movement after the initial foothold.

The attack surface is becoming the entire graph of systems an agent can reach👀

text:
Why Is the Universe So Amenable to Mathematical Description?
At first glance, mathematics may seem something primary and fundamental. The astonishing elegance of its equations gives rise to a Platonic intuition: as though mathematical structures possessed an independent ideal existence and would exist even in the absence of the physical world.
Yet another view is possible. Mathematics may be understood above all as a universal language for expressing the quantitative, structural, and logical relations of the real or possible world, rather than as an independent substance of which physical reality is composed.
It is important to distinguish between what humans create and what they discover. We create the language of mathematics — its symbols, definitions, and formal systems — but by means of it we uncover relations and regularities that do not depend on our wishes. Historically, mathematics developed through the interaction of the intellect with the surrounding world: counting grew out of our ability to distinguish quantities, geometry from space and form, measurement from the comparison of magnitudes. Later, abstract thought allowed mathematics to reach far beyond immediate experience.
Human cognitive capacities themselves were shaped in a world of stable patterns and regularities. The ability to distinguish quantity, form, distance, motion, causal connections, and recurring structures had adaptive value. It is therefore unsurprising that an intellect arising in such a world proved capable of discovering and formalizing many of its regularities.
At the same time, the space of mathematically conceivable structures is considerably wider than what has been found in physical reality. Many mathematical constructions have no known physical application and perhaps never will. Moreover, the possibility of describing some world mathematically without contradiction does not yet mean that such a world is physically possible. One must distinguish between the mathematically conceivable, the physically possible, and the physically realized.
It is especially interesting that certain mathematical structures were initially explored as pure abstractions and later found unexpected applications in physics. The historical connection of mathematics with practical experience is therefore not sufficient by itself to explain its effectiveness. Perhaps abstract thought explores a far wider space of structural relations, some of which are also found in physical reality.
Seen in this light, the mathematical beauty of physical laws appears differently. Mathematics is astonishing not because the Universe obeys beautiful equations, but because the Universe those equations describe is itself astonishing. The elegance of the mathematics applicable to physics may reflect the depth and the intricacy of physical reality itself.
But why is the Universe so amenable to mathematical description at all?
Part of the answer may lie in the very possibility of a complex, self-organizing world. For stable structures, stars, chemistry, life, and ultimately intelligence to arise within it, such a world must be sufficiently ordered and governed by stable regularities. And the presence of such regularities makes their mathematical description possible.
An observer-selection effect also comes into play here: we are able to pose this question precisely because we exist in a reality whose structure allows life and intelligence to emerge. In a world devoid of sufficient stability, observers capable of investigating it mathematically might simply never have arisen.
Furthermore, our mathematics did not arise outside the Universe. Its language was developed by an intellect that itself arose within the Universe and whose cognitive capacities were formed through interaction with physical reality. The effectiveness of mathematics is therefore perhaps somewhat less mysterious than it seems: the intellect formalizes the structures of the very reality of which it is a part.
Thus the enigma lies not so much in the existence of mathematics itself as in the question of why physical reality possesses precisely those regularities that permit complex self-organization — up to life, intelligence, and the capacity of intelligent beings to comprehend through mathematics the world that gave rise to them.
On this understanding, mathematics is not a miracle governing matter from without, but an expression of the regularities of physical reality. Perhaps the Universe is so amenable to mathematical description in part because a complex, self-organizing world capable of giving rise to life and intelligence must possess stable regularities — and thereby contain within itself the possibility of its own mathematical description.

text:
"As agents take on more economically valuable work and expect to be paid for it, we will need a way for two agents that don't trust each other to agree on when a job is done."

⚡ The Kleros Agentic Commerce Court is live, and ready to solve these cases. Some examples ↓
author: Kleros_io
quoted_text:
An underrated opportunity right now is figuring out how to measure subjective agent work.

Crypto has historically relied on objective mechanisms such as:

- Proof-of-Work to prove computational work was expended
- Validity rules to determine whether transactions and state transitions follow the protocol
- Slashing to penalise provable misbehaviour like double-signing

None of these mechanisms measure whether a buyer received what they intended to purchase. 

We have some infrastructure for resolving bespoke disputes, but we do not have sufficient infrastructure for determining whether a scoped job completed by an agent actually met a buyer's expectations at scale.

Existing approaches solve adjacent problems such as:

@Kleros_io and @UMAprotocol - can adjudicate disputes but rely on human participation and is designed for infrequent disputes

@bittensor - evaluates miner performance within subnets, not whether a buyer's intent was executed

@virtuals_io - has evaluator agents, but evaluators are selected per task and there are no economic guarantees tied to the outcomes (yet)

A missing primitive that is yet to be built is a way for two agents that do not trust each other to scope a job, agree on conditions for success, execute the work, evaluate the outcome and release payment at scale.

Lots of open questions around how to build this, such as how to:

- Resolve disputes at machine speed
- Keep sensitive information private during negotiation and evaluation
- Prevent collusion between agents using the same model providers
- Evaluate outcomes where quality is subjective
- Determine who bears cost when agent fails

In general, I think liability will be important here. If agents have capital and/or reputation at stake, they can be penalised when they fail to deliver against clearly specified commitments.

I do think pricing the risk is hard though. In saying that, if a protocol can accurately price the probability that an agent delivers a specified outcome and that pricing improves with every buyer–seller interaction, it will become more valuable over time. The data could be used to build a kind of matchmaking moat, e.g. understanding which agents reliably deliver which outcomes for which buyers.

It's an early space but I expect mechanisms for evaluating subjective agent work will be critically needed soon. As agents take on more economically valuable work and expect to be paid for it, we will need a way for two agents that don't trust each other to agree on when a job is done.
