text:
CLARITY, closing the loop.

Cloture failed 49 to 50. NO was the play, as flagged. Needed 60, got 49, so this wasn't a near miss, it was never close.

One thing surprised me. I expected fresh size to pile into NO before the vote. Didn't happen. Just the usual Polymarket regulars, tourist and co, came through and bought big NO. Right side, less flow than I wanted.

Two plays I left on the table:

1) Resting YES bids at 2 to 3ct. Some accounts were market selling YES, but this market can't even resolve before year end and there's still a thin lame duck revival path, so 2 to 3ct YES is cheap optionality, not a directional bet. Free shares if you're sitting there to catch them.

2)Shorting BTC/crypto into the failure.

But I was busy with other stuff during the vote. So fine overall.

今天复盘了这半年做的单子，奇了怪，做的几次山寨几乎都在亏。手里的单今天也被强平了。日线级别收敛，拿了4天，最后还是被割了几千U。小资金也疼。更魔幻的是，ETH几天前都突破了，它一动不动。山寨不是所有收敛都叫机会。现在山寨太多，注意力不够分，资金更不够分。没人讨论、没大V/顶流关注、没资金持续进的币，日线收敛突破也可能只是自嗨，甚至是流动性陷阱。只有被市场焦点选中的山寨，某些级别的收敛突破才有意义。我那单如果真突破，按结构至少看翻倍，结果亏了80%。
所以现在玩山寨，先看热度，再看资金，最后才看K线。有热度 + 有资金 +形态才有溢价。不然，ETH突破是ETH的，山寨还是你的山寨。

16 個 Vault

5 種資產

今年 6 月 Zama 才跟 Morpho、Steakhouse 推第一個 Confidential USDC Vault，7 週 TVL 就做到 4,000 萬美金。

Public Blockchain 的 HTTPS Layer。

這次連 Swap 都補上了，等於從：

如果未來 Stablecoin、RWA、Institutional DeFi 繼續成長，我不認為「所有部位全部公開」會是最終型態。

所以 Zama 這條線，我會繼續看。

捋了一遍CLARITY 投票没过的细节顺便脑补一下后续的影响。

最终投票结果是 49 票赞成、50 票反对的结果宣告失败（且全为共和党人，无一民主党或独立参议员跨界）。距离推进法案所需的 60 票门槛相差整整 11 票。

后续马上要中期选举，如果中选共和党失利就是跛脚鸭阶段了，成功可能性更小。我个人觉得2027甚至更后面才会通过了。

这次投票最大的影响因素是民主党针对Trump的腐败批判，觉得通过法案会进一步帮助其家族在Crypto上获利，尤其Warren讲话非常直接犀利。

“这不是监管分歧，而是一位巨额利益获得者借国家机器为自己的私人产业量身立规。” 😂😂😂

当一部法案与党争，与特定人物结合在一起的时候，那么事情就变的复杂了。不过还好民主党针对的并不是Crypto本身，也并不是“美国不需要crypto监管”。

Warren 在投票前其实直接说过：
“We need crypto regulation”
她反对的是当前版本/自肥的Trump，而不是“监管清晰化”这个目标本身。

所以迟早法案会通过，只是可能更严苛，时间比预期的更久一些。

说实话现在CLARITY不通过与加息预期48小时内放一起出来不见得完全是坏事，毕竟利空一起落地比一个个出来好。

我是不觉得 $BTC 还能跌去6字头甚至更低，如果出现了大回调就打算多买点了，蹲个中选后的行情反弹。

要知道从历史数据看中期选举后美股的行情一直都不错的。

我让ChatGPT帮我率了一下：

1938年以来，中期选举结束后的12个月，S&P 500约95%的时期上涨，平均涨幅约14%。

所以大家Calm Down，耐心多等几个月，延迟满足不是坏事，可能高潮更刺激强烈呢😌😍

text:
Started testing a looping strategy on @ZestProtocol to farm some of their new incentive campaign.

Here's what I've been doing:

• Supplied ~$92 of $sBTC
• Borrowed 30 $USDCx against it
• Swapped the USDCx into more $sBTC
• Supplied that sBTC back into Zest
• Repeated with another 10 $USDCx

Final position:

• $133 $sBTC supplied
• 40 $USDCx debt
• $93 net equity

Zest is now paying 0.5 BTC per month in incentives in $STX.

Half goes to $sBTC suppliers, while the other half goes to $USDCx borrowers with 20%+ LTV.

So the loop potentially lets me increase my sBTC exposure while earning incentives on both the supply and borrow side.

Of course, leverage cuts both ways.

A 10% rise in sBTC adds roughly $13 to my supplied position before interest and fees. A 10% drop does the opposite while also pushing my LTV higher.

Anyone running other loops on Zest?

Disclosure: I’m a long-time Stacks supporter and $STX holder.

text:
前段时间zcash因为其隐私特性成为热门隐私币之一。zama也做隐私，不过它走的是完全不同的路子：它搞的是隐私层。

也就是，Zama不是独立的隐私L1区块链，而是可以叠加在不同L1/L2上的隐私层，为应用提供隐私能力。

Zama的这条路是从DeFi开始试验的，这也是最现实的路子。

今年6月份，Zama跟Morpho/Steakhouse合作推出隐私USDC收益平台，当时只有一个金库/一位策展人/一种资产。

看起来Zama这条路基本上走出来了。今天看到消息说，它拓展到16个金库/5位策展人（Steakhouse、Armitage by Wintermute、Flowdesk、RockawayX、Bitwise），隐私资产也多了cWBTC/cTGBP等资产的隐私版。此外，还上线了Zama Swap协议。

这种在基础设施上推出的应用层隐私，是机构比较喜欢的玩法：在目前以太坊L1/或L2等基础设施上，只在应用入口叠加隐私。

这样一来，机构在玩DeFi时候，可以实现隐身，金额/时间都只有自己知道，无须担心对手/机器人/跟单玩家看见。

Zama的隐私目前有两种模式：一种是混合型金库，允许存款人在现有已经上线的金库中存入隐私代币（cUSDC/cUSDT等），持仓不会在公开记录中出现。

还有一种是，独享型金库，这是纯机密金库，没有普通存款入口，目前包括了隐私wbtc收益金库，这对于wBTC持有人来说，可以获得隐私好处。

I am not sure who on Tucker's staff wrote this for him but that is a lot of lies in one statement. Purposeful I am sure. Any reader can hit the @grok button and ask true? See my article on the 2,000 pound bomb fallacies, why they are used in war to include by the U.S. today. 

A Mark 84 does not destroy everything within half a mile. Yes, fragments can travel farther than the area where the point of impact occurs, but terrain, surrounding structures, and the circumstances of the explosion affect the extent of the blast. It also does not send out a sun-temperature wave that melts surrounding rock and vaporizes people at 100 feet. It is not a nuclear weapon. Yes, it can collapse apartment buildings and leave large craters, but a thirty-five-foot crater is not a standard result. Crater size depends on the factors of the structure/ground conditions of where the bomb detonates.

Dresden is not recognized as a war crime under the standards of World War II. Interesting choice of example tho as the city had about 560,000 residents in early 1945. A 250,000 civilians killed figure was devised by Joseph Goebbels’ ministry and pushed for decades, later recycled by David Irving. More than 50 years later, a historical commission put the death toll at 25,000.

The March 1945 Berlin raid was not “the largest American air raid of WWII.” Some people call it the largest U.S. raid on Berlin. A bigger American raid was Christmas Eve 1944, Eighth Air Force operation against targets in western Germany. Comparing that one day Berlin drop to a planned Israeli stockpile of 40,000 two-thousand-pound bombs is lazy, not a like for like measure of an attack. Operation Meetinghouse over Tokyo did kill 80,000–100,000 people and is often called the most destructive single air raid in history, but the load was 1,665 tons of incendiaries, not “1,600 tons of bombs.” Different weapons, different effect. The 7.5% line only works if you treat an arms-sale inventory as if it were already dropped in one raid.

By no definition (words have meaning) has Israel done a genocide in Gaza. Not by the definition's intent or actions requirements. No actual evidence support the intent or actions allegation. 

The government of Israel was in a war against the terror army of Hamas in Gaza after they invaded Israel on October 7th and withdrew into Gaza with 250 hostages; they were also at war with the terror army (more equipped than many nations) Hezbollah in Lebanon after they attack on October 8th. 

Israel is not working to exterminate an unarmed civilian population in Gaza or Lebenon. No evidence shows they have targeted civilians. 

All of the Gaza, Lebanon, Yemen, Syria, and Iran fronts have contained buried and fortified targets that can justify the use of modern 2,000-pound bombs.

According to an informed federal official, in the coming months the Trump administration plans to send a total of 40,000 Mark 84 and Blu-117 bombs to the government of Israel. Each bomb weighs 2,000 pounds. This appears to be the largest transfer of conventional explosive ordnance from the United States in modern history.

How big is this shipment? It amounts to 40,000 tons of bombs. For perspective, the largest American air raid of World War Two was the Eighth Air Force’s attack on Berlin in March of 1945. Combined, the 2,023 Allied aircraft involved dropped about 3,000 tons of bombs. That’s 7.5 percent of what Trump is sending to Israel. That same month, March of 1945, the US Army Air Forces began the single most destructive bombing raid in human history, Operation Meetinghouse over Tokyo. More than 100,000 Japanese civilians were killed. By the end of that operation, the US had dropped 1,600 tons of bombs. That’s four percent of what Trump is sending to Israel. World War Two ended five months later, when the US dropped an atomic bomb on the city of Hiroshima. The shipment Trump is sending to Israel amounts to more than three times the destructive power of that nuclear explosion. There is no precedent for what the Trump administration is doing.

Nor is there a justification. The government of Israel is not fighting World War Two, or even a war. It is engaged in periodic skirmishes with a guerrilla force in Lebanon, and it is working to exterminate an unarmed civilian population in Gaza. Neither front requires modern 2,000-pound bombs.

An American-made Mark 84 has a destruction radius of half a mile. It releases a thermal wave the temperature of the surface of the sun. Within 100 feet of the explosion, rock melts and human flesh turns to vapor. The bomb collapses apartment buildings and leaves craters thirty-five feet deep. Until the war with Iran, the US military generally avoided using the Mark 84 in urban areas. It kills too many civilians.

For the Netanyahu government, that’s been the upside. In the weeks after October 7, the IDF dropped nearly six hundred 2,000-pound bombs on densely populated areas in Gaza, including on more than 100 officially designated civilian evacuation zones. The slaughter was so grotesque and embarrassing that for a moment the Biden administration paused a shipment of Mark 84s. Those shipments quickly resumed under Trump. Now they’ve accelerated.

It’s hard to overstate the scale of the crime the Israeli government is committing in Gaza. Over the last three years, more than a quarter-million Palestinians have been killed or wounded by Israeli forces there. The majority of them have been noncombatants: women, the elderly and tens of thousands of children. Many thousands more remain missing, presumably entombed under the rubble of 200,000 collapsed buildings. So far the Israelis have destroyed 92 percent of all homes in Gaza, and 34 of the 36 hospitals. By comparison, the 1945 Allied bombings of Dresden, now acknowledged as a war crime, destroyed about half of the city’s inhabited buildings.

By any definition, what the Netanyahu government has done in Gaza is genocide. The 40,000 new bombs the Trump administration is sending will be used to do the same in Lebanon, and likely in other countries in the region. If you wanted to extend the Iran war into the indefinite future, this is exactly what you’d do.

So far none of this has received public scrutiny. At some point, inevitably, it will be described in media accounts as an “arms sale.” It is not an arms sale. It is a gift, funded by American taxpayers through the Foreign Military Financing program, an arrangement designed to disguise welfare as capitalism: Congress appropriates money to the executive branch, which transfers the cash to Israel to “buy” American-made weapons, in this case from General Dynamics. Politicians claim this is a win for America. Most voters have no idea they paid for it. The bill in this case is about $3 billion. Add that to the $352 billion the US Treasury has transferred to Israel since 1951.

How did this happen? The request for 40,000 new high-explosive civilian-killing bombs originated at the US Embassy in Jerusalem, which is run by Christian Zionist Ambassador Mike Huckabee and his aide David Milstein, who is the stepson of Fox News host Mark Levin. From there it moved to the State Department, where Marco Rubio enthusiastically approved it.

At this point, only four more people need to sign off before the bombs ship to Israel: Senators Jim Risch and Jeanne Shaheen, the chairman and ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee; and Congressmen Brian Mast and Gregory Meeks, the top two members of the equivalent House committee. All four are committed neocons. Collectively they’ve taken millions from the Israel lobby. In 2015, Brian Mast traveled to Israel to volunteer for the Israeli military. In 2023, Mast showed up in the House of Representatives wearing an IDF uniform.

It’s hard to imagine any of them hesitating before sending more free bombs to Israel. Only public outrage can stop this.

Last month I wrote about how we can build a positive and safe future for everyone: https://t.co/eoLGVY8yad

Every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens.

The reality is:

- People won't want to use agents that are misaligned with them and that don't do what they ask, so labs have a strong natural incentive to make their models more aligned.

There is a lot of debate about slowing progress on capabilities until alignment catches up. My view is that trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models. Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind.

- Labs face significant liability if their models cause harm, so they have a strong incentive to prevent this as well.

Meta delayed shipping Muse for several months to focus on safety and security. We didn't call for everyone else to do this before we would. We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and for us. I'm proud of the security foundations we've built.

- Engaging independent evaluators and advisors is industry best practice. MSL already does this today in several areas because it helps produce better work. Other labs can just do this too. In general, it would be helpful for there to be a larger and more diverse ecosystem of evaluators.

- Committing the significant majority of compute towards serving people rather than racing towards recursive self-improvement is one of the best ways to ensure we develop this technology safely. Meta has made this commitment and other labs can do this as well.

I believe the key to building a positive future for everyone is maintaining the right balance of power. This is within our power to do.

text:
How can I protect my X account?

There are a lot of guides on the internet, many of them are written in such a way that the average person will have a hard time understanding what they are talking about.

So, a list of simple tips from me, a thread:

• First of all, if you are not using this functionality, turn off delegation!

• Turn on password reset protect, it's very important.

• Install 2FA via Authy or any other service like Aegis. Google Authenticator is generally not recommended anymore in order to stay out of the Google ecosystem, and Authy offers more robust account recovery options (Aegis does not offer the same level of account recovery options). 

Keep in mind that the codes generated by 2FA apps are device specific. If your account is not manually backed up to Google cloud or iCloud and you lose your phone, you’ll need to spend some time proving your identity to restore your 2FA. 

The added security is worth the hassle! Hardware-based 2FA options are regarded as more secure than phone-based OTP options since the keys are stored on the YubiKey device itself, not on your phone, or in the cloud, or on your computer. 

Aegis Authenticator is open source (licensed under GPL v3) and the source code can be found here. The issue with Authy is that it depends on a phone number which can be changed through an email request, allowing anyone access to HOTP/TOTP after an approximate 4-day wait period. To avoid that, disable multi-device function in Authy's settings!

1/5

text:
Requests for Builders

I put together a list of ideas for builders joining our Runtime Hackathon.

Submissions are due Saturday, September 19 at 4 PM EDT, with demos starting at 5 PM.

All the details: https://t.co/ytsvbHovmX

After putting this together, I figured it was worth sharing more broadly with anyone looking for interesting things to build.

Here’s what I shared with builders:

We’re looking for ambitious products that push forward onchain finance, markets and autonomous agents.

These are starting points, not boundaries. Build something people want. Put it onchain where being onchain actually makes the product better.

1. Tokenized Stocks & 24/7 Markets
Build products around stocks and other traditional assets moving onchain. Think market making, liquidity, arbitrage, peg monitoring, rebalancing, price discovery, portfolio products and strategies that take advantage of the gap between traditional market hours and 24/7 crypto markets.

2. New Trading Products & Interfaces
Rethink how people discover, analyze and trade assets. Trading terminals, social trading, copy trading, indexes, automated strategies, DCA, perps, prediction markets, portfolio automation, risk tools and entirely new interfaces for interacting with markets.

3. New Market Infrastructure
Build primitives that make onchain markets better. Dynamic fees, new AMMs, Uniswap v4 hooks, onchain options, volatility markets, order books, RFQ systems, new launch mechanisms, liquidity-management systems and new forms of price discovery.

4. Stablecoins, Payments & Global Money
Make money move better. Stablecoin payments, merchant tools, remittances, payroll, subscriptions, invoicing, cross-border settlement, local-currency stablecoins, savings products and infrastructure that makes stablecoins invisible to the end user.

5. Agentic Commerce
Build a world where software can transact on its own. Agents that buy services, pay APIs, negotiate, subscribe, hire other agents, manage budgets or participate in marketplaces using programmable payments.

6. Autonomous Financial Agents
Give AI agents wallets and let them participate directly in financial markets. Agents that trade, rebalance portfolios, manage treasury, move liquidity, execute strategies, monitor risk, find yield, hedge positions or manage financial operations for users and businesses.

7. Agent-to-Agent Economies
Build infrastructure for agents to discover, trust, pay and coordinate with each other. Agent marketplaces, reputation systems, service networks, shared resources, machine-to-machine payments and protocols where autonomous agents become economic participants.

8. Borrowing, Yield & Leverage
Build better ways to access capital. Borrow against tokenized stocks and RWAs, create new lending markets, optimize yield, manage collateral, refinance positions and build leveraged or structured financial products.

9. Onchain Credit & Reputation
Explore credit that does not require everything to be overcollateralized. Onchain reputation, financial history, identity and behavioral data could unlock credit products for individuals, agents and businesses that traditional crypto lending cannot serve.

10. Token Lifecycle & Treasury Tools
Tokens need infrastructure after launch. Build systems for buybacks, burns, fee reinvestment, liquidity management, treasury management, vesting, distributions, community takeovers, ownership transitions and automated token operations.

11. Internet-Native Capital Formation
Rethink how new companies and projects get funded. Products that let founders raise directly from users, customers or communities and use tokens to coordinate ownership, distribution, incentives and growth.

12. Tokenized Real-World Assets
Stocks are only the beginning. Explore private credit, startup equity, treasuries, real estate, commodities, collectibles, revenue streams or other assets that become more useful when they are programmable, composable and globally accessible.

13. Onchain Asset Management
Build the next generation of funds and investment products. Automated portfolios, tokenized funds, indexes, strategy vaults, structured products, risk-managed portfolios and products that combine traditional and crypto assets.

14. Onchain Content & Creator Businesses
Build media and social products where content has an economic layer. Video, livestreaming, research, communities, creator markets and social products where creators and users can own, fund, trade or participate in the networks they help grow.

15. Financial Data, Intelligence & Risk
Make onchain markets easier to understand. Real-time analytics, portfolio intelligence, risk engines, fraud detection, market surveillance, agent-readable financial data, research agents and tools that turn raw onchain activity into useful decisions.

16. Consumer Finance Rebuilt Onchain
Take something people already use in finance and rebuild it around crypto rails. Banking, savings, brokerage, payments, credit, insurance, investing or financial management where 24/7 settlement, global access and programmable money create a materially better experience.

17. Something We Haven’t Thought Of
Some of the best products will not fit neatly into an existing category. If there is a financial product, market or autonomous business that only becomes possible because money and assets are programmable, we want to see it.

The goal: build a real product with the potential to become a company, not a demo built around a sponsor API.

Bankr does not need to be the core infrastructure of the product. Where a token makes sense, think about how it can help fund, distribute, coordinate or grow the project, with Bankr serving as the launch and distribution layer.

text: China preparing for war
author: zerohedge
quoted_text:
In the event of a conflict, Beijing wants to be able to quickly switch to a war economy. A new law will allow the government to access all companies based in China for this purpose, including, explicitly, foreign companies and their subsidiaries.

The new rules will take effect on October 1, 2026.

In the future, companies will be required to provide the authorities with comprehensive information about their capacities even in peacetime. In the event of an emergency, according to Article 2, this is intended to “ensure a rapid transition from a state of peace to a state of war and to convert economic and social strength into defensive strength”. This conversion encompasses a wide range of resources: production facilities, equipment and intellectual property, such as data and software, could be seized.

The law no longer refers solely to confiscation but, for the first time, also to expropriation. It also enshrines the possibility of shifting production to goods that can be used for military purposes.

Another striking change is the wording stating that China intends to use the new regulations to respond to its “development interests”. The term appears in the law for the first time and seems deliberately vague.
Since the Chinese security narrative typically encompasses economic security, access to technology, raw materials and supply chains, this expansion could also include sanctions, export controls or a blockade directed against China.

However, the new law does not affect only businesses. In the event of a mobilization, male citizens between the ages of 18 and 60 and female citizens between the ages of 18 and 55 are required to perform national defense service.

The law thus reflects lessons learned from Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine. It demonstrates Beijing’s efforts to streamline the mechanisms and structures of military mobilization and to improve its ability to quickly allocate and mobilize the necessary resources and manpower in the event of potential conflicts.

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
真实实验太贵怎么办？

先让 Agent 在自己的历史轨迹里「做梦」几百遍，再决定下一步把算力花在哪里。

这篇 Dream-RSI 做的就是这件事。

每次真实探索后，系统会把走过的分支、失败方案、评测结果和计算成本保存成一棵 Discovery Tree。

这些历史随后被重组成一个 Replay Simulator。Agent 可以在里面低成本尝试新的搜索策略，比如先探索哪条路、什么时候并行、什么时候停止，而不用重新执行真实实验。

选出更好的策略后，再放回真实环境继续探索。新的轨迹又会进入模拟器，形成下一轮自我改进。

有意思的是，底层 Coding Agent 始终没变。

真正持续进化的是「怎么探索」这层策略。

实验覆盖算法设计、数学优化和 GPU Kernel。Lasso 任务里，相比 SimpleTES，Agent 调用最高减少约 162×；GPU Kernel 任务中，相同预算下最高获得 2.09× 性能提升。

所以 Agent 的历史轨迹可能远不止是 Memory。

只要把过去的分支、决策和结果保存得足够完整，它们也可以变成训练下一版探索策略的模拟环境。

有点像人做研究时在脑子里反复推演：

先想清楚哪条路更值得走，再真正动手做实验。

text:
A few thoughts on Muse by Meta.

1. Good at the basics. I asked it for a recap of NFL Week 1 as a ravens fan and it offered to send me a weekly recap of the NFL. The UX is very smooth and intuitive.

2. Tool use feels limited. I asked it to update a link in my Instagram bio, and it asked me to link my Instagram (which I did) and then told me it could only update the description, not links in the bio.

3. I also asked it to connect Co-Invest, a custom connector, and I hit some snags there. All the AI products are fairly similar now, so it’s nice to see an axis along which they differentiate. 

If you tell Grok Bot or Claude Code to connect to a custom connector in plain English, they’ll usually do it. If you tell Muse or plain Claude to do this, they’ll often refuse. This might reflect that the first two are more developer-focused (Grok Bot from Cursor) and the latter two are more consumer facing.

All in all, it seems clear that we are still early in the personal agent space. Excited to see how these products evolve, as well as any potential new entrants. 😉

text: 这个应该是关于 Uniswap v4 恶意 hooks 分析的非常清楚的一个帖子。
author: fishkiller
quoted_text:
看到很多朋友还是不懂，再加上聚合器是我目前的工作，再详细的解释一下。在我看来，这更接近利用系统盲区进行的恶意攻击，危害不亚于常见的 MEV 夹子，而且更加隐蔽。

简单描述这个攻击方法：交易可以正常成功，但你最后收到的钱变少了。

用户发起交易后，聚合器会在多个协议和流动性池之间寻找路线。交易经过一连串操作，最后有一步进入一个带恶意 Hook 的 Uniswap v4 池。这个池在报价时表现得很便宜，等真实交易执行，再把动态 LP fee 调高到 12.8%，直接从输入资产中收走一大笔费用。

---
用户发起交易
  ↓
聚合器寻找并模拟最优路线
  ↓
路线进入 Uniswap v4 动态费池
  ↓
报价模拟：低费率 / 甚至 0%
真实执行：LP fee 突然变成 12.8%
  ↓
交易仍然成功，但用户收到的钱明显减少
---

这里有三个疑问需要先讲清楚。

1. 聚合器为什么没有在模拟报价时发现？

聚合器一般会先用 eth_call 模拟交易，比较不同路线能拿到多少输出。为了避免模拟因为 gas 不够而失败，报价系统经常会给 eth_call 一个很高的 gas ceiling。

这个恶意 Hook 恰好会读取执行时的 gas 环境。高 gas 的模拟调用会落入低费率分支，看起来像一个非常有竞争力的池；真实交易的 gas limit 低得多，于是会落入另一个分支，被收取更高的 LP fee。

对完全相同的 beforeSwap calldata，只修改 call gas，可以复现出不同返回值：

---
gas = 1,000,000   → 10%
gas ≈ 16,000,000  → 0.5%
gas = 30,000,000  → 0%
---

这些数值是调查时合约的当前配置。历史真实交易中的 12.8%，由 PoolManager 的 Swap event 直接证明。攻击的核心是让 quote 和 execution 看到不同规则。

2. Uniswap v4 Hook 是什么？

Uniswap v4 允许每个池绑定一个 Hook。Hook 可以在 swap 前后运行自定义逻辑。正常情况下，它可以根据市场波动、流动性深度或其他条件动态调整费用。

Dynamic-fee pool 还允许 beforeSwap Hook 为每笔交易单独覆盖 LP fee。这个能力本身是 Uniswap v4 的正常设计。问题在于恶意 Hook 可以把“当前调用看起来像报价模拟还是真实执行”也放进费率逻辑里。

PoolKey 里的 0x800000 只是 dynamic-fee flag，表示这个池的 LP fee 可以被动态覆盖，并不代表 800% 手续费。真实费率要看每笔 Swap event 里的 fee 字段。本案出现的 fee = 128000，换算后就是 12.8%。

3. amountOutMin 为什么没有拦住？

amountOutMin 是用户愿意接受的最终输出底线。实际输出低于这个数，交易回滚；高于这个数，交易就会成功。

它只检查整条路线最后拿到了多少，不会逐个检查中间池子的 fee 是否和 quote 一致，也不知道某个 Hook 是否临时改变了规则。

如果 slippage 设置得很宽，或者路线里其他步骤带来了一些正向 price improvement，恶意池抽走一部分价值之后，最终输出仍然可能高于 amountOutMin。链上检查会认为交易合格，用户却拿少了。

具体案例：Relay 路线在哪里出了问题

代表交易：https://t.co/XErm89VqCi
这笔交易走的是 Relay 顶层流程，source-side swap 由 0x BnbSettler 执行。完整调用层级大致是：

---
ERC-4337 EntryPoint
  ↓
Relay v3 Router / ApprovalProxy / Depository
  ↓
0x BnbSettler
  ├─ FOMO action：USDT → WBNB
  └─ Uniswap v4 action：WBNB → USDC
                              ↓
                     目标动态费池 + 恶意 Hook
---

关键点是 FOMO 只完成 USDT → WBNB 这一步。随后 0x BnbSettler 才单独进入有问题的 Uniswap v4 池，把 WBNB 换成 USDC。

这一步之前大约有 5,926.9 USDT，FOMO 输出约 8.536 WBNB。进入目标 v4 pool 后，最后只得到约 5,169.5 USDC。稳定币价值差约 757.4 美元，约为 12.779%，与 Swap event 记录的 12.8% LP fee 基本吻合。

这笔交易的正确 minAmountOut 是约 4,742.5 USDC，相比费前路线价值低约 20%。实际输出 5,169.5 USDC，虽然被抽走约 12.8%，仍然比 minimum 高约 9%，所以交易正常成功。

amountOutMin 没有失效，它严格执行了用户或上层系统写入的最终底线。问题是这个底线留出的空间足以容纳中间的异常高费。仅凭链上数据，我们还不能确定这约 20% 是用户手动设置，还是 Relay、0x 或上层集成针对 meme、tax、低流动性和多跳路线自动加入的 buffer。

反编译后看到的核心逻辑

这个 Hook 没有 verified source，也没有 Sourcify metadata。调查中取得了约 7,191-byte runtime bytecode，通过 Heimdall 反编译，并配合 live eth_call 验证。下面是按恢复出的控制流整理的高层伪代码，不是项目方公开源码：

---
function beforeSwap(...) returns (..., uint24 lpFeeOverride) {
    require(msg.sender == PoolManager);
    poolSwapCount[poolId]++;

    Config memory config = poolConfig[poolId];
    uint24 fee = selectFeeTier(
        gasleft(),
        block.gaslimit,
        config.thresholds,
        config.feeTiers
    );

    return (beforeSwap.selector, 0, OVERRIDE_FEE_FLAG | fee);
}
---

可以确认的链上行为有两个：同一输入在不同 gas envelope 下会返回不同 fee override；历史 Swap event 确实记录了 12.8%。函数名、变量名和部分控制流来自逆向恢复，因此不应该把这段伪代码当成 verified source。

为什么是 12.8%？

128000 不是 Uniswap v4 的特殊常量。v4 的 LP fee 单位是 1 / 1,000,000，所以 128000 / 1,000,000 = 12.8%。

目前没有 verified source 或攻击者说明解释为什么精确选择 128000。下面只能从攻击经济学推断。

报价阶段已经伪装成低费率，真实 fee 从 5% 提高到 12.8%，不一定会降低聚合器选中这个池的概率。真正限制攻击者的是：提高费用后，最终输出是否仍高于 amountOutMin，交易是否会大量回滚，以及异常多久会被监控发现并拉黑。

在 split route 中，这种做法会更隐蔽。底层池即使收取 12.8%，只要进入它的分片很小，对整条路线的影响就会被稀释，也可能被 slippage buffer 或其他分片的正向价格改善覆盖。

所以 12.8% 更像是在单笔抽取、交易成功率和暴露风险之间选择的高收益档位，而不是技术上必须使用的数字。这一点属于合理推断，目前没有直接证据证明攻击者的具体动机。

怎么防？

对普通用户来说，最直接的保护仍然是 amountOutMin。确认钱包或聚合器给出的 minimum 是否能接受，避免为了提高成交率设置过宽的 slippage。它是损失底线，但无法保证中间路线诚实。

对聚合器和 swap 服务来说，只做一次高 gas eth_call 已经不够。至少应该：

对同一 calldata 分别使用高 gas 和接近真实交易 gas limit 的环境模拟。fee 或 output 明显变化时直接拒绝。

识别 dynamic-fee pool 和 unknown/unverified Hook，对实际 LP fee 设置可接受上限。

交易完成后核对 quote 与 receipt 中的 Pool ID、Hook、LP fee 和实际输出。即使交易成功，低费报价、高费执行也应该立即告警。

这件事说明，可编程 AMM 带来了更多定价策略，也打开了识别报价环境、针对路由器行为差异化收费的新攻击面。聚合器以后既要检查最终输出，也要确认报价时看到的规则和真实执行时完全一致。正在增强中。

text:
I'm not of fan of regulation for two reasons - 1) its hard to get right, and 2) its highly susceptible to regulatory capture. That said, if we insist on doing it, we should try to get it correct. 

As "safety" seems is the primary goal of this AI regulation exercise, I wanted to share that I recently went deep on both the 737 Max (2 crashes) and Fukushima accidents. In both cases, the investigations led to a conclusion that "regulatory capture" was the EXACT failure that led to both safety incidents. Boeing/FAA and Tepco/NISA.

As a result, with safety as the #1 goal, the regulator MUST BE someone with authority and accountability "over" the regulated company. The idea that it could be a friendly third party with lots of cross-relationships is structurally  broken idea. Ask Mr. Kiyoshi Kurokawa. 

If we insist on doing this the regulator (1) needs to be 100% independent, 2) the "tests" and "procedures" need to come for the regulator not the company, and (3) the regulator needs to understand their responsibility is to the American people. They need to feel the authority over the regulated company and the responsibility to the nation.

It's imperative. Or it will fail.

Boeing 737 Max: MCAS used one AOA sensor and could repeatedly force nose-down. Boeing minimized it to skip simulator training and costs, withheld data from FAA. FAA delegated most certification to Boeing staff via ODA, creating conflicts; managers overruled experts. House report labeled this regulatory capture; 346 died in 2018-19 crashes.

Fukushima: NAIIC (Kurokawa) called it a man-made disaster from collusion. NISA (under pro-nuclear METI) let TEPCO self-regulate, ignored known tsunami/station-blackout risks, and delayed upgrades. Classic capture where the regulator served industry over public safety.

Crypto can't be uninvented. With clarity emerging through the regulators, we'll continue updating the financial system.

circle almost had another name.  in january 2014, twobitidiot published an article reporting that circle’s original name and brand was supposed to be bancor. the company chose circle, but the other name survived in an old post that’s still online today. [the original receipt]
(https://t.co/S48MIfA4eP).  

and that name already carried decades of history.  in the 1940s, john maynard keynes proposed bancor as an international unit for settling balances between countries. the proposal never became the world’s monetary system, but the idea of money beyond national borders endured. [the keynes plan]
(https://t.co/GqSLVUUM7y). 

then came the phoenix.  in 1988, the economist pictured a phoenix above burning banknotes, wearing a coin marked 2018. the accompanying article imagined a future world currency. thirty years later, circle launched usdc on september 26, 2018. that shared year is a coincidence, and it became the visual thread in bancor’s mythology. [1988 archive]
(https://t.co/2XGVfBQIHG), [usdc launch]

(https://t.co/0OSfUaItMX).

the name resurfaced again in 2020, when jeremy allaire discussed whether a synthetic global digital currency could become a bancor on circle’s own show. he was discussing the monetary idea, years before this memecoin. [the official transcript]

(https://t.co/AOl9s0yYR5). 

then circle introduced arc, a blockchain designed around stablecoin finance, with usdc as native gas. [arc announcement](https://t.co/Uke4sPMsnR).  

that gives $bancor its homecoming story: an independent community takes the name circle reportedly left behind, pairs it with the phoenix, and frames its arrival on arc as a return.  an abandoned monetary idea. a name almost chosen. a bird that rises again.  that’s the lore of $bancor: giving an old name another life.  the project is independent, with no affiliation or endorsement from circle or arc, and is unrelated to bancor protocol’s bnt.
